You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **Attorneys at Law**

400 South Ashbury Asset Advisors, Suite 3000 Wilmington, Delaware 19801 Telephone: (302) 555-7800 \| Facsimile: (302) 555-7801

New York Office: 620 Eighth Avenue, 42nd Floor New York, New York 10018 Telephone: (212) 555-9400 \| Facsimile: (212) 555-9401

www.calderwoodharkness.com

April 2, 2025

**VIA EMAIL AND FIRST-CLASS MAIL**

Catherine E. Loomis, Esq. General Counsel & Chief Compliance Officer Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC 1200 Concord Pike, Suite 600 Wilmington, Delaware 19803

> **Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Formation of Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP and Related Vehicles** **Matter Number: 1003-00002**

Dear Ms. Loomis:

We are delighted to set forth the terms pursuant to which Calderwood & Harkness LLP (the \"Firm,\" \"we,\" \"us,\" or \"our\") will represent Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC (\"HCP\" or the \"Client\") in connection with the formation and fundraise of the Client\'s fifth flagship private equity fund, as described in greater detail below. This letter (this \"Engagement Letter\"), when countersigned by the Client, shall constitute the binding agreement between the Firm and the Client with respect to the engagement described herein.

**[1. Engagement and Client Identification]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP is pleased to confirm its engagement by Harrowgate Capital Partners LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, in connection with the formation, structuring, and fundraise of the Client\'s fifth flagship private equity fund and the related fund vehicles described in Section 2 below (collectively, the \"Engagement\"). HCP will serve as the Sponsor and promoter of the fund and its related vehicles, and in that capacity is responsible for all aspects of the fundraise, investor relations, and fund management.

We note that HCP is a registered investment adviser with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC File No. 801-79223; CRD No. 298417) and is subject to the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended, and the rules and regulations promulgated thereunder.

For purposes of this Engagement, HCP is the sole client of the Firm. Although we will be forming and advising on various related entities in the course of the Engagement --- including the fund partnership entities, the general partner entity, the blocker corporation, and the offshore feeder vehicle, each as identified in Section 2 below --- HCP is the sole entity to which we owe a duty of loyalty and professional responsibility. We do not represent, and will not be deemed to represent, any limited partner, prospective limited partner, placement agent, lender, fund administrator, or any other third party in connection with this matter. Each such third party should engage its own legal counsel as it deems appropriate.

**[2. Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

The scope of our Engagement encompasses the following workstreams, each as more fully described below. Matters that fall outside the scope of this Section 2 are excluded from the Engagement unless separately agreed in writing.

**2.1 Fund Vehicles to Be Formed**

We will form and structure the following entities in connection with the fundraise (collectively, the \"Fund Complex\"):

**(a) Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP (\"HPE Fund V\" or the \"Fund\")** --- a Delaware limited partnership that will serve as the main fund vehicle for the fifth flagship private equity fund. The target hard cap for capital commitments to HPE Fund V is Two Billion Dollars (\$2,000,000,000).

**(b) Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC (the \"General Partner\")** --- a Delaware limited liability company to be organized as the sole general partner of HPE Fund V and the Parallel Fund. The sole member of the General Partner shall be HCP.

**(c) Harrowgate Fund V Parallel LP (the \"Parallel Fund\")** --- a Delaware limited partnership to be organized as a parallel vehicle for the investment by certain tax-exempt and non-U.S. limited partners that may require alternative structuring to address specific tax, regulatory, or policy considerations. The Parallel Fund will invest on a substantially pari passu basis alongside the Fund.

**(d) Harrowgate Fund V Offshore SLP (the \"Offshore Feeder\")** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership to be organized as a feeder vehicle for non-U.S. investors seeking to invest through a non-U.S. jurisdiction. Subject to the exclusion described in Section 2.10 below, our work with respect to the Offshore Feeder will be limited to the drafting of the exempted limited partnership agreement under New York law governing provisions, with Cayman Islands formation filings and CIMA registration to be handled by local Cayman counsel engaged by the Client.

**(e) HGF V blocker Corp. (the \"Blocker\")** --- a Delaware C corporation to be organized as a blocker entity through which certain tax-exempt investors may invest in the Fund Complex in order to mitigate exposure to unrelated business taxable income (\"UBTI\") under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended (the \"Code\").

**2.2 Core Formation Work**

In connection with the formation of the Fund Complex, we will perform the following work:

> \(a\) Drafting and negotiating the Agreement of Limited Partnership of HPE Fund V LP (the \"LPA\"), which shall set forth the terms and conditions governing the formation, governance, investment activities, capital contributions, distributions, allocations, management fees, carried interest, expenses, reporting obligations, and dissolution of the Fund.
>
> \(b\) Drafting the Agreement of Limited Partnership of the Parallel Fund, which shall contain terms and conditions substantially consistent with the LPA, adapted as necessary to accommodate the particular tax, regulatory, and structural considerations applicable to the Parallel Fund\'s investor base.
>
> \(c\) Drafting the Exempted Limited Partnership Agreement of the Offshore Feeder, which shall contain terms and conditions consistent with the LPA, adapted as necessary for the Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership structure and the particular requirements of non-U.S. investors.
>
> \(d\) Drafting the Limited Liability Company Agreement of the General Partner, which shall set forth the governance, capitalization, and operating terms of the General Partner entity.
>
> \(e\) Preparing and filing the Certificate of Limited Partnership for HPE Fund V LP with the Delaware Secretary of State, Division of Corporations.
>
> \(f\) Preparing and filing the Certificate of Formation for Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC with the Delaware Secretary of State, Division of Corporations.
>
> \(g\) Preparing and filing the Certificate of Incorporation for HGF V blocker Corp. with the Delaware Secretary of State, Division of Corporations.
>
> \(h\) Drafting the Bylaws of HGF V blocker Corp., including provisions governing the board of directors, officers, indemnification, and corporate procedures.

**2.3 Offering Documents**

We will prepare the following offering and subscription documents for the Fund Complex:

> \(a\) Drafting and negotiating the Confidential Private Placement Memorandum (the \"PPM\") for HPE Fund V LP, which shall describe the investment strategy, key fund terms, risk factors, tax considerations, regulatory disclosures, track record information for predecessor funds (HPE Fund I through HPE Fund IV), biographies of key investment professionals, and other material information required in connection with the private placement offering.
>
> \(b\) Drafting the form Subscription Agreement and Investor Questionnaire for each vehicle in the Fund Complex (i.e., the Main Fund, the Parallel Fund, and the Offshore Feeder), which shall include customary investor representations, warranties, and certifications (including accredited investor, qualified purchaser, ERISA, FATCA, and anti-money laundering certifications).
>
> \(c\) Drafting the Investor Suitability Questionnaire / Know Your Customer (\"KYC\") Form, incorporating current anti-money laundering and sanctions screening requirements applicable to the Fund Complex.

**2.4 Side Letters and LP Negotiations**

We will perform the following work in connection with side letter negotiations with prospective limited partners:

> \(a\) Preparing a form Side Letter template containing standard concession provisions commonly requested by institutional limited partners, including without limitation provisions addressing most favored nation (\"MFN\") rights, enhanced reporting and transparency requirements, co-investment allocation rights, transfer and secondary sale provisions, ERISA-related representations and covenants, and tax-related provisions (including withholding and allocation matters).
>
> \(b\) Negotiating individual side letters with anchor and institutional limited partners and their respective counsel. As of the date hereof, the following investors and their counsel have been identified as likely participants in the side letter negotiation process:
>
> \(i\) Northmoor State Pension System (counsel: Aldworth & McBride LLP);
>
> \(ii\) The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund (counsel: Pelham Chambers LLP);
>
> \(iii\) Edgecombe Insurance Group Ltd.;
>
> \(iv\) Velthorn Family Office LLC;
>
> \(v\) Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority (counsel: Ramsden Clarke International LLP); and
>
> \(vi\) Stonewall Partners Fund of Funds III LP.
>
> Additional investors and their counsel will be identified as the fundraise progresses, and we will negotiate side letters with such investors as directed by the Client.
>
> \(c\) Preparing the form MFN Election Notice to be distributed to all limited partners entitled to elect the benefit of MFN-protected side letter provisions following each closing.

**Please note:** All work described in this Section 2.4, including the negotiation of individual side letters with limited partners and their respective counsel, will be billed on an hourly basis at the rates set forth in Section 5.1 below and is **outside** the Fee Cap described in Section 5.2 below. This carve-out reflects the inherently unpredictable nature of side letter negotiations, which are driven by the number of investors, the complexity of their requests, and the responsiveness of their counsel. Estimates of anticipated side letter negotiation costs will be provided to the Client as specific LP negotiations commence.

**2.5 Tax Structuring**

Our tax practice will advise on the following matters in connection with the formation and structuring of the Fund Complex:

> \(a\) Advising on the partnership tax classification of the Main Fund and the Parallel Fund under Subchapter K of the Code (Sections 701--777), including confirmation of classification as partnerships for U.S. federal income tax purposes and analysis of relevant elections.
>
> \(b\) Analyzing UBTI considerations for tax-exempt limited partners (including charitable organizations, pension plans, university endowments, and other exempt entities) and advising on the role and structure of the blocker entity in mitigating UBTI exposure under Sections 511--514 of the Code.
>
> \(c\) Analyzing effectively connected income (\"ECI\") and Foreign Investment in Real Property Tax Act (\"FIRPTA\") withholding issues for non-U.S. investors investing through the Offshore Feeder and/or the Main Fund, including analysis of Sections 1445 and 1446 of the Code and applicable income tax treaty provisions.
>
> \(d\) Advising on compliance with Section 1061 of the Code, including the application of the three-year holding period requirement for carried interest (applicable profits interest) received by HCP and its investment professionals in connection with the Fund Complex.
>
> \(e\) Analyzing the Cayman Islands tax neutrality of the Offshore Feeder, including consideration of the economic substance requirements under Cayman Islands law and the absence of Cayman Islands income tax, capital gains tax, or withholding tax applicable to the Offshore Feeder and its partners.
>
> \(f\) Preparing written tax structuring memoranda for the Client summarizing the foregoing analyses and providing recommendations regarding the optimal tax structure for the Fund Complex.
>
> \(g\) Preparing the ERISA Analysis Memorandum, which shall analyze the benefit plan investor percentage threshold under 29 C.F.R. § 2510.3-101(f) (as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA) and advise on procedures and monitoring mechanisms to ensure that the assets of the Fund are not treated as \"plan assets\" under ERISA --- i.e., that benefit plan investors hold less than 25% of the value of each class of equity interests in the Fund (excluding interests held by the General Partner and its affiliates).

**2.6 Regulatory and Compliance**

We will advise on the following regulatory and compliance matters:

> \(a\) Preparing and filing Form D (Notice of Exempt Offering of Securities) with the SEC within fifteen (15) days of the First Close of the Fund, in accordance with the requirements of Regulation D under the Securities Act of 1933, as amended (the \"Securities Act\"), Rule 506(b).
>
> \(b\) Coordinating state blue sky notice filings in all U.S. states and territories where limited partners are domiciled, as required by applicable state securities laws. The number and timing of such filings will depend on the geographic distribution of the Fund\'s investor base, and filing fees incurred in connection therewith will be billed to the Client at cost.
>
> \(c\) Advising on the qualification of the Fund under Section 3(c)(7) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended (the \"Investment Company Act\"), including confirmation that all investors in the Fund are \"qualified purchasers\" as defined in Section 2(a)(51) of the Investment Company Act.
>
> \(d\) Advising on Investment Advisers Act compliance matters as applicable to the fundraise, including consideration of advertising and performance presentation requirements, Form ADV disclosure updates, and custody rule compliance.
>
> \(e\) Preparing the Placement Agent Disclosure & Compliance Memorandum regarding Osprey Capital Markets LLC, which has been engaged by the Client as the placement agent for the Fund. This memorandum will address compliance with SEC guidance on placement agent disclosures, state pay-to-play restrictions, and Rule 206(4)-5 under the Investment Advisers Act (political contributions and placement agent regulations for government entity investors).

**2.7 Ancillary and Administrative Documents**

We will prepare the following ancillary and administrative documents for use in connection with the Fund\'s operations:

> \(a\) Drafting the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") Charter / Terms of Reference, setting forth the composition, authority, meeting procedures, and conflict-of-interest review protocols for the LPAC.
>
> \(b\) Drafting the form Capital Call Notice, to be used by the General Partner in connection with drawdowns of capital commitments from limited partners.
>
> \(c\) Drafting the form Distribution Notice, to be used by the General Partner in connection with distributions to limited partners.
>
> \(d\) Drafting the form Transfer (Assignment) Agreement, to be used in connection with any permitted transfer or assignment of a limited partner\'s interest in the Fund in accordance with the transfer provisions of the LPA.
>
> \(e\) Preparing the First Close Checklist, which shall set forth all conditions precedent, deliverables, filings, and corporate actions required to be completed or delivered on or prior to the First Close of the Fund.

**2.8 Legal Opinions**

We will deliver the following legal opinions at the First Close of the Fund:

> \(a\) A legal opinion addressed to the Fund, the General Partner, and (to the extent required by the LPA or any side letter) the limited partners, as to the valid formation of HPE Fund V LP and Harrowgate Fund V GP LLC under the Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act and the Delaware Limited Liability Company Act, respectively, and as to the enforceability of the LPA against the parties thereto (subject to customary exceptions, qualifications, and assumptions).
>
> \(b\) A legal opinion addressed to the Fund and the General Partner as to the availability of the Regulation D, Rule 506(b) exemption from registration under the Securities Act with respect to the offering and sale of limited partnership interests in the Fund, and as to the availability of the Section 3(c)(7) exclusion from registration under the Investment Company Act (subject to customary exceptions, qualifications, and assumptions, including reliance on the representations of the limited partners in their respective Subscription Agreements).

**2.9 Third-Party Agreement Review**

We will review and comment on the following third-party agreements:

> \(a\) Reviewing and marking up the Fund Administration Agreement to be entered into between the Fund and Pinnacle Fund Services LLC, the Client\'s selected fund administrator. Our review will focus on the scope of services, standard of care, liability and indemnification provisions, data security obligations, and termination provisions.
>
> \(b\) Reviewing the indicative term sheet for the subscription credit facility (the \"Credit Facility\") to be provided by Ashford National Bank, N.A. to the Fund. The Credit Facility contemplates a revolving credit commitment of up to Five Hundred Million Dollars (\$500,000,000), secured by the unfunded capital commitments of the limited partners. We will prepare a Term Sheet Review Memorandum summarizing the key terms, conditions, and legal issues raised by the indicative term sheet, including borrowing conditions, advance rates, collateral coverage ratios, events of default, and limited partner consent requirements.

**Please note:** The negotiation of definitive subscription credit facility documentation (including the credit agreement, security agreement, account control agreements, and related documents) is not included within the scope of this Engagement. If the Client desires the Firm\'s assistance in negotiating definitive Credit Facility documentation, such work will be scoped as a separate workstream and will be subject to a separate fee arrangement to be agreed upon between the parties.

**2.10 Excluded Matters**

The following matters are expressly excluded from the scope of this Engagement:

> \(a\) Representation of any limited partner or prospective limited partner in the Fund Complex in connection with their investment in the Fund, the negotiation of side letters, or any other matter.
>
> \(b\) Cayman Islands legal advice. The Client shall engage local Cayman Islands counsel for the formation and filing of the Offshore Feeder with the Cayman Islands Registrar of Exempted Limited Partnerships, and for any registration or notification requirements under the Mutual Funds Act (as revised) with the Cayman Islands Monetary Authority (\"CIMA\"). We will coordinate with such Cayman Islands counsel as necessary in connection with the Engagement but will not render opinions or advice on matters of Cayman Islands law.
>
> \(c\) Negotiation of definitive subscription credit facility documentation (including the credit agreement, security documents, and ancillary financing documents), unless separately agreed in writing as described in Section 2.9 above.
>
> \(d\) Portfolio company-level acquisition work, including due diligence, negotiation and drafting of acquisition agreements, and post-closing integration matters.
>
> \(e\) Regulatory examinations or enforcement matters, including SEC examinations, inquiries, or proceedings.
>
> \(f\) Litigation of any kind, including disputes with limited partners, counterparties, portfolio companies, or regulators.

**[3. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

The following attorneys will serve as the core engagement team for this matter. The Client may direct questions or communications to any member of the team, and the Responsible Partner and Billing Partner identified below will have overall supervisory responsibility for the quality and timeliness of our work product.

**Graham Sutherland** --- *Responsible Partner*, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group (Wilmington office). Mr. Sutherland has twenty-four (24) years of experience in private equity fund formation and investment management matters. He will have overall responsibility for the Engagement and will serve as the primary relationship partner for HCP. Mr. Sutherland can be reached at gsutherland@calderwoodharkness.com or (302) 555-7810.

**Pamela Cross** --- *Billing Partner*, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group (New York office). Ms. Cross has twenty (20) years of experience in fund formation and institutional investor relations. She will oversee billing, budgeting, and day-to-day project management for the Engagement, including coordination of internal resources and monitoring of progress against the fundraise timeline. Ms. Cross can be reached at pcross@calderwoodharkness.com or (212) 555-9415.

**Stephen Adler** --- *Lead Associate*, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group (Wilmington office). Mr. Adler is a seventh-year associate with significant experience in the formation of private equity, venture capital, and credit fund vehicles. He will serve as the primary drafter of the LPA, PPM, subscription documents, and ancillary formation documents for the Fund Complex. Mr. Adler can be reached at sadler@calderwoodharkness.com or (302) 555-7822.

**Theresa Kim** --- *Working Associate*, Funds & Asset Management Practice Group (New York office). Ms. Kim is a fourth-year associate who will assist with document drafting, third-party agreement review (including the Pinnacle Fund Services administration agreement and the Ashford National Bank term sheet review), regulatory filings (Form D, blue sky notices), and investor communications. Ms. Kim can be reached at tkim@calderwoodharkness.com or (212) 555-9428.

**Sylvia Hartwell** --- *Specialist Partner*, Tax Practice Group (New York office). Ms. Hartwell has eighteen (18) years of experience in partnership taxation, fund structuring, and international tax planning for private investment funds. She will advise on all fund-level tax structuring matters described in Section 2.5 above, including the design of the blocker entity, the structure of the parallel vehicles, the ERISA analysis, Section 1061 carried interest compliance, and international tax considerations for the Offshore Feeder and non-U.S. investors. Ms. Hartwell can be reached at shartwell@calderwoodharkness.com or (212) 555-9440.

Additional attorneys, paraprofessionals, or other support staff may be assigned to the Engagement as needed to ensure timely and efficient delivery of work product. The Client will be informed of any material changes to the composition of the core engagement team.

**[4. Client Responsibilities]{.underline}**

The efficient and timely completion of the Engagement will depend on the Client\'s cooperation in providing information, reviewing drafts, and coordinating with third parties. In particular, the Client agrees to the following:

> \(a\) **Information Provision.** The Client shall provide, on a timely basis, all information necessary for the preparation of the formation and offering documents, including (without limitation) information regarding the investment strategy, target geographies and sectors, fund terms (including management fees, carried interest, hurdle rate, waterfall structure, GP commitment, key person provisions, and investment period terms), and track record data for the predecessor funds (Harrowgate Private Equity Fund I LP through Harrowgate Private Equity Fund IV LP), including realized and unrealized performance data, attribution, and relevant disclaimers.
>
> \(b\) **Draft Review Timeline.** The Client shall review and provide comments on drafts within the timelines agreed upon between the Client and the Firm in order to meet the following target fundraise schedule:
>
> \(i\) PPM initial draft delivered by the Firm to the Client: **May 1, 2025**;
>
> \(ii\) LPA initial draft delivered by the Firm to the Client: **May 9, 2025**;
>
> \(iii\) Distribution of PPM, LPA summary, and subscription documents to prospective limited partners: **June 2, 2025**; and
>
> \(iv\) Target First Close: **August 15, 2025**.
>
> The foregoing timeline is subject to adjustment based on the Client\'s review and comment cycle and the progress of investor negotiations. The Firm and the Client will communicate regularly regarding the status of the fundraise timeline and will work cooperatively to address any delays or changes in schedule.
>
> \(c\) **Investor Counsel Coordination.** The Client shall coordinate communications with investor-side counsel, including but not limited to:
>
> \(i\) Aldworth & McBride LLP, counsel for Northmoor State Pension System;
>
> \(ii\) Pelham Chambers LLP, counsel for The Kingsbridge Endowment Fund; and
>
> \(iii\) Ramsden Clarke International LLP, counsel for Tidewater Sovereign Investment Authority.
>
> The Client shall provide introductions and facilitate initial communications between the Firm and investor-side counsel as necessary to commence side letter negotiations.
>
> \(d\) **Third-Party Coordination.** The Client shall be responsible for the engagement and coordination of the placement agent (Osprey Capital Markets LLC) and the fund administrator (Pinnacle Fund Services LLC), and shall facilitate the Firm\'s access to such parties and their respective documentation as necessary for the Firm to perform the work described in Section 2.
>
> \(e\) **Cayman Islands Counsel.** The Client shall engage local Cayman Islands counsel as necessary for the formation and regulatory filings of the Offshore Feeder. The Client shall provide the Firm with the identity and contact information of such Cayman Islands counsel in a timely manner so that we may coordinate the drafting of the Offshore Feeder\'s exempted limited partnership agreement.
>
> \(f\) **PPM Data.** The Client shall provide final data for the predecessor fund performance tables, team biographies, and other factual content to be included in the PPM. The Client shall be responsible for the accuracy and completeness of all factual information provided for inclusion in the PPM.

**[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**

**5.1 Billing Rates**

Our current standard hourly billing rates for calendar year 2025 are as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Timekeeper Level**                **Rate Range**
  ----------------------------------- -----------------------------------
  Partners                            \$1,450 -- \$1,650 per hour

  Associates                          \$850 -- \$1,050 per hour
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The specific billing rate for each attorney will be determined based on the attorney\'s seniority, expertise, and role on the Engagement. Within the above ranges, current hourly rates for the core engagement team members are: Mr. Sutherland (\$1,625/hr); Ms. Cross (\$1,575/hr); Ms. Hartwell (\$1,600/hr); Mr. Adler (\$1,025/hr); and Ms. Kim (\$900/hr).

Billing rates are subject to annual adjustment, typically effective as of January 1 of each calendar year. The Client will be notified in advance of any rate changes applicable to the Engagement. Any such rate change will apply only to time recorded on or after the effective date of the change.

Calderwood & Harkness LLP has been engaged to represent Briarwood Family Office LLC (\"BFO\" or the \"Client\") in connection with the negotiation and execution of a side letter to the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership (the \"LPA\") of Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. Fund IV pursues a value-add and opportunistic investment strategy focused on North American commercial real estate, real estate operating companies, and asset management platforms. Calloway (BFO, Director of External Investments) contacted Calderwood & Harkness LLP on January 15, 2024, to discuss potential representation in connection with the proposed commitment and side-letter negotiation. > **(a)** **Review and Analysis of Fund Documents.** Review and analysis of the Fund IV Limited Partnership Agreement, dated December 20, 2023, and the Fund IV Private Placement Memorandum, dated December 15, 2023, including all exhibits, schedules, and ancillary documents. >
> **(c)** **Subscription Documentation.** Review, markup, and finalization of the Fund IV subscription agreement and investor questionnaire, including all related representations, warranties, certifications, and supporting documentation required for admission to the Fund.
>
> **(d)** **Advisory on Fund Terms, Economics, and Governance.** Ongoing advisory services to the Client regarding the economic and governance terms of the Fund, including but not limited to management fees, carried interest, preferred return mechanics, clawback provisions, key-person provisions, no-fault divorce and removal rights, investment restrictions and concentration limits, co-investment rights, reporting and transparency provisions, most-favored-nation (\"MFN\") protections, transfer restrictions, and excuse and exclusion provisions.

Third, the Helix SaaS Holdings Ltd. interest is held through a Cayman Islands exempted company, and the contribution of that interest to a domestic partnership will require careful analysis of any potential outbound transfer issues, even though our preliminary view is that IRC § 367 does not apply to partnership-to-partnership transfers.

**[V. Business Rationale for the Reorganization]{.underline}**

Stefan Dalmqvist and Priya Narasimhan articulated four principal business rationales for the proposed reorganization during the intake calls. These rationales are summarized below and will be incorporated into the PLR request to establish the non-tax business purpose underlying the transaction, consistent with the requirements of Rev. Proc. 2025-1 and the IRS\'s general expectation that ruling requests demonstrate a bona fide business purpose independent of any tax benefit.

**A. Operational Cost Reduction**

Solara currently incurs approximately \$3.8 million annually in duplicative offshore administration, audit, and regulatory fees across the four Cayman and Luxembourg vehicles. These costs include fund administration fees paid to Clarendon Fund Services Ltd. for each offshore vehicle, annual audit fees for separate financial statement audits of each offshore entity conducted by Caldwell Pierce & Co. LLP (or its affiliated international member firms), CIMA annual registration fees for the two Cayman vehicles, Luxembourg regulatory compliance costs for the two SCSp vehicles, and fees for local registered office and corporate services providers in both jurisdictions. Additionally, Solara\'s internal tax and compliance team devotes approximately 2,400 hours annually to managing the multi-jurisdictional fund structure, including the preparation and coordination of separate tax filings, investor reports, and regulatory submissions for each vehicle.

Consolidation of the four offshore vehicles into a single Delaware-domiciled Consolidated Master Fund LP, with two Cayman feeder vehicles (one for non-U.S. investors and one for U.S. tax-exempt investors), would substantially reduce these recurring costs. Solara estimates annual savings of approximately \$2.1 million in external fees and a meaningful reduction in internal staff time. Over the remaining projected life of the Fund IV and Fund V investments (estimated at five to seven years), these savings are expected to total between \$10.5 million and \$14.7 million on an undiscounted basis.

**B. OECD Pillar Two GloBE Rules**

The OECD Pillar Two Global Anti-Base Erosion (\"GloBE\") rules, as implemented in Luxembourg through the Grand Ducal Law of December 22, 2023, transposing Council Directive (EU) 2022/2523 (the \"EU Minimum Tax Directive\"), became effective for Solara\'s Luxembourg entities beginning with fiscal year 2025. These rules impose a minimum effective tax rate of 15% on the income of constituent entities of multinational enterprise groups meeting specified revenue thresholds. While the Luxembourg SCSp vehicles were historically attractive to certain non-U.S. investors due to the combination of Luxembourg\'s favorable tax treaty network and the tax transparency of the SCSp structure, the GloBE rules have substantially diminished the incremental tax benefits historically obtained through the Luxembourg-domiciled structures.

Stefan Dalmqvist noted during the May 22 call that the firm\'s preliminary analysis, conducted in consultation with Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l. (Luxembourg counsel), indicates that the top-up tax liability exposure for certain Luxembourg vehicle constituent entities could range from €2.5 million to €4.2 million annually, which, when combined with the incremental compliance costs of Pillar Two reporting, further erodes the economic rationale for maintaining separate Luxembourg vehicles. The reorganization would eliminate the Luxembourg SCSp vehicles entirely, thereby avoiding both the substantive top-up tax exposure and the associated compliance burden.

**C. FATCA and CRS Compliance Simplification**

The current multi-jurisdictional fund structure creates duplicative reporting obligations under the Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (\"FATCA\") and the OECD\'s Common Reporting Standard (\"CRS\"). Each offshore vehicle is separately registered as a reporting financial institution under FATCA and CRS in its jurisdiction of organization, resulting in separate FATCA reporting to the IRS (via the Cayman Islands and Luxembourg intergovernmental agreements) and separate CRS reporting to the relevant local tax authorities for exchange with other participating jurisdictions. The consolidation of the four offshore vehicles into a Delaware master fund with two Cayman feeders would simplify these compliance obligations by reducing the number of reporting entities from four to two (the two remaining Cayman feeders), while the consolidated master fund would report directly to the IRS as a domestic partnership.

Stefan Dalmqvist estimated that the duplicative FATCA and CRS compliance currently costs approximately \$450,000 annually in external advisory and filing fees and consumes approximately 600 hours of internal staff time.

**D. LP-Requested Governance Simplification**

The limited partners, acting through the LP Advisory Committee, have formally requested that Solara explore a streamlined governance structure for the fund platform. The LPAC\'s concerns centered on the complexity of the existing structure, including the need to review and approve matters separately across six parallel vehicles, the lack of a unified governance framework, and the administrative burden of maintaining multiple sets of fund documents with differing governing law provisions (Delaware, Cayman, and Luxembourg).

Preliminary LP consent to explore the reorganization was obtained at the LPAC meeting held on April 22, 2025, with 78% in interest of the LPAC members approving the exploration of the proposed restructuring. This approval was advisory in nature; formal LP consent to the actual reorganization will be required under the applicable limited partnership agreements and will be sought following completion of the PLR process. The LPAC is represented by independent counsel, Whitfield, Carruthers & Doyle LLP, with Diana Carruthers, Partner (Fund Formation & Tax), serving as the lead partner. Ms. Carruthers\'s office is located at 200 South Biscayne Boulevard, Suite 4000, Miami, Florida 33131. Calderwood & Harkness anticipates coordinating with Ms. Carruthers on the PLR process and the terms of the formal LP consent.

**[VI. Proposed Reorganization --- Multi-Step Transaction]{.underline}**

**A. Overview.** The proposed reorganization consists of five integrated steps, planned for execution in the fourth quarter of 2025, with a target effective date of December 1, 2025 for the final step. The reorganization is designed to domesticate and merge the four offshore fund vehicles --- Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP, Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp, Fund V-A (Cayman) LP, and Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp --- into a newly established Delaware-domiciled master fund structure, the Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP. Following the reorganization, the platform will consist of three Delaware partnerships (the existing Fund IV LP, the existing Fund V LP, and the new Consolidated Master Fund LP), together with two Cayman Islands feeder partnerships (one for non-U.S. investors and one for U.S. tax-exempt investors) that will invest through the Consolidated Master Fund LP. The five steps of the proposed reorganization are described in detail below.

The engagement team notes at the outset that the multi-step nature of the transaction raises potential step transaction doctrine issues, which will need to be addressed in the PLR request. The steps are structured to occur over a period of approximately ten weeks (from the target date for Step 2 on October 1, 2025, through the target effective date for Step 5 on December 1, 2025) and are designed to be independently meaningful and separately motivated, but the IRS may seek to collapse the steps for analytical purposes. The PLR request will need to address the step transaction doctrine proactively, as discussed further in Section VIII below.

**B. Step 1 --- Formation of New Entities (Target: September 15, 2025)**

Step 1 involves the formation of four new entities that will constitute the post-reorganization fund platform:

> 1\. **Solara Consolidated Master Fund GP LLC** --- a Delaware limited liability company to serve as the general partner of the Consolidated Master Fund LP. This entity will be manager-managed, with Viktor Raines as the sole manager, mirroring the governance structure of the existing Solara Digital Infrastructure GP LLC.
>
> 2\. **Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP** --- a Delaware limited partnership that will serve as the master fund into which all offshore vehicle portfolio assets will be contributed. This entity will be the central investment vehicle in the post-reorganization structure.
>
> 3\. **Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership that will serve as the feeder fund for non-U.S. investors. Non-U.S. limited partners currently invested in the offshore vehicles will be migrated to this feeder in Step 5.
>
> 4\. **Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP** --- a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership that will serve as the feeder fund for U.S. tax-exempt investors, designed to mitigate UBTI concerns by maintaining appropriate UBTI blocker structures between the feeder and the master fund\'s debt-financed investments.

Concurrently with formation, IRS Form 8832 (Entity Classification Election) will be filed for each new entity to elect classification as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes under Treasury Regulation § 301.7701-3. Although the default classification for a domestic LLC with two or more members and a domestic limited partnership is partnership classification, affirmative elections will be filed for the avoidance of doubt and to establish a clear record for the PLR submission. For the two Cayman feeder entities, affirmative elections are necessary because a foreign eligible entity with two or more members defaults to partnership classification only if at least one member has unlimited liability; the exempted limited partnership structure may present ambiguity depending on the terms of the partnership agreement, and an affirmative election eliminates any uncertainty. The engagement team will work with Meridian Offshore Legal (Cayman counsel) on the formation of the two new Cayman vehicles.

**C. Step 2 --- Contribution of Fund IV-A Cayman Assets (Target: October 1, 2025)**

In Step 2, Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP will contribute all of its portfolio assets --- consisting of interests in portfolio companies, cash, and other fund-level assets --- to the newly formed Solara Consolidated Master Fund LP in exchange for a limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund. The key financial parameters of this contribution are as follows:

> • **Aggregate Fair Market Value:** \$2.31 billion
>
> • **Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis:** \$1.62 billion
>
> • **Aggregate Built-In Gain:** \$690 million

The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment of Step 2 is as a tax-free contribution under IRC § 721(a), which provides that no gain or loss shall be recognized to a partnership or to any of its partners in the case of a contribution of property to the partnership in exchange for an interest in the partnership. No gain or loss would be recognized by Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP as the contributing partner or by the Consolidated Master Fund LP as the receiving partnership.

Several ancillary tax provisions will require careful analysis in connection with Step 2:

> • **IRC § 721(b) Exception.** Section 721(b) provides that Section 721(a) does not apply to gain realized on a transfer of property to a partnership that would be treated as an \"investment company\" (within the meaning of IRC § 351(e)) if the partnership were incorporated. The engagement team will need to analyze whether the Consolidated Master Fund LP, after receiving the contributed assets, would constitute an investment company. Our preliminary view, based on the intake facts, is that the portfolio consists of operating companies in the digital infrastructure and SaaS sectors --- not stocks, securities, or other passive investment assets --- and therefore the investment company exception should not apply. However, this analysis will require a detailed review of the composition of the contributed assets and the definition of \"stock and securities\" under Treas. Reg. § 1.351-1(c)(1).
>
> • **Carryover Basis.** Under IRC § 723, the Consolidated Master Fund LP will take a carryover basis in the contributed assets equal to the adjusted tax basis of such assets in the hands of Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP immediately prior to the contribution. This preserves the \$690 million built-in gain for future recognition upon a taxable disposition of the contributed assets.
>
> • **Holding Period Tacking.** Under IRC § 1223(2), the Consolidated Master Fund LP\'s holding period in the contributed assets will include the period during which Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP held such assets, provided the assets were capital assets or property described in IRC § 1231 in the hands of the contributing partner. This tacking is critical for preserving long-term capital gain treatment on future dispositions.

**D. Step 3 --- Contribution of Fund IV-B Luxembourg Assets (Target: October 15, 2025)**

In Step 3, Solara Digital Partners Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp will contribute all of its portfolio assets to the Consolidated Master Fund LP in exchange for a limited partnership interest. The key financial parameters are as follows:

> • **Aggregate Fair Market Value:** €1.07 billion / \$1.16 billion (at 1.08 EUR/USD)
>
> • **Aggregate Adjusted Tax Basis:** €782 million / \$844.6 million
>
> • **Aggregate Built-In Gain:** €288 million / \$311 million

The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment is the same as Step 2: a tax-free contribution under IRC § 721(a), with no gain or loss recognized by the contributing Luxembourg SCSp or by the Consolidated Master Fund LP. The Section 721(b) investment company exception analysis and the carryover basis and holding period tacking analysis described in connection with Step 2 apply equally to Step 3.

Step 3 raises two additional tax issues not present in Step 2:

> • **IRC § 367 Analysis.** Step 3 involves the transfer of assets by a foreign partnership (the Luxembourg SCSp) to a domestic partnership (the Consolidated Master Fund LP). IRC § 367(a) provides special rules for transfers of property from the United States to foreign corporations, and IRC § 367(b) provides rules for certain exchanges involving foreign corporations. Our preliminary position is that IRC § 367 does not apply to the Step 3 contribution because Section 367, by its terms, applies to transfers to or from *corporations*, not partnerships. The Luxembourg SCSp is classified as a partnership for U.S. federal income tax purposes, and the Consolidated Master Fund LP is likewise a domestic partnership. Accordingly, the Section 367 gain recognition rules and outbound transfer provisions should not be implicated. Nevertheless, given the aggregate built-in gain of \$311 million and the cross-border nature of the transfer, we expect the IRS to scrutinize this position, and we recommend including a specific ruling request on this point.
>
> • **Luxembourg Withholding Tax Analysis.** Under Luxembourg domestic law, the SCSp is a tax-transparent entity, and no Luxembourg capital gains tax is expected to apply at the SCSp level on the transfer of its portfolio assets to the Consolidated Master Fund LP. Specifically, Article 3(2) of the Luxembourg law of July 12, 2013 provides that the SCSp is not itself subject to Luxembourg income tax; rather, each partner is subject to tax in its jurisdiction of residence on its allocable share of SCSp income. Solara\'s Luxembourg counsel, Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l., will provide a formal opinion on this point. Additionally, to the extent any deemed disposition occurs at the partner level, the engagement team will analyze whether Section 1446 withholding obligations arise with respect to any effectively connected income allocable to the foreign partners of the Luxembourg SCSp.

**E. Step 4 --- Contribution of Fund V Offshore Assets (Target: November 1, 2025)**

Step 4 replicates the contribution structure of Steps 2 and 3 with respect to the Fund V offshore vehicles. Specifically:

> • **Fund V-A (Cayman) LP** will contribute all of its portfolio assets to the Consolidated Master Fund LP in exchange for a limited partnership interest. Aggregate FMV: \$2.89 billion; aggregate adjusted tax basis: \$2.34 billion; aggregate built-in gain: \$550 million.
>
> • **Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp** will contribute all of its portfolio assets to the Consolidated Master Fund LP in exchange for a limited partnership interest. Aggregate FMV: €1.29 billion / \$1.39 billion (at 1.08 EUR/USD); aggregate adjusted tax basis: €1.14 billion / \$1.23 billion; aggregate built-in gain: €150 million / \$162 million.

The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment of both contributions is the same as Steps 2 and 3: tax-free contributions under IRC § 721(a), with no gain or loss recognized. The same ancillary analyses --- including the Section 721(b) investment company exception, Section 367 inapplicability to partnership-to-partnership transfers, Luxembourg withholding tax, Section 1446 withholding, carryover basis under Section 723, and holding period tacking under Section 1223(2) --- apply to the Step 4 contributions.

The engagement team notes that Step 4 is scheduled to occur one month after the completion of Step 2 (the Fund IV-A Cayman contribution) and approximately two weeks after the completion of Step 3 (the Fund IV-B Luxembourg contribution). The compressed timeline between Steps 2 through 4 reinforces the need to address step transaction doctrine concerns in the PLR request, as discussed in Section VIII below.

**F. Step 5 --- Dissolution of Legacy Offshore Vehicles and LP Migration (Target: December 1, 2025)**

Step 5 is the final step of the reorganization and involves two integrated sub-steps:

**Sub-Step 5(a): Dissolution and Distribution.** Each of the four legacy offshore vehicles --- Fund IV-A (Cayman) LP, Fund IV-B (Luxembourg) SCSp, Fund V-A (Cayman) LP, and Fund V-B (Luxembourg) SCSp --- will dissolve and distribute its respective limited partnership interest in the Consolidated Master Fund LP (received in Steps 2 through 4) to its existing limited partners in complete liquidation. Following these distributions, the four legacy offshore vehicles will cease to exist as legal entities. The dissolution of the two Cayman vehicles will be effected in accordance with the Cayman Islands Exempted Limited Partnership Act (As Revised) and will require CIMA deregistration, to be coordinated by Meridian Offshore Legal. The dissolution of the two Luxembourg SCSps will be effected in accordance with the Luxembourg law of July 12, 2013 and will require notification to the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (\"CSSF\"), to be coordinated by Veldhuis & Gérard S.à r.l.

**Sub-Step 5(b): LP Migration to Feeders.** Following receipt of their respective Consolidated Master Fund LP interests, the limited partners of the dissolved offshore vehicles will be allocated to the appropriate feeder vehicle based on their investor category:

> • **Non-U.S. investors** (e.g., Nordhaven Sovereign Wealth Fund, Kestrel Pacific Insurance Group) will contribute their Consolidated Master Fund LP interests to Solara International Feeder (Cayman) LP in exchange for limited partnership interests in the feeder.
>
> • **U.S. tax-exempt investors** (e.g., Pinnacle State Employees\' Retirement System, Grandview University Endowment) will contribute their Consolidated Master Fund LP interests to Solara Tax-Exempt Feeder (Cayman) LP in exchange for limited partnership interests in the feeder.

The intended U.S. federal income tax treatment of the liquidating distributions in Sub-Step 5(a) is as tax-free distributions under IRC § 731(a), which provides that in the case of a distribution by a partnership to a partner, gain is recognized only to the extent that any money distributed exceeds the adjusted basis of the partner\'s interest in the partnership immediately before the distribution. Because the dissolved vehicles will distribute only partnership interests (in the Consolidated Master Fund LP), and not money or other property, no gain should be recognized under Section 731(a), provided that the distributed partnership interests do not constitute \"marketable securities\" within the meaning of IRC § 731(c).

The engagement team will need to conduct a thorough analysis of IRC § 731(c), which treats the distribution of \"marketable securities\" by a partnership as a distribution of money, potentially triggering gain recognition. The term \"marketable securities\" is defined in Section 731(c)(2) to include, among other things, interests that are \"actively traded\" within the meaning of IRC § 1092(d)(1). The Consolidated Master Fund LP interests to be distributed in Step 5 are limited partnership interests in a private investment fund and are not publicly traded or actively traded on an established securities market. Accordingly, our preliminary view is that Section 731(c) should not apply to these distributions. However, this analysis will require further review, and the PLR request will include a specific ruling on this point.

The contributions of Consolidated Master Fund LP interests by the non-U.S. and U.S. tax-exempt LPs to the new feeder vehicles in Sub-Step 5(b) are intended to be treated as additional tax-free contributions under IRC § 721(a).

\(c\) Drafting and negotiating limited liability company agreements for each of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including provisions governing capital contributions, profit and loss allocations, distribution waterfalls, governance (including voting and consent requirements), transfer restrictions, withdrawal and removal mechanics, non-compete and non-solicitation covenants, and such other provisions as may be appropriate.

\(d\) Preparing amended and restated limited liability company agreements for the General Partner and the ManCo to reflect the new holding-company structure, including modifications to membership interest provisions, management and officer provisions, and capital account and allocation provisions necessitated by the interposition of HoldCo and GP Intermediate.

\(b\) Analyzing compliance with the Fund\'s fourteen (14) existing side letters, with particular attention to key-person provisions under Section 5.2 of the LPA and any expanded or supplemental key-person provisions contained in certain side letters, to determine whether the departures of Mr. Kellner and Ms. Trask or the structural changes contemplated by the restructuring trigger key-person events, consent requirements, or notification obligations under any such side letter.

\(d\) Advising on the preparation and filing of an amended SEC Form ADV (Parts 1 and 2) to reflect the restructuring, and advising on any other regulatory filings or notifications required in connection with the restructuring, including any applicable state regulatory filings.

**2.5 Tax Structuring**

Calderwood & Harkness will provide tax analysis and structuring advice in connection with the restructuring, including:

\(a\) Federal income tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including the tax treatment of the contribution or transfer of interests in the General Partner and the ManCo to HoldCo.

\(b\) Delaware tax analysis of the formation of HoldCo and GP Intermediate, including any applicable Delaware franchise taxes, formation taxes, or annual reporting obligations.

\(c\) Federal income tax analysis of the reallocation of carried interest among the principals, including the application of Section 1061 of the Internal Revenue Code and any implications arising from the modification of existing partnership interests.

\(d\) Tax analysis of the economic arrangements with departing principals, including the characterization of carry retention payments and the tax treatment of any consideration paid in connection with the separation arrangements.

\(e\) Section 704(b) and Section 704(c) analysis of built-in gain allocations with respect to existing Fund investments, including the impact of the restructuring on the allocation of built-in gains and losses among the principals and the mechanics for tracking and allocating such amounts through the revised entity structure.

\(f\) All tax structuring advice under this engagement will be provided by Sylvia Hartwell, Specialist Partner (Tax), who will coordinate as necessary with the Client\'s independent accountants at Heathrow Whitman & Co.

**2.6 Limitations on Scope**

The scope of this engagement is limited to the matters described in Sections 2.1 through 2.5 above. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, the following matters are expressly excluded from the scope of this engagement:

\(a\) Routine fund operations, portfolio company transactions, and ongoing limited partner communications unrelated to the restructuring described herein. We understand that such matters will continue to be handled by Pemberton Hale LLP (Victoria Langford, Partner), which serves as the Fund\'s existing fund formation and operations counsel.

\(b\) Accounting, auditing, and valuation services, which we understand are provided by Heathrow Whitman & Co. (accountants and auditors) and Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation), respectively. Nothing in this engagement shall be construed as the provision of accounting, auditing, or valuation advice by Calderwood & Harkness.

\(c\) Representation of any departing principal, including David Kellner and Joanna Trask, in connection with the restructuring or any other matter. Each departing principal is separately represented by Whitford & Chase LLP.

\(d\) Representation of any limited partner of the Fund in connection with the restructuring or any other matter.

To the extent matters arise during the course of this engagement that fall outside the scope described herein but that may benefit from our involvement, we will discuss with the Client whether and on what terms such matters should be added to the scope of this engagement or addressed through a separate engagement.

The Client will be notified in advance of any such additions to the engagement team.

**[4. Fee Arrangement and Billing]{.underline}**

**4.1 Hourly Rates**

Fees for services rendered in connection with this engagement will be charged on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:

**CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **Attorneys at Law** 555 California Street, 40th Floor San Francisco, CA 94104 Telephone: (415) 392-7800 Facsimile: (415) 392-7801 www.calderwoodharkness.com

>
