**Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- Side Letter Agreements and Most Favored Nation Election Framework for Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP**

Dear Mr. Mehta and Ms. Dubois:

**[1. Purpose and Confirmation of Engagement]{.underline}**

Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"Calderwood & Harkness\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Pinnacle Venture Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (the \"GP\"), in its capacity as the general partner of Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP, a Delaware limited partnership (the \"Fund\"), in connection with the negotiation, preparation, and documentation of side letter agreements with certain anchor limited partners of the Fund and the structuring and documentation of the most favored nation (\"MFN\") election framework applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund, each as more fully described in Section 2 below.

The Fund was organized pursuant to a Certificate of Limited Partnership filed with the Office of the Secretary of State of the State of Delaware on August 12, 2025, under File No. 7924813. The rights, obligations, and governance terms of the Fund and its limited partners will be set forth in the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of the Fund, to be dated as of the date of the Fund\'s initial closing (the \"First Close\") (as may be further amended, restated, supplemented, or otherwise modified from time to time, the \"LPA\"). The side letters to be prepared in connection with this engagement will supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable limited partner, modify certain terms of the LPA in the manner described herein.

This letter (the \"Engagement Letter\") sets forth the terms and conditions of our engagement, including the scope of the Firm\'s representation, the engagement team, our fee arrangements, and other matters relevant to the attorney-client relationship between Calderwood & Harkness and the GP. We ask that you review this Engagement Letter carefully and confirm your agreement to its terms by countersigning a copy of this letter as provided in Section 13 below.

**[2. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

The scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s engagement in connection with the Fund\'s side letter program and MFN election framework shall encompass the following:

**(a) Anchor Limited Partner Side Letter Agreements**

Calderwood & Harkness will draft, negotiate, and finalize individual side letter agreements (each, a \"Side Letter\") with the following three anchor limited partners of the Fund (collectively, the \"Anchor LPs\"):

> \(i\) **Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System** (\"Cascadia PERS\"), a governmental pension plan organized under the laws of the State of Washington. Cascadia PERS has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Seventy-Five Million Dollars (\$75,000,000), representing approximately 12.5% of the Fund\'s target fund size of Six Hundred Million Dollars (\$600,000,000) (the \"Target Fund Size\").
>
> \(ii\) **Northstar Endowment Partners LLC** (\"Northstar\"), a limited liability company organized under the laws of the State of Delaware, serving as the dedicated investment vehicle for the endowment of Veltrano University. Northstar has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000), representing approximately 8.33% of the Target Fund Size.
>
> \(iii\) **Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP** (\"Brindoval\"), a limited partnership organized under the laws of the State of Delaware. Brindoval has committed to a capital commitment to the Fund in the amount of Forty Million Dollars (\$40,000,000), representing approximately 6.67% of the Target Fund Size.

The aggregate capital commitments of the Anchor LPs total One Hundred Sixty-Five Million Dollars (\$165,000,000), representing approximately 27.5% of the Target Fund Size. Given the significance of these commitments to the Fund\'s initial closing and overall capital formation, the Firm understands that the timely completion of Side Letter negotiations with each of the Anchor LPs is a priority for the GP.

**(b) Side Letter Terms and Provisions**

Each Side Letter will be structured to supplement and, solely as between the GP and the applicable Anchor LP, modify certain terms and conditions of the LPA. The specific provisions to be addressed in each Side Letter will vary based on the nature, regulatory status, and specific requirements of the applicable Anchor LP, but are expected to include, as applicable, the following categories of terms:

> \(i\) **Management fee concessions**, including reduced management fee rates, management fee offsets, and fee calculation methodologies applicable during the investment period and the post-investment period;
>
> \(ii\) **Co-investment rights**, including rights to participate in co-investment opportunities alongside the Fund, allocation priority, notification procedures, and minimum co-investment allocation amounts;
>
> \(iii\) **Excuse and opt-out rights**, including the right of certain limited partners to be excused from, or to opt out of, specific Fund investments on the basis of legal, regulatory, tax, or policy considerations applicable to such limited partner;
>
> \(iv\) **Reporting enhancements**, including supplemental reporting obligations of the GP, enhanced transparency regarding portfolio company performance, ESG-related reporting, and diversity and inclusion metrics;
>
> \(v\) **FOIA and public records protections**, particularly relevant to Cascadia PERS, including provisions addressing the treatment of Fund information in the event of a public records request, prior notice and consultation obligations of the limited partner, and the GP\'s right to seek protective relief;
>
> \(vi\) **Advisory committee seats**, including the right of certain Anchor LPs to designate a representative to serve on the Fund\'s advisory committee, as well as related governance provisions;
>
> \(vii\) **Key-person event notifications**, including enhanced notification rights in the event of a key-person event under the LPA, consultation rights, and accelerated information delivery timelines;
>
> \(viii\) **Transfer rights**, including any enhanced or modified transfer, assignment, or secondary sale rights negotiated with an Anchor LP, subject to the transfer restrictions and consent provisions of the LPA;
>
> \(ix\) **Fee netting provisions**, addressing the application and allocation of transaction fees, monitoring fees, break-up fees, and other fees received by the GP or its affiliates in connection with Fund investments;
>
> \(x\) **Information rights**, including the right to receive additional information from the GP regarding the Fund\'s investments, operations, or financial condition, beyond the standard reporting obligations set forth in the LPA; and
>
> \(xi\) **Other customary terms**, including provisions relating to indemnification, representations and warranties, sovereign immunity (if applicable), governing law modifications, and such other terms as may be customary for side letters in institutional venture capital fund formations.

The Firm will work closely with the GP to tailor each Side Letter to the specific requirements and negotiation objectives of each Anchor LP, while maintaining consistency across the side letter package and managing the GP\'s exposure under the MFN framework.

**(c) Most Favored Nation Election Framework**

Calderwood & Harkness will structure and document a comprehensive most favored nation election framework (the \"MFN Framework\") applicable to qualifying limited partners of the Fund. The MFN Framework will include the following components:

> \(i\) **MFN Eligibility Threshold.** The Firm will advise on and document the MFN eligibility threshold, which the GP has preliminarily determined shall be set at capital commitments of Twenty-Five Million Dollars (\$25,000,000) or greater. Limited partners whose capital commitments equal or exceed this threshold (each, an \"Eligible LP\") will be entitled to elect certain rights and benefits granted in Side Letters to other limited partners of the Fund, subject to the exclusions described below.
>
> \(ii\) **MFN Election Procedures Letter and Election Form.** The Firm will draft a template MFN election procedures letter (the \"MFN Procedures Letter\") to be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP, together with a standardized MFN election form (the \"MFN Election Form\") to be completed and returned by any Eligible LP wishing to make an MFN election. The MFN Procedures Letter will set forth the procedures, timing, and conditions applicable to MFN elections, including the process for the GP\'s review and confirmation of elected provisions.
>
> \(iii\) **Excluded Provisions.** The Firm will define and categorize certain provisions that will not be available for election under the MFN Framework (collectively, \"Excluded Provisions\"). Excluded Provisions are expected to include, without limitation: (A) provisions granted to a limited partner in order to satisfy specific legal, regulatory, or tax requirements applicable to such limited partner by reason of its status, jurisdiction, or governing law; (B) advisory committee seats and related governance rights; (C) portfolio company board observer rights; and (D) any other terms that the GP reasonably determines are specific to the legal, regulatory, or organizational status of a particular limited partner and are not appropriate for general election by other limited partners.
>
> \(iv\) **Redacted MFN Side Letter Compilation.** The Firm will prepare a redacted compilation of the Side Letters entered into by the Fund (the \"MFN Side Letter Compilation\"), from which the identities of the limited partners party thereto and all Excluded Provisions shall be redacted. The MFN Side Letter Compilation will be delivered by the GP to each Eligible LP within fifteen (15) business days following the final closing of the Fund (the \"Final Close\"), which is currently targeted to occur on or before July 15, 2026.
>
> \(v\) **MFN Election Period.** Following delivery of the MFN Side Letter Compilation, each Eligible LP shall have a period of thirty (30) calendar days (the \"MFN Election Period\") in which to review the MFN Side Letter Compilation and submit a completed MFN Election Form to the GP indicating which provisions, if any, such Eligible LP elects to receive. The Firm will advise the GP on the review, confirmation, and administration of MFN elections following the close of the MFN Election Period.

**(d) Coordination with Counterparty Counsel**

Calderwood & Harkness will serve as lead counsel to the GP in all negotiations with the Anchor LPs and will coordinate directly with the legal counsel representing each of the Anchor LPs during the negotiation period. The Firm understands that the following law firms will serve as counterparty counsel:

> \(i\) **Whitfield & Gage LLP** (Portland, Oregon), with Sandra Okafor as lead partner, serving as counsel to Cascadia Public Employees\' Retirement System;
>
> \(ii\) **Hollander McKee & Stone LLP** (Boston, Massachusetts), with David Tannenbaum as lead partner, serving as counsel to Northstar Endowment Partners LLC; and
>
> \(iii\) **Prescott & Langley LLP** (Chicago, Illinois), with Angela Ferris as lead partner, serving as counsel to Brindoval Family Office Holdings LP.

The Firm will coordinate the distribution of initial Side Letter drafts to each counterparty counsel, manage the negotiation process, track open issues, and seek to resolve negotiation points in a manner consistent with the GP\'s objectives and the Fund\'s overall commercial terms. The Firm will also facilitate, as appropriate, the scheduling and conduct of negotiation calls between the parties and their respective counsel.

**(e) Internal Analyses and Negotiation Support**

In support of the Side Letter negotiations and the MFN Framework, Calderwood & Harkness will prepare the following internal analyses and work product for the GP\'s use:

> \(i\) **Redline Comparison Chart.** A comprehensive redline comparison chart setting forth, on a term-by-term and LP-by-LP basis, the specific provisions granted in each Side Letter, highlighting differences among the Anchor LP Side Letters and identifying areas of potential MFN exposure.
>
> \(ii\) **MFN Exposure Analysis.** An analysis of the GP\'s exposure under the MFN Framework resulting from the provisions included in the Anchor LP Side Letters, including an assessment of the likelihood and potential impact of Eligible LP elections with respect to specific provisions, and recommendations for mitigating MFN risk through the designation of Excluded Provisions or the structuring of Side Letter terms.
>
> \(iii\) **Negotiation Issues Tracker.** A running issues tracker to be maintained throughout the negotiation period, cataloging open negotiation points, counterparty positions, the GP\'s responses, and the resolution status of each issue.

These materials will be prepared for the GP\'s internal use and will be subject to the attorney-client privilege and work product protections, as applicable.

**(f) Closing Checklist --- First Close Deliverables**

Calderwood & Harkness will prepare a closing checklist identifying all deliverables and conditions related to Side Letter execution that must be completed in connection with the First Close, including the execution and delivery of each Anchor LP Side Letter, the GP\'s execution of any related certificates, confirmations, or ancillary documents, and the distribution of any required notices or disclosures to the Anchor LPs or other limited partners of the Fund.

**[3. Matters Outside the Scope of Engagement]{.underline}**

The GP and the Firm acknowledge and agree that the following matters are expressly outside the scope of this engagement and are not included in the services to be provided by Calderwood & Harkness hereunder:

> \(a\) The drafting, negotiation, or review of the LPA itself, or any amendments or restatements thereto;
>
> \(b\) The preparation, drafting, or review of the Fund\'s private placement memorandum, confidential offering memorandum, subscription agreements, investor questionnaires, or other offering or subscription documents;
>
> \(c\) Any filings with, or submissions to, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the \"SEC\") or any state securities regulator, including Form D filings, Form ADV amendments, or blue sky filings;
>
> \(d\) Tax structuring, tax planning, or the rendering of any tax opinion or tax advice in connection with the Fund, the GP, or any limited partner, including any analysis under Subchapter K of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended, or any state or local tax regime;
>
> \(e\) Analysis of compliance with the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or the plan asset regulations thereunder, except to the extent of any ERISA-related representations, warranties, or acknowledgments that may be included in the Side Letters as a matter of standard drafting practice;
>
> \(f\) Any representation of, or advice to, the GP or the Fund in connection with the Fund\'s placement agent arrangements with Greystone Capital Advisors LLC, including the negotiation, review, or interpretation of any placement agent agreement; and
>
> \(g\) Any litigation, arbitration, mediation, or other dispute resolution proceeding, whether arising out of or related to the Side Letters, the LPA, the Fund, or otherwise.

In the event that the GP wishes to expand the scope of Calderwood & Harkness\'s representation to include any of the foregoing matters or any other matter not described in Section 2 above, such expansion of scope shall be confirmed in a separate engagement letter or in a written amendment to this Engagement Letter, setting forth the additional scope, engagement team, fee arrangements, and other applicable terms.

**[4. Engagement Team]{.underline}**

The following attorneys will comprise the Calderwood & Harkness engagement team for this matter:

  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Team Member**     **Role**              **Practice Group**         **Primary Responsibilities**
  ------------------- --------------------- -------------------------- ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Nicholas Stern      Responsible Partner   Funds & Asset Management   Primary point of contact for strategic matters and client relationship management; overall supervision of the engagement; participation in key negotiation sessions with counterparty counsel

  Graham Sutherland   Billing Partner       Funds & Asset Management   Billing administration and fee monitoring; periodic review of engagement progress and work product

  Owen Fischer        Lead Associate        Funds & Asset Management   Day-to-day management of the engagement; principal drafter of all Side Letters, MFN Framework documents, and internal analyses; primary liaison with counterparty counsel; coordination of negotiation schedules and issue resolution

  Stephen Adler       Working Associate     Funds & Asset Management   Supporting drafting and research; preparation of the MFN exposure analysis, redline comparison charts, and negotiation issues tracker; assistance with closing checklist preparation
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The GP\'s primary day-to-day contact for the engagement will be Owen Fischer. For strategic and client relationship matters, the GP may contact Nicholas Stern directly. The Firm may, from time to time, assign additional attorneys or professional staff to the engagement as circumstances warrant, and will inform the GP of any material changes to the composition of the engagement team.

**[5. Fees and Billing]{.underline}**

**(a) Billing Rates**

Services rendered in connection with this engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at the Firm\'s standard 2025 billing rates, which are as follows:

  -----------------------------------------------------------------------
  **Timekeeper**          **Rate Category**       **Hourly Rate**
  ----------------------- ----------------------- -----------------------
  Nicholas Stern          Partner                 \$1,450

  Graham Sutherland       Partner                 \$1,450

  Senior Associates       Senior Associate        \$950

  Owen Fischer            Associate               \$750

  Stephen Adler           Associate               \$750
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

The foregoing billing rates are the Firm\'s standard rates in effect as of January 1, 2025. Billing rates are subject to annual adjustment, which typically takes effect on January 1 of each calendar year. The Firm will notify the GP in advance of any changes to the billing rates applicable to this engagement. In the event that senior associates are assigned to the engagement in a supporting capacity, the applicable senior associate rate set forth above will apply.

**(b) Fee Estimate**

Based on the scope of services described in Section 2 above, and on the Firm\'s experience with comparable side letter programs for venture capital and private equity fund formations, Calderwood & Harkness estimates that total professional fees for the engagement will be in the range of **\$185,000 to \$225,000**. This estimate is based on an anticipated total of approximately **170 to 210 hours** of attorney time across the engagement team, and assumes a negotiation process involving a customary number of drafting rounds and negotiation sessions with each of the three Anchor LPs.

The foregoing estimate is provided solely for the GP\'s budgeting and planning purposes and **does not constitute a cap on fees or a fixed fee arrangement**. Actual fees may be higher or lower than the estimate depending on a number of factors, including the complexity and duration of negotiations with each Anchor LP, the number and scope of negotiation rounds, the extent of LP-specific requirements or unusual provisions, and the responsiveness of counterparty counsel. The Firm will provide the GP with monthly updates on accrued fees relative to the estimate and will promptly notify the GP if the Firm believes that fees are likely to materially exceed the estimated range.

**(c) Disbursements and Expenses**

19: **[I. Purpose of Memorandum]{.underline}**
20: 
21: This memorandum summarizes the facts received from Solara Digital Infrastructure LP\'s (\"Solara\" or the \"Client\") in-house legal and tax teams during two initial intake calls conducted on May 22, 2025, and May 26, 2025, in advance of the formal matter opening on May 27, 2025. The May 22 call was approximately ninety minutes in duration and focused primarily on the existing fund structure and business rationale for the proposed reorganization. The May 26 call was approximately two hours in duration and covered the proposed multi-step transaction, the representative portfolio company holdings, the aggregate financial parameters of the reorganization, and outstanding data needs. Both calls were conducted by videoconference, with Robert Jansen and Garrett Simmons participating from Calderwood & Harkness\'s Washington, D.C. and New York offices, respectively.

**[I. Purpose of Memorandum]{.underline}**

This memorandum summarizes the facts received from Solara Digital Infrastructure LP\'s (\"Solara\" or the \"Client\") in-house legal and tax teams during two initial intake calls conducted on May 22, 2025, and May 26, 2025, in advance of the formal matter opening on May 27, 2025. **[VI. GENERAL PARTNER AND MANAGEMENT COMPANY --- STRUCTURAL CONSIDERATIONS]{.underline}**

**[A. Separation of GP and Management Company]{.underline}**

We recommend that the General Partner entity (CLSO GP I, LLC) and the Management Company entity (CLSO Management I, LLC) be organized as **separate legal entities**, each formed as a Delaware limited liability company. The separation of the GP and Management Company functions into distinct entities is market-standard for institutional-grade fund structures and serves several important purposes:

**Liability Isolation.** The General Partner bears unlimited liability for the obligations of the Fund as a matter of Delaware partnership law. By separating the General Partner from the Management Company, the employment-related and operational liabilities of the Management Company (including employee claims, lease obligations, vendor contracts, and regulatory obligations) are contained within the Management Company and do not directly expose the General Partner to additional liability beyond its partnership obligations. Conversely, the General Partner\'s partnership liabilities (including its obligations under the clawback provision and its joint and several liability among the principals) are contained within the GP entity and do not directly expose the Management Company\'s assets.

**Economic Clarity.** The economic flows to the two entities are distinct: carried interest flows through the General Partner, while management fee revenue flows to the Management Company. This separation provides clear economic attribution for tax, accounting, and regulatory purposes, and simplifies the analysis of conflicts of interest and fee-offset calculations.

**Market Standard.** The vast majority of institutional-quality private investment funds with which we are familiar --- including virtually all funds at or above the \$500 million target size --- employ separate GP and Management Company entities. Institutional limited partners and their investment consultants expect and are comfortable with this structure.

Both entities will be formed as Delaware LLCs. The LLC operating agreements for the GP (the \"GP LLC Agreement\") and the Management Company (the \"Management Company LLC Agreement\") will be prepared as separate workstreams, with target first drafts to be circulated to the principals on May 31, 2026, concurrent with the first draft of the LPA.

**[B. GP Commitment Mechanics]{.underline}**

The General Partner will make a commitment to the Fund as a limited partner, equal to a minimum of **two percent (2%) of aggregate commitments**. At the target fund size of \$750 million, this equates to a GP commitment of **\$15,000,000**. This commitment level is consistent with market expectations for first-time funds and demonstrates meaningful alignment of interest between the Sponsor\'s principals and the Fund\'s limited partners.

The source of the GP commitment will be personal capital from the Fund\'s principals --- Dr. Yeung, Ms. Dasgupta, and Mr. Whitford --- and/or capital from Cobalt Ventures LP. The proportions in which the GP commitment is funded by each principal (and by Cobalt Ventures LP, if applicable) will be determined by the principals in consultation with their personal tax and financial advisors, and will be documented in the GP LLC Agreement and the Fund\'s subscription documents.

The GP commitment will be invested on the **same terms as LP commitments**: drawn pro rata with LP capital calls, returned pro rata with distributions, and subject to the same distribution waterfall (including the preferred return and carried interest mechanics). The GP commitment will **not be subject to the management fee**, which is consistent with market practice (the management fee compensates the Management Company for services provided to the Fund, and charging a management fee on the GP\'s own capital would be economically circular).

The GP commitment will be reflected in the Fund\'s capital accounts and will participate in gains and losses on the same basis as LP capital. For purposes of calculating the 25% plan asset threshold under ERISA (discussed in Section VII.A), the GP commitment is generally excluded from the denominator, as the GP\'s interest is not a \"class of equity interests\" within the meaning of DOL Reg. §2510.3-101.

**[C. Key Person Provisions]{.underline}**

The LPA will designate **Dr. Marcus Yeung** and **Priya Dasgupta** as the Fund\'s \"Key Persons.\" The Key Person provision is a critical governance mechanism that protects limited partners\' investment by ensuring that the principals whose expertise and judgment are central to the Fund\'s investment strategy remain actively engaged in the Fund\'s operations throughout the investment period.

**Trigger.** The Key Person event will be triggered if either Key Person ceases to devote **substantially all** of his or her business time to the affairs of the Fund. The \"substantially all\" standard is the market-standard formulation and is generally understood to mean that the Key Person\'s primary professional activity is the management of the Fund and the performance of the Management Company\'s obligations thereunder, with limited exceptions for personal investments, charitable activities, and industry board memberships that do not materially interfere with the Key Person\'s responsibilities to the Fund.

**Consequence.** Upon the occurrence of a Key Person event, the **investment period will be suspended** --- the General Partner will not be permitted to make new investments or draw down additional capital for new investments (although commitments for follow-on investments in existing portfolio companies and investments for which binding commitments have been made prior to the Key Person event will generally be permitted). The investment period suspension will continue until the limited partners vote, by a specified majority (to be determined in the LPA, typically a majority-in-interest of limited partners excluding the GP\'s interest), to either (a) **reinstate** the investment period (with or without the designation of a replacement Key Person) or (b) **terminate** the investment period.

**Structural Implication.** The GP LLC Agreement should contain provisions requiring each Key Person to devote substantially all of his or her business time to the affairs of the Fund and the Management Company, and restricting each Key Person\'s outside activities during the Fund\'s term. These provisions should be consistent with the Key Person obligations set forth in the LPA, and should provide for appropriate consequences (including potential forfeiture or reduction of carried interest) in the event of a Key Person\'s breach of the devotion-of-time obligation. The specific terms of the Key Person restrictions in the GP LLC Agreement will be coordinated with the LPA provisions and are part of the GP LLC Agreement drafting workstream.

**[VII. ERISA AND VCOC CONSIDERATIONS]{.underline}**

**[A. Plan Asset Analysis]{.underline}**

The Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), imposes fiduciary obligations on persons who manage the assets of employee benefit plans. Under regulations promulgated by the Department of Labor (\"DOL\"), specifically DOL Reg. §2510.3-101 (as modified by Section 3(42) of ERISA), if **\"benefit plan investors\"** hold twenty-five percent (25%) or more of any class of equity interests in the Fund (excluding interests held by the General Partner, the Management Company, and their affiliates), the Fund\'s underlying assets will be treated as **\"plan assets\"** for purposes of ERISA. If the Fund\'s assets are treated as plan assets, the General Partner and the Management Company will be subject to ERISA\'s fiduciary duties (including the duties of prudence and loyalty) and prohibited transaction rules, which impose significant operational constraints and potential personal liability on the Fund\'s managers.

\"Benefit plan investors\" is defined broadly to include employee benefit plans subject to ERISA, plans subject to Section 4975 of the Internal Revenue Code (including individual retirement accounts), and entities whose underlying assets include plan assets by reason of a plan\'s investment in such entity. The definition may also encompass certain governmental plans and church plans, depending on the specific regulatory analysis.

**Application to the Fund\'s Anticipated Investor Base.** The anticipated investor base includes:

> • **Ironwood PERS** --- a state government pension fund organized under Oregon law. Governmental plans are generally not subject to ERISA (they are excluded from ERISA\'s coverage under ERISA §4(b)(1)). However, governmental plan assets may be counted as \"benefit plan investor\" assets for purposes of the 25% threshold under certain interpretations of DOL Reg. §2510.3-101. The regulatory analysis is not entirely settled on this point, and conservative fund sponsors typically count governmental plan assets in the 25% calculation.
>
> • **Northgate Endowment Management** --- a university endowment. Whether Northgate constitutes a \"benefit plan investor\" depends on its specific legal structure. If the endowment is a commingled investment vehicle that includes assets of employee benefit plans (such as the university\'s defined benefit pension plan or defined contribution plan), it may be treated as a benefit plan investor to the extent that plan assets are invested in the endowment. Northgate\'s specific structure should be confirmed during the subscription process.

**Monitoring.** We recommend that the Fund monitor the 25% benefit plan investor threshold at each closing and on an ongoing basis. The subscription agreement and investor questionnaire should require each limited partner to disclose its status as a benefit plan investor (or the percentage of its assets that constitute plan assets) and to notify the Fund of any change in status. Halcyon Fund Services should be engaged to track the 25% threshold as part of its fund administration responsibilities.

**[B. VCOC Election]{.underline}**

To avoid plan asset treatment even if benefit plan investors hold 25% or more of the Fund\'s equity interests, the Fund will elect to qualify as a **\"venture capital operating company\" (VCOC)** under DOL Reg. §2510.3-101(d). The VCOC exception provides that the assets of a VCOC are not treated as plan assets for purposes of ERISA, regardless of the level of benefit plan investor participation.

**VCOC Requirements.** To qualify as a VCOC, the Fund must satisfy two requirements:

> \(i\) **Investment Test.** At least fifty percent (50%) of the Fund\'s assets (valued at cost, at the time of each investment and on the last day of each annual valuation period thereafter) must be invested in **\"venture capital investments.\"** A \"venture capital investment\" is defined as an investment in an operating company with respect to which the Fund obtains **\"management rights\"** --- contractual rights that give the Fund the right to substantially participate in or substantially influence the management of the operating company. Management rights may take the form of board seats, board observer rights, contractual consultation rights, veto rights over specified management decisions, or other governance provisions.
>
> \(ii\) **Exercise Test.** The Fund must **actually exercise** management rights with respect to at least one portfolio company during each annual valuation period. Passive governance rights are not sufficient --- the Fund must affirmatively participate in or influence the management of at least one portfolio company.

**Application to CLSO Fund I.** The Fund\'s investment strategy is well-suited for VCOC qualification. The Fund targets board seats or contractual governance rights in one hundred percent (100%) of its portfolio companies. The Fund\'s check sizes (\$30 million to \$100 million) and focus on clinical-stage therapeutics, medical devices, and platform biotechnology companies ensure that the Fund\'s portfolio companies are \"operating companies\" within the meaning of the regulation. Accordingly, we expect the Fund to satisfy the 50% investment test with substantial margin, and to readily satisfy the exercise test through active board participation and governance involvement with portfolio companies.

**LPA Provisions.** The LPA should include VCOC-related covenants, including:

> • An obligation of the General Partner to use commercially reasonable efforts to **maintain VCOC status** throughout the Fund\'s term.
>
> • A right (but not obligation) of the General Partner to **refuse subscriptions** from, or limit transfers by, investors whose participation would jeopardize the Fund\'s VCOC qualification (for example, by causing the Fund\'s benefit plan investor percentage to exceed a level at which VCOC qualification becomes critical).
>
> • An obligation of the General Partner to obtain management rights in connection with each investment and to exercise management rights as required to satisfy the VCOC exercise test.

**VCOC Testing.** Ongoing VCOC compliance testing --- including annual verification of the 50% investment test and documentation of the exercise of management rights --- will be coordinated with **Halcyon Fund Services, Inc.** (Thomas Varga, Director -- Private Equity Administration) as part of the Fund\'s ongoing fund administration. Halcyon will maintain records of the cost basis of each investment, the management rights obtained in connection with each investment, and evidence ofn and are tracked on the Closing Checklist (a separate deliverable). We recommend that account opening procedures be initiated in **October 2026** to ensure that all accounts are operational in advance of the target first close on November 15, 2026.

The Fund\'s banking arrangements should comply with any applicable custody rule requirements under the Advisers Act (if Cobalt becomes a registered investment adviser) and should be coordinated with Halcyon Fund Services to ensure seamless integration with the fund administrator\'s capital call and distribution processing systems.

**[XI. GOVERNANCE STRUCTURE --- LP ADVISORY COMMITTEE]{.underline}**

The LPA will establish an **LP Advisory Committee (LPAC)** to provide a forum for consultation between the General Partner and the limited partners on matters involving potential conflicts of interest, valuation issues, and other governance matters specified in the LPA.

**Composition.** The LPAC will consist of a minimum of **three (3)** and a maximum of **seven (7)** members, each of whom must be a representative of a limited partner in the Fund. Members will be selected by the General Partner from among the Fund\'s limited partners, with priority given to the largest limited partners and anchor investors. If non-U.S. commitments reach or exceed **\$50,000,000**, at least one LPAC member must be a representative of a non-U.S. limited partner, ensuring that the perspectives of non-U.S. investors are represented in the governance process.

**Functions.** The LPAC\'s functions, as specified in the LPA, will include:

> • **Consent to conflicts of interest.** The LPAC will be authorized to consent, on behalf of the limited partners, to transactions or arrangements that involve actual or potential conflicts of interest between the General Partner (or its affiliates) and the Fund, including co-investment allocations, cross-fund transactions, and related-party arrangements.
>
> • **Review of GP valuations.** The LPAC will review and provide input on the General Partner\'s valuations of portfolio company investments, particularly in connection with quarterly NAV calculations and the annual audit process.
>
> • **Approval of second fund extension.** While the General Partner may extend the Fund\'s term by one year at its discretion (from the initial ten-year term ending May 15, 2037 to May 15, 2038), the second one-year extension (from May 15, 2038 to May 15, 2039) requires the **consent of the LPAC**.
>
> • **Other matters.** The LPAC may be consulted on other matters specified in the LPA, including GP removal for cause, amendments to the LPA, and the formation of AIVs involving potential conflicts of interest.

**Anticipated Initial Members.** Based on the current investor pipeline, the anticipated initial LPAC members will include representatives of the Fund\'s anchor investors. **Ironwood PERS has specifically requested an advisory committee seat**, which we recommend granting given the size of Ironwood PERS\'s anticipated commitment (\$100 million) and its status as the Fund\'s largest expected limited partner. Representatives of Northgate and Pinnacle may also be invited to serve on the LPAC, depending on the final LPAC composition.

**LPAC Procedures.** The LPAC is an advisory body and does not have the authority to bind the Fund or the General Partner except as specifically provided in the LPA. LPAC members serve in their capacity as limited partners and do not owe fiduciary duties to the Fund or to other limited partners by virtue of their LPAC service. The LPA will include customary protections for LPAC members, including indemnification for actions taken in good faith in their LPAC capacity and release from liability for LPAC-approved transactions.

**[XIII. CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION]{.underline}**

Based on the analysis set forth in this memorandum, we recommend the following fund structure for Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I:

**Core Structure:**

> • **Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP** --- a single-tier Delaware limited partnership serving as the primary fund vehicle.
>
> • **Cobalt Life Sciences GP I, LLC** --- a Delaware LLC serving as the General Partner, managed by Dr. Marcus Yeung and Priya Dasgupta, holding the carried interest entitlement (allocated Dr. Yeung 55%, Ms. Dasgupta 35%, Mr. Whitford 10%).
>
> • **Cobalt Life Sciences Management I, LLC** --- a Delaware LLC serving as the Management Company, employing the Fund\'s investment professionals and receiving the management fee.

**Ancillary Structures:**

> • **AIV Provisions** --- to be included in the LPA as a standard feature, authorizing the General Partner to form deal-specific or investor-specific alternative investment vehicles as needed to address tax, legal, regulatory, or operational requirements.
>
> • **blocker Corporation** --- Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I (Blocker), Inc., a Delaware C-corporation, to be formed as needed based on confirmed investor participation requiring blocker access (Pinnacle Insurance Group and potentially Northgate Endowment Management are likely initial users).
>
> • **Parallel Fund Enabling Provisions** --- to be included in the LPA, authorizing the General Partner to form a parallel fund without LP consent if non-U.S. investor demand reaches or exceeds \$50 million.
>
> • **Feeder Fund(s)** --- reserved as a future option, not currently planned. May be formed if fundraising dynamics warrant aggregation of smaller commitments.

**Structures Not Recommended at This Time:**

> • **Master-Feeder Architecture** --- not recommended due to disproportionate cost and complexity relative to the predominantly U.S. domestic institutional investor base.
>
> • **Standalone Feeder Funds** --- not recommended for initial formation; reserved as a future option.

These structural recommendations remain available for reassessment if fundraising dynamics, investor demands, or regulatory developments change materially. The recommended structure provides a robust, institutional-quality architecture that is consistent with market practice for first-time opportunistic life-sciences funds at the \$750 million scale, while preserving maximum flexibility to accommodate the diverse requirements of the Fund\'s anticipated investor base.

The Co-Investment Allocation Agreement governs the allocation mechanics and ensures parallel treatment of Fund IV and the Vehicle throughout the life of the investment.

The Partnership is not authorized to engage in any business or activity other than the foregoing, and the General Partner is not authorized to cause the Partnership to make any investment other than the Cascadia co-investment without the prior written consent of the Limited Partner.
**[IV. Governance and Decision-Making Authority]{.underline}**
**[A. General Partner Authority (§3.01 of LP Agreement)]{.underline}**

Pursuant to Section 3.01 of the LP Agreement, the General Partner has exclusive authority to manage and control the business and affairs of the Partnership. This broad grant of authority is consistent with the default rules under DRULPA and with customary market practice for sponsor-led co-investment vehicles. Specifically, the General Partner\'s authority includes, without limitation, the following:

> \(a\) making, monitoring, and disposing of the Partnership\'s investment in Cascadia, including all decisions relating to the acquisition, post-closing management, restructuring, refinancing, and ultimate disposition of the investment;
> \(b\) issuing capital calls to the partners and managing capital contributions in accordance with the terms of the LP Agreement;
> \(c\) making distributions to the partners in accordance with the distribution waterfall set forth in Section 6.01 of the LP Agreement;

> \(d\) executing transaction documents on behalf of the Partnership, including the Equity Purchase Agreement, ancillary acquisition agreements, financing agreements, and all other instruments and documents necessary or desirable in connection with the Cascadia acquisition;

> \(e\) engaging service providers on behalf of the Partnership, including fund administrators, independent auditors, tax preparers, legal counsel, valuation consultants, and any other advisors or consultants deemed necessary or appropriate by the General Partner;
> \(f\) incurring and paying expenses on behalf of the Partnership, including organizational expenses, ongoing operating expenses, and transaction-related expenses;

> \(g\) taking all actions necessary or desirable in connection with the Cascadia acquisition, including the negotiation and execution of the Equity Purchase Agreement, the stockholders\' agreement, the management services agreement, and all related transaction documents; and
> \(h\) generally taking all actions that the General Partner deems necessary or appropriate to carry out the purposes of the Partnership and to protect the Partnership\'s investment.

The General Partner acts through its managers --- David R. Hargreaves (Managing Partner), Lillian Fong (Partner, Portfolio), and Graham Whitfield (Partner, Operations) --- or such other authorized officers or representatives as the managers may designate from time to time in accordance with the GP\'s operating agreement. Decisions of the General Partner are made by majority vote of the managers, except as otherwise provided in the GP\'s operating agreement.
**[B. Limitations on GP Authority]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding the broad grant of authority to the General Partner described above, the LP Agreement imposes certain limitations on the General Partner\'s authority. Specifically, the General Partner may not take any of the following actions without the prior written consent of the Limited Partner (Ironside):
> \(a\) amend, modify, or waive any provision of the LP Agreement or the Side Letter;
> \(b\) admit additional limited partners to the Partnership;
> \(c\) increase the aggregate capital commitments of the Partnership beyond \$300,000,000;
> \(d\) merge, consolidate, or convert the Partnership into another entity or form of organization;

> \(e\) voluntarily file for bankruptcy, make an assignment for the benefit of creditors, or consent to the appointment of a receiver or trustee for the Partnership or any substantial part of its assets;

> \(f\) enter into any related-party transaction (including any transaction with the General Partner, its affiliates, Fund IV, or their respective principals, officers, or employees) that is not expressly contemplated by the LP Agreement or the Co-Investment Allocation Agreement; and
> \(g\) extend the investment period or term of the Partnership beyond the limits set forth in the LP Agreement.

11: > **Re: Engagement of Calderwood & Harkness LLP --- GP Advisory Regarding Key-Person Event, Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd.**
12: >
13: > **Matter No.: 1024-00002**
14: 
15: Dear Ms. Sato:
16: 
17: **[1. Introduction and Engagement Overview]{.underline}**
18: 
19: Calderwood & Harkness LLP (\"C&H\" or the \"Firm\") is pleased to confirm its engagement by Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\"), a Delaware limited liability company (EIN: 82-4917653), in its capacity as the General Partner of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Fund\"), a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership registered with the Cayman Islands Registrar of Exempted Limited Partnerships under Registration No. ELP-87234. This engagement letter sets forth the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to DCM and the Fund in connection with the Key Person Event (as defined below) and related governance matters described herein.
20: 
21: The Fund is governed by its Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement dated March 15, 2017 (as amended from time to time, the \"A&R LPA\"), which is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware. The A&R LPA provides for certain key-person protections in favor of the Fund\'s limited partners, as more fully described in Section 3 below.
22: 
23: This engagement is precipitated by the medical incapacitation of Marcus J. Whitmore, Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and Managing Member (holding a ninety percent (90%) membership interest) of DCM. Mr. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024, and has been incapacitated since that date. Mr. Whitmore is the sole individual designated as a \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. As a result of Mr. Whitmore\'s continued incapacitation for a period exceeding seven consecutive calendar days from the date of the medical event, a Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA is deemed to have been triggered as of June 10, 2024 (the \"Key Person Event\"). The occurrence of the Key Person Event gives rise to a number of contractual obligations, rights, and remedies under the A&R LPA that require prompt legal attention and careful navigation by DCM in its capacity as General Partner of the Fund.
24: 
25: This engagement letter confirms the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to the Clients (as defined below) in connection with the Key Person Event, including, without limitation, analysis of the A&R LPA\'s key-person provisions, preparation of required limited partner notifications, development of a successor governance framework, drafting of LPA amendments, and coordination of the limited partner consent solicitation process.
26: 
27: **[2. Clients]{.underline}**
28: 
29: For purposes of this engagement, C&H\'s clients shall consist of both DCM and DARF (collectively, the \"Clients\").
30: 
31: DCM\'s principal office is located at 680 Lexington Avenue, 31st Floor, New York, NY 10022. DCM\'s registered agent for service of process in the State of Delaware is Capitol Registered Agents, Inc., located at 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.
32: 
33: DARF\'s registered office is located at 4th Floor, Harbour Place, 103 South Church Street, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1104, Cayman Islands. DARF\'s registered agent in the Cayman Islands is Archipelago Corporate Services Ltd., P.O. Box 2681, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1111, Cayman Islands.
34: 
35: It is important that the scope of this representation be clearly understood. C&H represents DCM and DARF as described herein and does not represent any individual limited partner of the Fund, the Investor Advisory Committee of the Fund (the \"IAC\"), or any individual member or officer of DCM in his or her personal capacity. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, C&H does not represent Mr. Whitmore individually, nor does C&H represent any member of the IAC in his, her, or its individual or fiduciary capacity. Each such person and entity is encouraged to seek independent legal counsel to the extent such person or entity deems it necessary or appropriate.
36: 
37: Elaine R. Sato, in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding a ten percent (10%) membership interest) of DCM, will serve as the primary point of contact for the Clients in connection with this engagement. All communications from C&H regarding this engagement will be directed to Ms. Sato unless otherwise instructed in writing by Ms. Sato. C&H will take direction from Ms. Sato with respect to all matters within the scope of this engagement, subject to the Firm\'s professional obligations.
38: 
39: **[3. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**
40: 
41: C&H\'s representation of the Clients will encompass the following workstreams in connection with the Key Person Event triggered under Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA. Each workstream is described in further detail below.
42: 
43: **3.1 Key-Person Event Analysis**
44: 
45: C&H will undertake a comprehensive analysis of the mechanics and consequences of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, including the following:
46: 
47: > \(a\) **Section 8.04(a) --- Definition of \"Key Person.\"** C&H will confirm the scope of the \"Key Person\" designation under the A&R LPA, which identifies Marcus J. Whitmore as the sole designated Key Person. C&H will analyze the definition for purposes of establishing the factual predicate for the Key Person Event and for advising on the requirements for designating any Successor Key Person(s) (as described in Section 3.3 below).
48: >
49: > \(b\) **Section 8.04(b) --- Trigger Conditions.** C&H will analyze the trigger conditions set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA in light of the facts surrounding Mr. Whitmore\'s incapacitation. Specifically, Section 8.04(b) provides that a Key Person Event is deemed to occur when the Key Person becomes unable, whether by reason of death, disability, incapacity, departure, or otherwise, to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. Based on the information provided to C&H, Mr. Whitmore has been continuously incapacitated since June 3, 2024, and the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold was met as of June 10, 2024. C&H will prepare a memorandum confirming the legal basis for this determination.
50: >
51: > \(c\) **Section 8.04(c) --- Consequences of the Key Person Event.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the full range of consequences triggered by the occurrence of the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, which include the following:
52: >
53: > \(i\) *Immediate Suspension of the Investment Period.* The Investment Period (as defined in Section 1.01 of the A&R LPA) is automatically suspended upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event. During such suspension, the General Partner may not make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Fund, except as provided in clause (ii) below.
54: >
55: > \(ii\) *Follow-On Investment Cap.* Notwithstanding the suspension of the Investment Period, the General Partner retains limited authority to make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not to exceed one percent (1%) of the Fund\'s assets under management as of the date of the Key Person Event. Based on the Fund\'s most recently reported AUM of approximately \$2.87 billion, the follow-on investment cap is \$28.7 million.
56: >
57: > \(iii\) *LP Notification Requirement.* The General Partner is required to provide written notice to all limited partners of the occurrence of the Key Person Event within five (5) business days of the date on which the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred. Given that the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred on June 10, 2024, the contractual deadline for delivery of such notice is June 17, 2024.
58: >
59: > \(iv\) *Commencement of the 90-Calendar-Day Cure Period.* Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, a cure period of ninety (90) calendar days (the \"Cure Period\") commences, during which the General Partner may propose one or more Successor Key Persons for approval by the limited partners. The Cure Period with respect to the current Key Person Event will expire on September 8, 2024.
60: >
61: > \(v\) *LP Consent Threshold.* Approval of any proposed Successor Key Person(s) requires the affirmative written consent of limited partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate capital commitments of all limited partners of the Fund, excluding for this purpose any co-investment by the General Partner. C&H will advise on the calculation of this threshold based on the most current LP commitment schedule maintained by the Fund\'s administrator.
62: >
63: > \(d\) **Consequences of Failure to Cure.** C&H will further analyze the consequences under Section 8.04(d) of the A&R LPA if no cure is achieved within the Cure Period, including the limited partners\' right to elect, by the same 66⅔% consent threshold described above, either (x) to extend the Cure Period for one or more additional periods or (y) to direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund\'s portfolio. C&H will advise the Clients on the mechanics, timing, and fiduciary considerations associated with each of these alternatives.
64: >
65: > \(e\) **Delaware Law Fiduciary Duty Analysis.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the fiduciary duties owed by DCM, as General Partner, to the limited partners of the Fund during the Key Person Event and throughout the consent solicitation process, as a matter of Delaware law. This analysis will address, among other things, the duty of care and the contractual modification of fiduciary duties under the A&R LPA, including the exculpation and indemnification provisions set forth in Article XII thereof.
66: 
67: **3.2 LP Notification**
68: 
69: C&H will draft the formal written notice to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund disclosing the occurrence of the Key Person Event in compliance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA (the \"Key Person Notice\"). The Key Person Notice will describe the factual basis for the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences thereof, the commencement and expected expiration date of the Cure Period, and the process by which the General Partner intends to propose Successor Key Person(s) for approval by the limited partners.
70: 
71: C&H will coordinate with Pinnacle Fund Services (Cayman) Ltd. (the \"Administrator\"), the Fund\'s third-party administrator, regarding the maintenance and accuracy of LP contact information, the appropriate method of delivery (including any notice provisions specified in the A&R LPA or in individual side letters), and the mechanics of distributing the Key Person Notice to all limited partners within the contractual timeframe. C&H will confirm with the Administrator that notice is delivered by a method that satisfies the delivery requirements of Section 15.01 of the A&R LPA.
72: 
73: It is critical that the Key Person Notice be delivered within the five (5) business-day contractual notification deadline, which, as noted above, falls on June 17, 2024. C&H will prioritize this workstream accordingly and will endeavor to deliver a draft of the Key Person Notice to Ms. Sato for review no later than June 13, 2024.
74: 
75: **3.3 Successor Governance Framework**
76: 
77: C&H will advise the Clients regarding the identification and evaluation of proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the development of a recommended successor governance framework for the Fund. This advisory work may encompass the following elements:
78: 
79: > \(a\) **Designation of Successor Key Person(s).** C&H will advise on the criteria and process for designating one or more Successor Key Persons under the A&R LPA, including the qualifications, investment experience, and operational capabilities that limited partners are likely to consider in evaluating any proposed successor. C&H will assist in preparing biographical and professional materials for inclusion in the consent solicitation package.
80: >
81: > \(b\) **Establishment of an Investment Committee.** In the event that the Clients determine that the successor governance framework should include the establishment of a formal Investment Committee or similar collective governance body (in lieu of, or in addition to, a sole Key Person designation), C&H will advise on the structure, composition, authority, and operating procedures of such body, and will prepare the necessary amendments to the A&R LPA to implement such structure.
82: >
83: > \(c\) **Modifications to Key-Person Clause Mechanics.** C&H will advise on potential modifications to the key-person provisions of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, which may include revised replacement periods, modified trigger events (including, for example, a threshold requiring the departure or incapacitation of more than one designated Key Person before a Key Person Event is deemed to occur), and other structural changes to reduce single-person dependency risk.
84: >
85: > \(d\) **Carried Interest Reallocation.** C&H will advise the Clients on the legal and governance considerations associated with any proposed reallocation of carried interest among GP personnel in connection with the transition, including the interplay between the carried interest provisions of the A&R LPA and the operating agreement of DCM.
86: >
87: > \(e\) **Designation of Senior Advisor or Emeritus Role.** To the extent the Clients determine it appropriate, C&H will advise on the creation of a Senior Advisor or emeritus role for Mr. Whitmore, including the scope of any continuing economic interest, advisory responsibilities, and governance rights that may be associated with such role.
88: >
89: > \(f\) **Fiduciary Duty Obligations.** Throughout the development of the successor governance framework, C&H will advise the Clients regarding their fiduciary duty obligations under applicable Delaware law, including the duty to act in good faith and in the best interests of the limited partners in proposing any successor governance arrangements.
90: 
91: **3.4 LPA Amendment Drafting**
92: 
93: C&H will prepare one or more amendments to the A&R LPA (each, an \"LPA Amendment\") to implement the successor governance framework developed pursuant to Section 3.3 above. It is anticipated that the LPA Amendments will include modifications to the following provisions of the A&R LPA, among others:
94: 
95: > \(a\) Section 8.04 (Key Person), to reflect the designation of Successor Key Person(s) and any revised key-person clause mechanics;
96: >
97: > \(b\) Section 9.02 (Investor Advisory Committee), to the extent any changes to the composition, authority, or procedures of the IAC are contemplated in connection with the successor governance framework;
98: >
99: > \(c\) Section 14.01 (Amendments), to the extent any changes to the amendment mechanics are necessary or advisable; and
100: >
101: > \(d\) Related schedules and exhibits, including the schedule of Key Persons attached to the A&R LPA.
102: 
103: All LPA Amendments will be subject to the consent requirements set forth in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, which generally requires the written consent of the General Partner and limited partners holding at least 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding GP co-investment) for amendments to certain specified provisions, including Section 8.04. C&H will advise the Clients regarding the applicable consent thresholds for each proposed amendment.
104: 
105: **3.5 LP Consent Solicitation**
106: 
107: C&H will advise on and coordinate the consent solicitation process necessary to obtain limited partner approval of the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. This workstream will include the following:
108: 
109: > \(a\) **Successor Key Person Proposal Letter.** C&H will draft a detailed letter to all limited partners setting forth the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the rationale for the proposed designation(s), the terms of the proposed successor governance framework, and a summary of the proposed LPA Amendments (the \"Proposal Letter\"). The Proposal Letter will be designed to provide limited partners with all information reasonably necessary to make an informed decision regarding the proposed successor arrangements.
110: >
111: > \(b\) **Form of LP Written Consent.** C&H will prepare a Form of LP Written Consent (the \"Consent Form\") for execution by limited partners approving the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. The Consent Form will be structured to comply with the requirements of Section 14.01 and Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA.
112: >
113: > \(c\) **Coordination of Consent Solicitation Process.** C&H will coordinate the distribution of the Proposal Letter and Consent Form to all forty-seven (47) limited partners, working in conjunction with the Administrator to ensure accurate and timely delivery. C&H will manage the consent solicitation timeline with a view toward obtaining the requisite LP consents prior to the expiration of the Cure Period on September 8, 2024.
114: >
115: > \(d\) **Tabulation and Certification.** C&H will tabulate the LP consents received and prepare a closing certificate confirming that the requisite consent threshold (66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments, excluding GP co-investment) has been satisfied and that the LPA Amendments are effective as of the date specified therein (the \"Closing Certificate\").
116: >
117: > \(e\) **Engagement with IAC Counsel.** C&H will engage with counsel to the Investor Advisory Committee, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, as necessary and appropriate regarding the IAC\'s review of and comments on the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the successor governance framework, and the LPA Amendments. C&H will coordinate with the Clients regarding any modifications to the proposed arrangements that may be requested by the IAC or its counsel.
118: 
119: **[4. Limitations on Scope]{.underline}**
120: 
121: The Clients should be aware of the following limitations on the scope of C&H\'s engagement:
122: 
123: > \(a\) **Cayman Islands Law.** C&H does not provide legal advice regarding the laws of the Cayman Islands. The Clients should consult separately with qualified Cayman Islands counsel regarding any Cayman Islands regulatory, partnership law, or other legal matters that may arise in connection with the Key Person Event or the transactions contemplated by this engagement, including any filings or notifications required under Cayman Islands law in connection with changes to the Fund\'s governance structure.
124: >
125: > \(b\) **Tax Advice.** C&H is not engaged to provide tax advice in connection with this engagement. The Clients should consult their own tax advisors regarding the U.S. federal, state, local, and non-U.S. tax implications of any carried interest reallocation, structural changes to the Fund or DCM, or other transactions contemplated by this engagement.
126: >
127: > \(c\) **Investment Advice.** C&H is not engaged to provide investment advice or to evaluate the investment merits of any portfolio positions held by the Fund. The Clients acknowledge that any decisions regarding the management, disposition, or retention of portfolio positions during the suspension of the Investment Period or otherwise are solely the responsibility of the Clients and their investment professionals.
128: >
129: > \(d\) **Third-Party Service Providers.** C&H does not represent the Fund\'s independent auditor (Graystone & Whitfield LLP), the Fund\'s prime broker (Halcyon Securities International Ltd.), the Administrator, or any other third-party service provider to the Fund or DCM. Each such service provider is represented by its own counsel, and the Clients should not assume that C&H\'s representation extends to any of those parties.
130: >
131: > \(e\) **Litigation and Regulatory Matters.** This engagement does not extend to any litigation, arbitration, regulatory investigation, enforcement action, or other adversarial or contested proceeding, whether existing or threatened, unless separately agreed in writing between C&H and the Clients. In the event any such matter arises during the course of this engagement, C&H will promptly advise the Clients and, if requested, discuss the terms of a separate engagement to address such matter.
132: 
133: **[5. Engagement Team]{.underline}**
134: 
135: C&H has assigned the following professionals to this engagement:
136: 
137:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
138:   **Name**                **Role**                **Title**
139:   ----------------------- ----------------------- -------------------------------------
140:   Graham Sutherland       Responsible Partner     Partner, Funds & Asset Management
141: 
142:   Pamela Cross            Billing Partner         Partner, Funds & Asset Management
143: 
144:   Stephen Adler           Lead Associate          Associate, Funds & Asset Management
145: 
146:   Theresa Kim             Working Associate       Associate, Funds & Asset Management
147:   -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
148: 
149: Graham Sutherland will serve as the responsible partner overseeing all legal advice rendered in connection with this engagement. Mr. Sutherland will be the Clients\' primary legal point of contact for substantive matters, and all material legal memoranda, draft documents, and advice letters will be reviewed and approved by Mr. Sutherland prior to delivery to the Clients.
150: 
151: Pamela Cross will serve as the billing partner responsible for fee arrangements, invoicing, and all financial aspects of the engagement. Any questions regarding billing, fees, or disbursements should be directed to Ms. Cross.
152: 
153: Stephen Adler will serve as the lead associate responsible for the day-to-day execution of the engagement workstreams described in Section 3 above, under the supervision of Mr. Sutherland. Theresa Kim will support Mr. Adler on all workstreams, with particular focus on document drafting and consent solicitation logistics.
154: 
155: C&H may assign additional attorneys, paralegals, or other professionals to this engagement as reasonably necessary to ensure the timely and effective completion of the workstreams described herein. C&H will provide prior notice to Ms. Sato before assigning any additional professionals whose time will be billed to the Clients.
156: 
157: **[6. Fee Arrangement]{.underline}**
158: 
159: **6.1 Hourly Rates**
160: 
161: Services rendered by C&H attorneys in connection with this engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:
162: 
163: > • **Partners:** \$1,650 per hour
164: >
165: > • **Associates:** \$895 per hour
166: 
167: The foregoing rates are effective as of the date of this engagement letter and are subject to annual adjustment in accordance with C&H\'s standard rate-setting process. C&H will provide the Clients with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any rate increase. Paralegal and other support staff time, if any, will be billed at rates communicated to the Clients in advance.
168: 
169: **6.2 Fee Cap**
170: 
171: Total professional fees for the engagement shall not exceed Three Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$385,000) (the \"Fee Cap\") without the prior written consent of the Clients. The Fee Cap encompasses all professional fees of C&H attorneys assigned to this engagement for the workstreams described in Section 3 above. In the event C&H anticipates that total fees may approach or exceed the Fee Cap, C&H will promptly notify the Clients and discuss whether an adjustment to the Fee Cap is warranted. No fees in excess of the Fee Cap will be billed to the Clients absent prior written authorization from Ms. Sato or another authorized representative of DCM. The Fee Cap does not include out-of-pocket disbursements, which are addressed separately in Section 6.3 below.
172: 
173: **6.3 Disbursements and Expenses**
174: 
175: The Clients will reimburse C&H for reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred in connection with this engagement, including, without limitation, costs of document production, photocopying, overnight courier and delivery charges, filing fees, database and research charges, and travel expenses (including airfare, lodging, and ground transportation), if any. All disbursements will be billed at cost, without markup. Disbursements are not subject to the Fee Cap set forth in Section 6.2. C&H will exercise reasonable judgment in incurring disbursements and will obtain the Clients\' prior approval before incurring any single disbursement in excess of Five Thousand Dollars (\$5,000).
176: 
177: **6.4 Billing and Payment**
178: 
179: C&H will issue monthly invoices to DCM at the address set forth in Section 2 above (or to such other address as DCM may designate in writing). Each invoice will include a reasonably detailed description of the services rendered and disbursements incurred during the applicable billing period. Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. C&H reserves the right to suspend the performance of services in the event of non-payment of any invoice for a period exceeding sixty (60) days following the date of such invoice, provided that C&H shall provide at least ten (10) days\' prior written notice to the Clients before exercising such right.
