Mr. Whitmore is the sole individual designated as a \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. As a result of Mr. Whitmore\'s continued incapacitation for a period exceeding seven consecutive calendar days from the date of the medical event, a Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA is deemed to have been triggered as of June 10, 2024 (the \"Key Person Event\"). The occurrence of the Key Person Event gives rise to a number of contractual obligations, rights, and remedies under the A&R LPA that require prompt legal attention and careful navigation by DCM in its capacity as General Partner of the Fund.

This engagement letter confirms the terms and conditions under which C&H will provide legal advisory services to the Clients (as defined below) in connection with the Key Person Event, including, without limitation, analysis of the A&R LPA\'s key-person provisions, preparation of required limited partner notifications, development of a successor governance framework, drafting of LPA amendments, and coordination of the limited partner consent solicitation process.
**[2. Clients]{.underline}**
For purposes of this engagement, C&H\'s clients shall consist of both DCM and DARF (collectively, the \"Clients\").

DCM\'s principal office is located at 680 Lexington Avenue, 31st Floor, New York, NY 10022. DCM\'s registered agent for service of process in the State of Delaware is Capitol Registered Agents, Inc., located at 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801.

DARF\'s registered office is located at 4th Floor, Harbour Place, 103 South Church Street, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1104, Cayman Islands. DARF\'s registered agent in the Cayman Islands is Archipelago Corporate Services Ltd., P.O. Box 2681, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1111, Cayman Islands.

It is important that the scope of this representation be clearly understood. C&H represents DCM and DARF as described herein and does not represent any individual limited partner of the Fund, the Investor Advisory Committee of the Fund (the \"IAC\"), or any individual member or officer of DCM in his or her personal capacity. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, C&H does not represent Mr. Whitmore individually, nor does C&H represent any member of the IAC in his, her, or its individual or fiduciary capacity. Each such person and entity is encouraged to seek independent legal counsel to the extent such person or entity deems it necessary or appropriate.

Elaine R. Sato, in her capacity as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding a ten percent (10%) membership interest) of DCM, will serve as the primary point of contact for the Clients in connection with this engagement. All communications from C&H regarding this engagement will be directed to Ms. Sato unless otherwise instructed in writing by Ms. Sato. C&H will take direction from Ms. Sato with respect to all matters within the scope of this engagement, subject to the Firm\'s professional obligations.
**[3. Scope of Representation]{.underline}**

C&H\'s representation of the Clients will encompass the following workstreams in connection with the Key Person Event triggered under Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA. Each workstream is described in further detail below.
**3.1 Key-Person Event Analysis**
C&H will undertake a comprehensive analysis of the mechanics and consequences of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, including the following:

> \(a\) **Section 8.04(a) --- Definition of \"Key Person.\"** C&H will confirm the scope of the \"Key Person\" designation under the A&R LPA, which identifies Marcus J. Whitmore as the sole designated Key Person. C&H will analyze the definition for purposes of establishing the factual predicate for the Key Person Event and for advising on the requirements for designating any Successor Key Person(s) (as described in Section 3.3 below).

> \(b\) **Section 8.04(b) --- Trigger Conditions.** C&H will analyze the trigger conditions set forth in Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA in light of the facts surrounding Mr. Whitmore\'s incapacitation. Specifically, Section 8.04(b) provides that a Key Person Event is deemed to occur when the Key Person becomes unable, whether by reason of death, disability, incapacity, departure, or otherwise, to devote substantially all of his professional time and attention to the affairs of the Fund for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. Based on the information provided to C&H, Mr. Whitmore has been continuously incapacitated since June 3, 2024, and the seven-consecutive-calendar-day threshold was met as of June 10, 2024. C&H will prepare a memorandum confirming the legal basis for this determination.

> \(c\) **Section 8.04(c) --- Consequences of the Key Person Event.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the full range of consequences triggered by the occurrence of the Key Person Event under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, which include the following:

> \(i\) *Immediate Suspension of the Investment Period.* The Investment Period (as defined in Section 1.01 of the A&R LPA) is automatically suspended upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event. During such suspension, the General Partner may not make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Fund, except as provided in clause (ii) below.

> \(ii\) *Follow-On Investment Cap.* Notwithstanding the suspension of the Investment Period, the General Partner retains limited authority to make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not to exceed one percent (1%) of the Fund\'s assets under management as of the date of the Key Person Event. Based on the Fund\'s most recently reported AUM of approximately \$2.87 billion, the follow-on investment cap is \$28.7 million.

> \(iii\) *LP Notification Requirement.* The General Partner is required to provide written notice to all limited partners of the occurrence of the Key Person Event within five (5) business days of the date on which the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred. Given that the Key Person Event is deemed to have occurred on June 10, 2024, the contractual deadline for delivery of such notice is June 17, 2024.

> \(iv\) *Commencement of the 90-Calendar-Day Cure Period.* Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, a cure period of ninety (90) calendar days (the \"Cure Period\") commences, during which the General Partner may propose one or more Successor Key Persons for approval by the limited partners. The Cure Period with respect to the current Key Person Event will expire on September 8, 2024.

> \(v\) *LP Consent Threshold.* Approval of any proposed Successor Key Person(s) requires the affirmative written consent of limited partners holding at least sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate capital commitments of all limited partners of the Fund, excluding for this purpose any co-investment by the General Partner. C&H will advise on the calculation of this threshold based on the most current LP commitment schedule maintained by the Fund\'s administrator.

> \(d\) **Consequences of Failure to Cure.** C&H will further analyze the consequences under Section 8.04(d) of the A&R LPA if no cure is achieved within the Cure Period, including the limited partners\' right to elect, by the same 66⅔% consent threshold described above, either (x) to extend the Cure Period for one or more additional periods or (y) to direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Fund\'s portfolio. C&H will advise the Clients on the mechanics, timing, and fiduciary considerations associated with each of these alternatives.

> \(e\) **Delaware Law Fiduciary Duty Analysis.** C&H will advise the Clients regarding the fiduciary duties owed by DCM, as General Partner, to the limited partners of the Fund during the Key Person Event and throughout the consent solicitation process, as a matter of Delaware law. This analysis will address, among other things, the duty of care and the contractual modification of fiduciary duties under the A&R LPA, including the exculpation and indemnification provisions set forth in Article XII thereof.
**3.2 LP Notification**

C&H will draft the formal written notice to all forty-seven (47) limited partners of the Fund disclosing the occurrence of the Key Person Event in compliance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA (the \"Key Person Notice\"). The Key Person Notice will describe the factual basis for the Key Person Event, the contractual consequences thereof, the commencement and expected expiration date of the Cure Period, and the process by which the General Partner intends to propose Successor Key Person(s) for approval by the limited partners.

C&H will coordinate with Pinnacle Fund Services (Cayman) Ltd. (the \"Administrator\"), the Fund\'s third-party administrator, regarding the maintenance and accuracy of LP contact information, the appropriate method of delivery (including any notice provisions specified in the A&R LPA or in individual side letters), and the mechanics of distributing the Key Person Notice to all limited partners within the contractual timeframe. C&H will confirm with the Administrator that notice is delivered by a method that satisfies the delivery requirements of Section 15.01 of the A&R LPA.

It is critical that the Key Person Notice be delivered within the five (5) business-day contractual notification deadline, which, as noted above, falls on June 17, 2024. C&H will prioritize this workstream accordingly and will endeavor to deliver a draft of the Key Person Notice to Ms. Sato for review no later than June 13, 2024.
**3.3 Successor Governance Framework**

C&H will advise the Clients regarding the identification and evaluation of proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the development of a recommended successor governance framework for the Fund. This advisory work may encompass the following elements:

> \(a\) **Designation of Successor Key Person(s).** C&H will advise on the criteria and process for designating one or more Successor Key Persons under the A&R LPA, including the qualifications, investment experience, and operational capabilities that limited partners are likely to consider in evaluating any proposed successor. C&H will assist in preparing biographical and professional materials for inclusion in the consent solicitation package.

> \(b\) **Establishment of an Investment Committee.** In the event that the Clients determine that the successor governance framework should include the establishment of a formal Investment Committee or similar collective governance body (in lieu of, or in addition to, a sole Key Person designation), C&H will advise on the structure, composition, authority, and operating procedures of such body, and will prepare the necessary amendments to the A&R LPA to implement such structure.

> \(c\) **Modifications to Key-Person Clause Mechanics.** C&H will advise on potential modifications to the key-person provisions of Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA, which may include revised replacement periods, modified trigger events (including, for example, a threshold requiring the departure or incapacitation of more than one designated Key Person before a Key Person Event is deemed to occur), and other structural changes to reduce single-person dependency risk.

> \(d\) **Carried Interest Reallocation.** C&H will advise the Clients on the legal and governance considerations associated with any proposed reallocation of carried interest among GP personnel in connection with the transition, including the interplay between the carried interest provisions of the A&R LPA and the operating agreement of DCM.

> \(e\) **Designation of Senior Advisor or Emeritus Role.** To the extent the Clients determine it appropriate, C&H will advise on the creation of a Senior Advisor or emeritus role for Mr. Whitmore, including the scope of any continuing economic interest, advisory responsibilities, and governance rights that may be associated with such role.

> \(f\) **Fiduciary Duty Obligations.** Throughout the development of the successor governance framework, C&H will advise the Clients regarding their fiduciary duty obligations under applicable Delaware law, including the duty to act in good faith and in the best interests of the limited partners in proposing any successor governance arrangements.
**3.4 LPA Amendment Drafting**

C&H will prepare one or more amendments to the A&R LPA (each, an \"LPA Amendment\") to implement the successor governance framework developed pursuant to Section 3.3 above. It is anticipated that the LPA Amendments will include modifications to the following provisions of the A&R LPA, among others:
> \(a\) Section 8.04 (Key Person), to reflect the designation of Successor Key Person(s) and any revised key-person clause mechanics;

> \(b\) Section 9.02 (Investor Advisory Committee), to the extent any changes to the composition, authority, or procedures of the IAC are contemplated in connection with the successor governance framework;
> \(c\) Section 14.01 (Amendments), to the extent any changes to the amendment mechanics are necessary or advisable; and
> \(d\) Related schedules and exhibits, including the schedule of Key Persons attached to the A&R LPA.

All LPA Amendments will be subject to the consent requirements set forth in Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, which generally requires the written consent of the General Partner and limited partners holding at least 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding GP co-investment) for amendments to certain specified provisions, including Section 8.04. C&H will advise the Clients regarding the applicable consent thresholds for each proposed amendment.
**3.5 LP Consent Solicitation**

C&H will advise on and coordinate the consent solicitation process necessary to obtain limited partner approval of the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. This workstream will include the following:

> \(a\) **Successor Key Person Proposal Letter.** C&H will draft a detailed letter to all limited partners setting forth the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the rationale for the proposed designation(s), the terms of the proposed successor governance framework, and a summary of the proposed LPA Amendments (the \"Proposal Letter\"). The Proposal Letter will be designed to provide limited partners with all information reasonably necessary to make an informed decision regarding the proposed successor arrangements.

> \(b\) **Form of LP Written Consent.** C&H will prepare a Form of LP Written Consent (the \"Consent Form\") for execution by limited partners approving the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the related LPA Amendments. The Consent Form will be structured to comply with the requirements of Section 14.01 and Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA.

> \(c\) **Coordination of Consent Solicitation Process.** C&H will coordinate the distribution of the Proposal Letter and Consent Form to all forty-seven (47) limited partners, working in conjunction with the Administrator to ensure accurate and timely delivery. C&H will manage the consent solicitation timeline with a view toward obtaining the requisite LP consents prior to the expiration of the Cure Period on September 8, 2024.

> \(d\) **Tabulation and Certification.** C&H will tabulate the LP consents received and prepare a closing certificate confirming that the requisite consent threshold (66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments, excluding GP co-investment) has been satisfied and that the LPA Amendments are effective as of the date specified therein (the \"Closing Certificate\").

> \(e\) **Engagement with IAC Counsel.** C&H will engage with counsel to the Investor Advisory Committee, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, as necessary and appropriate regarding the IAC\'s review of and comments on the proposed Successor Key Person(s), the successor governance framework, and the LPA Amendments. C&H will coordinate with the Clients regarding any modifications to the proposed arrangements that may be requested by the IAC or its counsel.
**[4. Limitations on Scope]{.underline}**
The Clients should be aware of the following limitations on the scope of C&H\'s engagement:

> \(a\) **Cayman Islands Law.** C&H does not provide legal advice regarding the laws of the Cayman Islands. The Clients should consult separately with qualified Cayman Islands counsel regarding any Cayman Islands regulatory, partnership law, or other legal matters that may arise in connection with the Key Person Event or the transactions contemplated by this engagement, including any filings or notifications required under Cayman Islands law in connection with changes to the Fund\'s governance structure.

> \(b\) **Tax Advice.** C&H is not engaged to provide tax advice in connection with this engagement. The Clients should consult their own tax advisors regarding the U.S. federal, state, local, and non-U.S. tax implications of any carried interest reallocation, structural changes to the Fund or DCM, or other transactions contemplated by this engagement.

> \(c\) **Investment Advice.** C&H is not engaged to provide investment advice or to evaluate the investment merits of any portfolio positions held by the Fund. The Clients acknowledge that any decisions regarding the management, disposition, or retention of portfolio positions during the suspension of the Investment Period or otherwise are solely the responsibility of the Clients and their investment professionals.

> \(d\) **Third-Party Service Providers.** C&H does not represent the Fund\'s independent auditor (Graystone & Whitfield LLP), the Fund\'s prime broker (Halcyon Securities International Ltd.), the Administrator, or any other third-party service provider to the Fund or DCM. Each such service provider is represented by its own counsel, and the Clients should not assume that C&H\'s representation extends to any of those parties.

> \(e\) **Litigation and Regulatory Matters.** This engagement does not extend to any litigation, arbitration, regulatory investigation, enforcement action, or other adversarial or contested proceeding, whether existing or threatened, unless separately agreed in writing between C&H and the Clients. In the event any such matter arises during the course of this engagement, C&H will promptly advise the Clients and, if requested, discuss the terms of a separate engagement to address such matter.
**[5. Engagement Team]{.underline}**
C&H has assigned the following professionals to this engagement:
**Name**                **Role**                **Title**
Graham Sutherland       Responsible Partner     Partner, Funds & Asset Management
Pamela Cross            Billing Partner         Partner, Funds & Asset Management
Stephen Adler           Lead Associate          Associate, Funds & Asset Management
Theresa Kim             Working Associate       Associate, Funds & Asset Management

Graham Sutherland will serve as the responsible partner overseeing all legal advice rendered in connection with this engagement. Mr. Sutherland will be the Clients\' primary legal point of contact for substantive matters, and all material legal memoranda, draft documents, and advice letters will be reviewed and approved by Mr. Sutherland prior to delivery to the Clients.

Pamela Cross will serve as the billing partner responsible for fee arrangements, invoicing, and all financial aspects of the engagement. Any questions regarding billing, fees, or disbursements should be directed to Ms. Cross.

Stephen Adler will serve as the lead associate responsible for the day-to-day execution of the engagement workstreams described in Section 3 above, under the supervision of Mr. Sutherland. Theresa Kim will support Mr. Adler on all workstreams, with particular focus on document drafting and consent solicitation logistics.

C&H may assign additional attorneys, paralegals, or other professionals to this engagement as reasonably necessary to ensure the timely and effective completion of the workstreams described herein. C&H will provide prior notice to Ms. Sato before assigning any additional professionals whose time will be billed to the Clients.
**[6. Fee Arrangement]{.underline}**
**6.1 Hourly Rates**
Services rendered by C&H attorneys in connection with this engagement will be billed on an hourly basis at the following standard rates:
> • **Partners:** \$1,650 per hour
> • **Associates:** \$895 per hour

The foregoing rates are effective as of the date of this engagement letter and are subject to annual adjustment in accordance with C&H\'s standard rate-setting process. C&H will provide the Clients with at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any rate increase. Paralegal and other support staff time, if any, will be billed at rates communicated to the Clients in advance.
**6.2 Fee Cap**

Total professional fees for the engagement shall not exceed Three Hundred Eighty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$385,000) (the \"Fee Cap\") without the prior written consent of the Clients. The Fee Cap encompasses all professional fees of C&H attorneys assigned to this engagement for the workstreams described in Section 3 above. In the event C&H anticipates that total fees may approach or exceed the Fee Cap, C&H will promptly notify the Clients and discuss whether an adjustment to the Fee Cap is warranted. No fees in excess of the Fee Cap will be billed to the Clients absent prior written authorization from Ms. Sato or another authorized representative of DCM. The Fee Cap does not include out-of-pocket disbursements, which are addressed separately in Section 6.3 below.
**6.3 Disbursements and Expenses**

The Clients will reimburse C&H for reasonable out-of-pocket disbursements incurred in connection with this engagement, including, without limitation, costs of document production, photocopying, overnight courier and delivery charges, filing fees, database and research charges, and travel expenses (including airfare, lodging, and ground transportation), if any. All disbursements will be billed at cost, without markup. Disbursements are not subject to the Fee Cap set forth in Section 6.2. C&H will exercise reasonable judgment in incurring disbursements and will obtain the Clients\' prior approval before incurring any single disbursement in excess of Five Thousand Dollars (\$5,000).
**6.4 Billing and Payment**

C&H will issue monthly invoices to DCM at the address set forth in Section 2 above (or to such other address as DCM may designate in writing). Each invoice will include a reasonably detailed description of the services rendered and disbursements incurred during the applicable billing period. Invoices are payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. C&H reserves the right to suspend the performance of services in the event of non-payment of any invoice for a period exceeding sixty (60) days following the date of such invoice, provided that C&H shall provide at least ten (10) days\' prior written notice to the Clients before exercising such right.

Whitmore, the Fund\'s sole designated Key Person under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. This memorandum sets forth our analysis of the relevant contractual provisions, identifies the operative trigger for the Key Person Event, details the immediate consequences and cure mechanics, and provides a recommended course of action for the General Partner.

**Key Conclusion.** A Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b)(iv) of the A&R LPA has been triggered effective June 10, 2024 --- that date representing the expiration of the seven consecutive calendar day period following Mr. Whitmore\'s hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024, during which he has been unable to devote substantially all of his professional time to the affairs of the Fund.
**Immediate Consequences.** The occurrence of the Key Person Event triggers the following immediate consequences under the A&R LPA:

> • **Suspension of the Investment Period.** The Investment Period (as defined in Section 1.01(bb) of the A&R LPA) is immediately suspended. The General Partner may not make any new portfolio investments on behalf of the Fund during the suspension. Follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions are permitted but capped at \$28.7 million, representing 1% of assets under management as of the most recent NAV reporting date (May 31, 2024).

The Fund pursues a multi-strategy absolute return investment program encompassing equity long/short, event-driven, and credit relative value strategies, with a particular sector focus on the asset management and banking industries. The Fund was established on its inception date of March 15, 2017, and has operated continuously since that date under the governance framework established by the A&R LPA.

As of the date of this memorandum, the Fund has forty-seven (47) limited partners. The Fund\'s governance structure includes a five-member Investor Advisory Committee (the \"IAC\"), established pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA and discussed in greater detail in Section IV.B below. The IAC serves in an advisory capacity to the General Partner with respect to certain matters, including conflicts of interest, valuation disputes, and --- of particular relevance here --- key governance events.

DCM serves as the sole general partner of the Fund and is responsible for the day-to-day investment management and operations of the Fund in accordance with the A&R LPA and applicable law. DCM is registered as an investment adviser with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission under the Investment Advisers Act of 1940, as amended.

Marcus J. Whitmore is the Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and Managing Member (90%) of DCM, and the sole designated \"Key Person\" under Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA. Mr. Whitmore has been designated as the Key Person since the Fund\'s inception on March 15, 2017, and no other individual has at any time been named as a Key Person or co-Key Person under the A&R LPA as currently in effect.

Mr. Whitmore\'s central role in the Fund\'s investment process, combined with his sole designation as Key Person under the A&R LPA, creates a structural vulnerability that is now acutely relevant. The A&R LPA provides no mechanism for automatic succession or substitution of the Key Person, and the entire key-person framework depends on Mr. Whitmore alone.
Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA provides, in relevant part:

Third, we note that Section 8.04(a) does not define or cross-reference the concept of a \"Successor Key Person,\" which is addressed separately in Section 8.04(c). The two provisions operate in tandem but are structurally independent: Section 8.04(a) establishes who the Key Person is, while Section 8.04(c) establishes the mechanism by which a successor may be installed following a Key Person Event. There is no ambiguity in the current designation, and no basis for an argument that any other individual currently qualifies as a Key Person under the existing terms of the A&R LPA.

**1. Triggering Events Enumerated.** Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA provides that a \"Key Person Event\" shall be deemed to have occurred upon the occurrence of any of the following events with respect to the Key Person:

Each of these triggering events is designed to address a different scenario in which the Key Person\'s active involvement in the Fund\'s operations is interrupted or terminated. Sub-clauses (i) through (iii) address definitive status changes (death, permanent disability, departure), while sub-clause (iv) addresses temporary or indefinite absences that may not rise to the level of the other triggers but nevertheless constitute a material disruption to the Fund\'s management.

The sub-clause (iv) trigger is particularly significant in this context because it operates on a short, seven-calendar-day timeline and does not require a determination of permanent disability or formal departure. It is, in effect, a \"business continuity\" trigger designed to ensure that LP interests are protected against even relatively short periods of Key Person absence that were not anticipated and disclosed in advance.
**Conclusion: A Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b)(iv) of the A&R LPA is deemed to have occurred effective June 10, 2024.**

We note that the A&R LPA does not specify whether the seven-day period is measured inclusive or exclusive of the first day of inability. Under the convention most commonly applied in Delaware contract interpretation --- and consistent with the general rule that the day of the triggering event is excluded from the count --- the seven-day period would run from June 4 through June 10, yielding a trigger date of June 10, 2024. However, even under the alternative calculation (June 3 through June 9, yielding a trigger date of June 9, 2024), the Key Person Event has already occurred as of the date of this memorandum. For purposes of clarity and conservative calculation of downstream deadlines, we use June 10, 2024 as the operative trigger date throughout this memorandum.

**Permanent Disability.** The A&R LPA does not define \"permanent disability.\" In the absence of a contractual definition, a Delaware court would likely interpret the term in accordance with its ordinary meaning, informed by relevant context and, potentially, analogous definitions in related legal instruments (such as disability insurance policies, employment agreements, or the Americans with Disabilities Act). Under these authorities, \"permanent disability\" generally requires a showing that the individual suffers from a physical or mental condition that is expected to be of indefinite duration or to prevent the substantial performance of the individual\'s duties on a permanent or near-permanent basis.
Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA establishes the consequences that flow from the occurrence of a Key Person Event and the mechanics by which the event may be cured. We address each consequence in turn.

The notification should be addressed to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners at the addresses set forth in Schedule B to the A&R LPA (or such updated addresses as have been provided by the LPs in accordance with Section 15.01 of the A&R LPA). > • **Firm Deadline.** The 90-day Cure Period represents a firm outer deadline that cannot be unilaterally extended by the General Partner. The A&R LPA does not provide for any extension at the discretion of the GP, nor does it authorize the GP to toll or suspend the running of the Cure Period for any reason. The only mechanism for extension is an LP vote following the expiration of the initial Cure Period, as discussed in Section III.C.5 below.

> • **Multiple Proposals Permitted.** The A&R LPA does not limit the General Partner to a single proposal during the Cure Period. If an initial proposal fails to achieve the requisite LP consent, the General Partner may submit a revised or alternative proposal, provided the Cure Period has not yet expired. As a practical matter, however, the compressed timeline makes sequential proposals difficult; the General Partner should aim to submit a single, well-supported proposal that is likely to achieve the necessary consent.

Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA governs amendments to the partnership agreement and provides that any amendment or modification of the A&R LPA requires the written consent of the General Partner and the requisite percentage of Limited Partners specified for the particular action in question. For purposes of the Successor Key Person approval, the requisite LP percentage is 66⅔% of aggregate LP capital commitments (excluding the GP\'s co-investment), as set forth in Section 8.04(c).

The A&R LPA expressly permits written consent in lieu of a formal meeting of the Limited Partners. Section 14.03 provides that any action that may be taken at a meeting of the Limited Partners may alternatively be taken without a meeting if a consent in writing, setting forth the action so taken, is signed by Limited Partners holding the requisite percentage of capital commitments. This written consent mechanism is the appropriate procedural vehicle for the Successor Key Person approval, and we do not recommend convening a formal LP meeting for this purpose.

The written consent must be executed in writing (which, under Section 15.01, includes electronic signature and delivery) and must specifically reference the action being consented to. A generic or open-ended consent form would be insufficient; the consent must describe the identity of the proposed Successor Key Person(s) and the terms of any associated amendment to the A&R LPA with sufficient specificity to demonstrate informed LP approval.

The 90-day Cure Period imposes a firm outer deadline of September 8, 2024. Within this window, the General Partner must (i) prepare the Successor Proposal and draft Amendment, (ii) engage with the IAC in advance of broader LP circulation, (iii) circulate the proposal materials to all 47 LPs, (iv) allow adequate time for LP review and deliberation, (v) negotiate with IAC counsel on any proposed revisions, and (vi) collect executed consents from LPs holding at least 66⅔% of aggregate voting LP capital commitments.

Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA provides that the agreement shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to conflict-of-laws principles that would require the application of any other jurisdiction\'s laws. The Delaware Revised Uniform Limited Partnership Act, 6 Del. C. §§ 17-101 *et seq.* (the \"DRULPA\"), provides the statutory framework governing the formation, operation, and governance of limited partnerships formed or operating under Delaware law. Although DARF is a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership rather than a Delaware limited partnership, the parties\' contractual election of Delaware law as the governing law of the A&R LPA means that Delaware substantive law --- including DRULPA principles --- governs the interpretation of the agreement and the rights and obligations of the General Partner and the Limited Partners thereunder. Certain procedural matters and matters relating to the Fund\'s legal status as a Cayman Islands entity (such as registration, filing requirements, and regulatory compliance) remain subject to Cayman Islands law.

Under DRULPA § 17-1101(d), a partnership agreement may expand, restrict, or eliminate fiduciary duties, subject to one important limitation: the partnership agreement may not eliminate the implied contractual covenant of good faith and fair dealing. This provision gives broad latitude to the parties to define the scope and nature of the fiduciary duties owed by the general partner, but preserves a baseline obligation of good-faith conduct in the performance of contractual obligations.

The A&R LPA does not eliminate the General Partner\'s fiduciary duties. Rather, Section 7.01 of the A&R LPA provides, in relevant part, that the General Partner shall manage the business and affairs of the Fund in accordance with its fiduciary obligations to the Limited Partners, subject to the contractual limitations, exculpation provisions, and safe harbors set forth elsewhere in the agreement. Specifically, Section 7.02 exculpates the General Partner from liability for losses arising from actions taken in good faith and without gross negligence or willful misconduct, and Section 7.03 provides for indemnification of the General Partner and its affiliates to the fullest extent permitted by Delaware law.

Delaware law strongly favors freedom of contract in the limited partnership context. DRULPA § 17-1101(c) provides that \"\[i\]t is the policy of \[DRULPA\] to give maximum effect to the principle of freedom of contract and to the enforceability of partnership agreements.\" The consent threshold (66⅔%) and solicitation mechanics established by the A&R LPA are therefore enforceable as written, and a Delaware court would give effect to these provisions according to their terms.

> • The GP must provide LPs with sufficient information to make an informed consent decision. This includes full and fair disclosure of the circumstances giving rise to the Key Person Event, the qualifications and experience of the proposed Successor Key Persons, the terms of any proposed amendment to the A&R LPA, and the consequences of failure to achieve LP consent within the Cure Period.

> • The GP must treat all LPs equitably in the solicitation process. The GP may not offer side arrangements, preferential economic terms, or other inducements to certain LPs in exchange for their consent, to the extent such arrangements would disadvantage other LPs or violate the equal treatment provisions of the A&R LPA.

However, to the extent that the carried interest reallocation is reflected in or necessitates changes to the A&R LPA --- for example, by amending Schedule A of the A&R LPA to update the allocation waterfall or by modifying the fee and incentive provisions of Article VI --- such changes would require LP consent at the applicable threshold under Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA. In practice, the most efficient approach is to incorporate any necessary carry reallocation provisions into the proposed First Amendment to the A&R LPA, so that the Successor Key Person approval and the carry reallocation are addressed in a single consent solicitation.

A Key Person Event under Section 8.04(b)(iv) of the A&R LPA has been triggered effective **June 10, 2024**, as a result of Mr. Whitmore\'s inability to devote substantially all of his professional time to the affairs of the Fund for a period of seven consecutive calendar days following his hemorrhagic stroke on June 3, 2024.

Accordingly, the Key Person Event was deemed triggered on June 10, 2024 (i.e., seven consecutive calendar days following June 3, 2024) (the \"Key Person Event Date\").

25: Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA provides that: (i) the Investment Period of the Partnership shall be automatically suspended; (ii) the General Partner shall not make any new portfolio investments on behalf of the Partnership, provided that the General Partner may make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not exceeding \$28.7 million (representing 1.0% of the Partnership\'s assets under management as of the most recent quarterly valuation); and (iii) a 90-calendar-day cure period (the \"Cure Period\") shall commence on the Key Person Event Date, during which the General Partner may propose one or more Successor Key Persons for approval by the Limited Partners. The Cure Period commenced on June 10, 2024 and was set to expire on September 8, 2024.
26: 
27: **C. LP Notification.**
28: 
29: Pursuant to Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, the General Partner was required to notify all Limited Partners in writing within five (5) business days of the occurrence of the Key Person Event. The Key Person Event occurred on June 10, 2024; accordingly, the notification deadline was June 17, 2024 (the fifth business day following June 10, 2024, accounting for the weekend of June 15--16, 2024).
30: 
31: The General Partner delivered written notice of the Key Person Event (the \"Key Person Event Notice\") to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners of the Partnership on June 14, 2024, which date was within the required five (5) business day notification period. The Key Person Event Notice was delivered by electronic mail transmission to the notice addresses on file for each Limited Partner, with a copy delivered by international courier (Granite Harbor Enterprises) to each Limited Partner\'s physical notice address, in each case as set forth in the records of the Partnership and in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA. The Key Person Event Notice described: (i) the nature of the Key Person Event; (ii) the suspension of the Investment Period; (iii) the restrictions on new portfolio investments; (iv) the commencement and expiration of the Cure Period; and (v) the General Partner\'s intention to propose one or more Successor Key Persons during the Cure Period.
32: 
33: **D. The Successor Proposal and the First Amendment.**
34: 
35: Following extensive consultations with the members of the Investor Advisory Committee (as described in Recital G below), the General Partner proposed Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons for the Partnership. Ms. Sato currently serves as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding 10% of the membership interests) of DCM. She has been with DCM since its formation in 2015 and has been a senior member of the investment team throughout the life of the Partnership. Mr. Huang currently serves as Head of Credit Strategies of DCM. He joined DCM in 2017 and has served in roles of progressively increasing responsibility within the investment team, most recently overseeing all credit-related investment strategies of the Partnership.
36: 
37: On July 15, 2024, the General Partner circulated the following documents to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners of the Partnership, in each case by electronic mail transmission and international courier delivery in accordance with Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA:
38: 
39: > \(i\) a Successor Key Person Proposal letter, dated July 15, 2024, setting forth the qualifications, experience, and proposed roles of Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons, together with biographical information and investment track records for each proposed Successor Key Person (the \"Successor Proposal\");
40: >
41: > \(ii\) a draft First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (the \"First Amendment\"), together with a blackline comparison to the A&R LPA showing all proposed amendments; and
42: >
43: > \(iii\) a Form of Written Consent of Limited Partners (the \"Form of Written Consent\"), to be executed and returned by each consenting Limited Partner on or before the LP Consent Deadline (as defined in Recital F below).
44: 
45: The First Amendment, among other things, provides for the following changes to the A&R LPA:
46: 
47: > \(a\) *Redefinition of \"Key Person.\"* Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA is amended to redefine \"Key Person\" to mean Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, jointly, for so long as each of them serves in her or his respective capacity with the General Partner and devotes substantially all of her or his professional time to the investment activities and affairs of the Partnership.
48: >
49: > \(b\) *Replacement Period for Loss of One Successor Key Person.* Sections 8.04(b) and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA are amended to provide that, in the event of the departure, death, permanent disability, incapacitation, or other loss of one (but not both) of the Successor Key Persons, a 180-calendar-day Replacement Period (rather than an automatic suspension of the Investment Period) shall be triggered, during which the remaining Successor Key Person and the General Partner shall identify and propose a replacement to the Limited Partners for approval. In the event of the departure, death, permanent disability, incapacitation, or other loss of both Successor Key Persons, a Key Person Event shall be deemed to have occurred, with consequences as previously provided in Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA.
50: >
51: > \(c\) *Establishment of Investment Committee.* A new Section 8.05 is added to the A&R LPA, establishing a three-member Investment Committee of the Partnership. The Investment Committee shall consist of: (1) Elaine R. Sato, who shall serve as Chair of the Investment Committee; (2) Jonathan K. Huang; and (3) one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee of the Partnership pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA. All new portfolio investments by the Partnership in excess of \$5.0 million shall require the approval of at least two (2) of the three (3) members of the Investment Committee. The Investment Committee shall meet no less frequently than bi-weekly during the first twelve (12) months following the Amendment Effective Date.
52: >
53: > \(d\) *Reduction of Follow-On Investment Cap.* The follow-on investment cap applicable during any future Key Person Event is reduced from \$28.7 million (representing 1.0% of the Partnership\'s assets under management) to \$14.35 million (representing 0.5% of the Partnership\'s assets under management), reflecting a more conservative posture during periods of leadership transition.
54: >
55: > \(e\) *Designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor.* Marcus J. Whitmore is designated as \"Senior Advisor\" to the Partnership and to the General Partner, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date. In such capacity, Mr. Whitmore shall have no governance authority, no voting rights with respect to any matter requiring the action or consent of the General Partner, and no authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner. Mr. Whitmore\'s role as Senior Advisor shall be limited to providing non-binding advisory input on investment matters, to the extent his health permits, and shall be subject to the terms and conditions of a separate Senior Advisor Agreement between Mr. Whitmore and DCM.
56: >
57: > \(f\) *Amendment to Schedule A (Carried Interest Allocation).* Schedule A to the A&R LPA is amended to reflect the following revised allocations of the General Partner\'s 20% incentive allocation (i.e., the \"Carried Interest\"):
58: >
59: > • Marcus J. Whitmore: 9% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (reduced from 18%);
60: >
61: > • Elaine R. Sato: 7% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (increased from 1.5%);
62: >
63: > • Jonathan K. Huang: 4% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (increased from 0.5%);
64: >
65: > • Remaining GP-level allocation (other DCM members and reserves): unchanged;
66: >
67: > • GP-level total incentive allocation: 20% (unchanged).
68: >
69: > Mr. Whitmore\'s carried interest shall vest on a modified schedule as follows: fifty percent (50%) of Mr. Whitmore\'s carried interest allocation shall be deemed vested immediately as of the Key Person Event Date (June 10, 2024); the remaining fifty percent (50%) shall vest ratably on a monthly basis over thirty-six (36) months commencing on June 10, 2024, subject to continued compliance by Mr. Whitmore with the non-competition and non-solicitation covenants set forth in the Operating Agreement of DCM and the Senior Advisor Agreement.
70: 
71: **E. Consent Requirement.**
72: 
73: Pursuant to Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, any amendment to the A&R LPA requires the written consent of the General Partner and of Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment). Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA further provides that the approval of Successor Key Persons and any related amendments to the A&R LPA shall be subject to the same consent threshold set forth in Section 14.01.
74: 
75: As of the Certification Date, the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments for purposes of the consent vote (the \"Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments\") are calculated as follows:
76: 
77: > Total Fund Net Asset Value (as of Q2 2024 quarterly valuation): \$2,870.0 million
78: >
79: > Less: Marcus J. Whitmore capital commitment (committed through the GP vehicle, DCM): (\$57.4 million)
80: >
81: > Less: Elaine R. Sato capital commitment (committed through the GP vehicle, DCM): (\$14.35 million)
82: >
83: > **Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments: \$2,798.25 million**
84: 
85: The capital commitments of Mr. Whitmore and Ms. Sato are excluded from the Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments because they were committed through the General Partner\'s co-investment vehicle and are therefore excluded pursuant to Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, which provides that \"for purposes of any vote or consent of the Limited Partners, the capital commitments of the General Partner and any Affiliate of the General Partner that are invested through the General Partner\'s co-investment shall be excluded from the denominator.\"
86: 
87: The required consent threshold is therefore:
88: 
89: > \$2,798.25 million × 66⅔% = **\$1,865.50 million**
90: 
91: **F. Consent Deadline.**
92: 
93: The General Partner established August 23, 2024 as the deadline by which all Forms of Written Consent were required to be received by the General Partner (the \"LP Consent Deadline\"). The LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024 represents forty (40) calendar days from the July 15, 2024 circulation date of the Successor Proposal, the First Amendment, and the Form of Written Consent. The forty-day consent period was determined by the General Partner to be reasonable and consistent with the time periods customarily afforded to Limited Partners in similar circumstances, and was within the Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024. The General Partner also delivered reminder notices to all Limited Partners who had not yet returned executed Forms of Written Consent on August 5, 2024 and August 12, 2024, respectively.
94: 
95: **G. IAC Review.**
96: 
97: The Investor Advisory Committee (the \"IAC\") of the Partnership, established pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA, consists of five (5) members, each of whom is a representative of a Limited Partner of the Partnership. As of the date hereof, the members of the IAC are as follows:
98: 
99: > 1\. Diana Cortland, Representative of Northvale Public Employees\' Retirement System --- IAC Chair;
100: >
101: > 2\. Richard Oshima, Representative of Sycamore Endowment Partners LP;
102: >
103: > 3\. Catherine Mercer, Representative of Velthorn Institutional Fund of Funds III, L.P.;
104: >
105: > 4\. Thomas Ashworth, Representative of Bridlewood Family Office Holdings Ltd.; and
106: >
107: > 5\. Nadia Al-Rashid, Representative of Atlas Sovereign Wealth Advisory LLC.
108: 
109: The IAC reviewed the Successor Proposal, the First Amendment, and related materials at a meeting held on July 29, 2024, at the offices of Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, 51 West 52nd Street, 40th Floor, New York, NY 10019. The meeting was attended by all five IAC members (Ms. Cortland, Mr. Oshima, Ms. Mercer, Mr. Ashworth, and Ms. Al-Rashid) and by legal counsel to the IAC, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (Helen M. Calloway, Partner, and David Pineda, Senior Associate). Also in attendance at the invitation of the IAC were Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang, who presented their qualifications, investment philosophy, and proposed governance structure, and responded to questions from the IAC members and their legal counsel. The IAC meeting lasted approximately three hours and forty-five minutes. Following the presentation and discussion, the IAC unanimously confirmed that it did not object to the Successor Proposal or the First Amendment, and that the IAC would recommend to the Limited Partners that they approve the same. The IAC\'s recommendation was communicated to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners by separate letter from Ms. Cortland, as IAC Chair, dated August 1, 2024.
110: 
111: **[CERTIFICATIONS]{.underline}**
112: 
113: NOW, THEREFORE, the General Partner, acting through its duly authorized representative, hereby certifies as follows:
114: 
115: **Section 1. Certification of Consent Tabulation.**
116: 
117: **1.1 Receipt of Written Consents.** The undersigned, on behalf of DCM as General Partner of the Partnership, hereby certifies that the General Partner has received duly executed Forms of Written Consent from thirty-eight (38) of the forty-seven (47) Limited Partners of the Partnership (collectively, the \"Consenting LPs\"). Each Form of Written Consent received by the General Partner was executed by an authorized signatory of the respective Limited Partner and delivered to the General Partner in accordance with the delivery instructions set forth in the Form of Written Consent and the notice provisions of Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA. The General Partner has verified the authority of each signatory based on the relevant subscription documents, incumbency certificates, and/or powers of attorney on file with the Partnership.
118: 
119: All thirty-eight (38) written consents were received by the General Partner on or before August 19, 2024, which date is four (4) calendar days prior to the LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024. No Forms of Written Consent were received by the General Partner after August 19, 2024 and on or before the LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024. No Forms of Written Consent were received by the General Partner after the LP Consent Deadline.
120: 
121: **1.2 Tabulation of Consenting LP Capital Commitments.** The aggregate capital commitments of the thirty-eight (38) Consenting LPs total Two Billion Four Hundred Twelve Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,412,800,000) (\$2,412.8 million). A detailed schedule of each Consenting LP and its respective capital commitment amount, together with the date on which the Form of Written Consent was received from such Consenting LP, is attached hereto as **Exhibit A** and is incorporated herein by reference.
122: 
123: **1.3 Percentage of Voting LP Capital Commitments.** The Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment, as described in Recital E above) are Two Billion Seven Hundred Ninety-Eight Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,798,250,000) (\$2,798.25 million). The consenting LP capital commitments of \$2,412.8 million represent approximately eighty-six and two-tenths percent (86.2%) of the Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments, calculated as follows:
124: 
125: > \$2,412,800,000 ÷ \$2,798,250,000 = 86.2% (rounded to the nearest tenth of a percent)
126: 
127: **1.4 Satisfaction of Consent Threshold.** The required consent threshold under Sections 14.01 and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA is sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments, which equals One Billion Eight Hundred Sixty-Five Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,865,500,000) (\$1,865.50 million). The consenting LP capital commitments of \$2,412.8 million exceed the required threshold of \$1,865.50 million by Five Hundred Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$547,300,000) (\$547.3 million). Accordingly, the General Partner hereby certifies that the consent threshold required under Sections 14.01 and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA has been satisfied, and the requisite written consent of the Limited Partners has been duly and validly obtained for purposes of approving the Successor Key Persons and the First Amendment.
128: 
129: **Section 2. Certification of Amendment Effectiveness.**
130: 
131: **2.1 Effectiveness of the First Amendment.** Having determined, as set forth in Section 1 above, that the requisite Limited Partner consent has been obtained in accordance with Sections 14.01 and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, and having further confirmed that all other conditions precedent to the effectiveness of the First Amendment have been satisfied (including, without limitation, the execution and delivery of the First Amendment by the General Partner on behalf of the Partnership), the General Partner hereby certifies that the First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. is effective as of August 26, 2024 (the \"Amendment Effective Date\"). The A&R LPA, as modified by the First Amendment, shall hereinafter be referred to as the \"LPA\" or the \"Partnership Agreement,\" and all references in any agreement, instrument, document, or certificate to the \"A&R LPA\" or the \"Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement\" shall be deemed to refer to the A&R LPA as amended by the First Amendment, unless the context otherwise requires.
132: 
133: **2.2 Summary of Key Amendments Now in Effect.** As of the Amendment Effective Date, the following material amendments to the A&R LPA, as effected by the First Amendment, are now in full force and effect:
134: 
135: > \(a\) *Section 8.04(a) --- Redefinition of \"Key Person.\"* The term \"Key Person\" is redefined to mean Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, jointly, for so long as each of them serves in her or his respective capacity with the General Partner and devotes substantially all of her or his professional time to the investment activities and affairs of the Partnership.
136: >
137: > \(b\) *Sections 8.04(b) and 8.04(c) --- Replacement Period.* Loss of one (but not both) Successor Key Person triggers a 180-calendar-day Replacement Period, during which the remaining Successor Key Person and the General Partner shall identify and propose a replacement to the Limited Partners for approval, rather than an automatic suspension of the Investment Period. Loss of both Successor Key Persons triggers a Key Person Event with consequences as previously provided in Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA.
138: >
139: > \(c\) *New Section 8.05 --- Investment Committee.* A three-member Investment Committee is established, consisting of Elaine R. Sato (Chair), Jonathan K. Huang, and one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA. All new portfolio investments in excess of \$5.0 million require approval of at least two (2) of the three (3) members of the Investment Committee.
140: >
141: > \(d\) *Follow-On Investment Cap.* The follow-on investment cap applicable during any future Key Person Event is reduced from \$28.7 million (1.0% of assets under management) to \$14.35 million (0.5% of assets under management).
142: >
143: > \(e\) *Designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor.* Marcus J. Whitmore is designated as Senior Advisor to the Partnership and to the General Partner, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, with no governance authority, no voting rights, and no authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner.
144: >
145: > \(f\) *Schedule A --- Carried Interest Allocation.* The revised allocations of the General Partner\'s 20% incentive allocation are as follows:
146: >
147: > • Marcus J. Whitmore: 9% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (reduced from 18%);
148: >
149: > • Elaine R. Sato: 7% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (increased from 1.5%);
150: >
151: > • Jonathan K. Huang: 4% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (increased from 0.5%);
152: >
153: > • GP-level total incentive allocation: 20% (unchanged).
154: >
155: > \(g\) *Whitmore Carried Interest Vesting.* Fifty percent (50%) of Mr. Whitmore\'s carried interest allocation vested immediately as of the Key Person Event Date (June 10, 2024). The remaining fifty percent (50%) vests ratably on a monthly basis over thirty-six (36) months commencing on June 10, 2024, subject to continued compliance by Mr. Whitmore with the non-competition and non-solicitation covenants set forth in the Operating Agreement of DCM and the Senior Advisor Agreement.
156: 
157: **2.3 Cure Period.** The 90-calendar-day Cure Period under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA commenced on the Key Person Event Date of June 10, 2024 and was set to expire on September 8, 2024. The effectiveness of the First Amendment on the Amendment Effective Date of August 26, 2024 --- which date is thirteen (13) calendar days prior to the expiration of the Cure Period --- constitutes a cure of the Key Person Event within the Cure Period, in accordance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA. Accordingly, the September 8, 2024 Cure Period expiration date is rendered moot.
158: 
159: Furthermore, the suspension of the Investment Period that took effect automatically upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event on June 10, 2024, pursuant to Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, is hereby terminated as of the Amendment Effective Date of August 26, 2024. The Investment Period shall continue from the Amendment Effective Date in accordance with its original terms as set forth in Section 7.01 of the A&R LPA (as amended by the First Amendment), and the General Partner (acting through the newly established Investment Committee) shall be permitted to make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Partnership, subject to the terms and conditions of the A&R LPA as amended by the First Amendment.

Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Certificate shall be resolved in accordance with the dispute resolution provisions set forth in Section 15.04 of the A&R LPA (as amended by the First Amendment).
