lines.text: **CERTIFICATE OF THE GENERAL PARTNER** **REGARDING LIMITED PARTNER CONSENT TABULATION** **AND EFFECTIVENESS OF THE FIRST AMENDMENT** **TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT** **OF** **DRIFTWOOD ABSOLUTE RETURN FUND LTD.**
August 26, 2024

Driftwood Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (EIN: 82-4917653) (\"DCM\" or the \"General Partner\"), in its capacity as the general partner of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd., a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership registered under Registration No. ELP-87234 (the \"Partnership\" or \"DARF\"), hereby issues this Certificate of the General Partner Regarding Limited Partner Consent Tabulation and Effectiveness of the First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of the Partnership (this \"Certificate\") as of August 26, 2024 (the \"Certification Date\"). This Certificate is delivered pursuant to, and in accordance with, the authority vested in the General Partner under the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of the Partnership dated as of March 15, 2017 (as defined below, the \"A&R LPA\"), and is based upon the following recitals of fact and the certifications set forth herein.
**[RECITALS]{.underline}**
**A. The Partnership and the A&R LPA.**

Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (\"DARF\" or the \"Partnership\") is a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership duly registered under the Exempted Limited Partnership Act (As Revised) of the Cayman Islands, bearing Registration No. ELP-87234, with its registered office located at 4th Floor, Harbour Place, 103 South Church Street, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1104, Cayman Islands. The registered agent of the Partnership in the Cayman Islands is Archipelago Corporate Services Ltd., P.O. Box 2681, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1111, Cayman Islands. The Partnership was originally formed pursuant to an Agreement of Limited Partnership dated as of November 2, 2015, which was subsequently amended and restated in its entirety by the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement dated as of March 15, 2017 (the \"A&R LPA\"). The A&R LPA is governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware, as provided in Section 15.02 thereof.

Driftwood Capital Management LLC (\"DCM\" or the \"General Partner\") is a limited liability company duly organized and existing under the laws of the State of Delaware, with its principal office located at 680 Lexington Avenue, 31st Floor, New York, NY 10022, and its Delaware registered agent at Capitol Registered Agents, Inc., 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, DE 19801. DCM serves as the sole general partner of the Partnership and, in such capacity, is responsible for the management, operation, and investment activities of the Partnership as set forth in the A&R LPA.

As of the date hereof, the Partnership has forty-seven (47) Limited Partners who have been admitted to the Partnership in accordance with the terms and conditions of the A&R LPA and the relevant subscription agreements. The General Partner confirms that no additional Limited Partners have been admitted, and no existing Limited Partners have withdrawn or been removed, since the date of the Key Person Event (as defined below).
**B. The Key Person Event.**

Pursuant to Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA, Marcus J. Whitmore, Founder, Chief Investment Officer, and Managing Member (holding 90% of the membership interests) of DCM, was designated as the sole \"Key Person\" of the Partnership. Section 8.04(a) provides, in relevant part, that the term \"Key Person\" shall mean \"Marcus J. Whitmore, individually, for so long as he serves as the Chief Investment Officer of the General Partner and devotes substantially all of his professional time to the investment activities and affairs of the Partnership.\"

On June 3, 2024, Mr. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke, resulting in his hospitalization and rendering him unable to devote substantially all of his professional time to the investment activities and affairs of the Partnership. Mr. Whitmore\'s medical condition, as confirmed by attending physicians at NewYork-Presbyterian Hospital / Weill Cornell Medical Center and communicated to the General Partner, has been such that he has been and remains unable to perform his duties as Chief Investment Officer or to participate in any material respect in the management, operation, or investment activities of the Partnership.

Pursuant to Section 8.04(b) of the A&R LPA, a \"Key Person Event\" is deemed to have occurred if the Key Person \"is unable to devote substantially all of his professional time to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days, whether by reason of death, permanent disability, incapacitation, resignation, removal, or any other cause.\" The seven (7) consecutive calendar day period commenced on June 3, 2024 and expired on June 10, 2024. Accordingly, the Key Person Event was deemed triggered on June 10, 2024 (i.e., seven consecutive calendar days following June 3, 2024) (the \"Key Person Event Date\").

Upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event, Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA provides that: (i) the Investment Period of the Partnership shall be automatically suspended; (ii) the General Partner shall not make any new portfolio investments on behalf of the Partnership, provided that the General Partner may make follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions in an aggregate amount not exceeding \$28.7 million (representing 1.0% of the Partnership\'s assets under management as of the most recent quarterly valuation); and (iii) a 90-calendar-day cure period (the \"Cure Period\") shall commence on the Key Person Event Date, during which the General Partner may propose one or more Successor Key Persons for approval by the Limited Partners. The Cure Period commenced on June 10, 2024 and was set to expire on September 8, 2024.
**C. LP Notification.**

Pursuant to Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, the General Partner was required to notify all Limited Partners in writing within five (5) business days of the occurrence of the Key Person Event. The Key Person Event occurred on June 10, 2024; accordingly, the notification deadline was June 17, 2024 (the fifth business day following June 10, 2024, accounting for the weekend of June 15--16, 2024).

The General Partner delivered written notice of the Key Person Event (the \"Key Person Event Notice\") to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners of the Partnership on June 14, 2024, which date was within the required five (5) business day notification period. The Key Person Event Notice was delivered by electronic mail transmission to the notice addresses on file for each Limited Partner, with a copy delivered by international courier (Granite Harbor Enterprises) to each Limited Partner\'s physical notice address, in each case as set forth in the records of the Partnership and in accordance with the notice provisions of Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA. The Key Person Event Notice described: (i) the nature of the Key Person Event; (ii) the suspension of the Investment Period; (iii) the restrictions on new portfolio investments; (iv) the commencement and expiration of the Cure Period; and (v) the General Partner\'s intention to propose one or more Successor Key Persons during the Cure Period.
**D. The Successor Proposal and the First Amendment.**

Following extensive consultations with the members of the Investor Advisory Committee (as described in Recital G below), the General Partner proposed Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons for the Partnership. Ms. Sato currently serves as Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding 10% of the membership interests) of DCM. She has been with DCM since its formation in 2015 and has been a senior member of the investment team throughout the life of the Partnership. Mr. Huang currently serves as Head of Credit Strategies of DCM. He joined DCM in 2017 and has served in roles of progressively increasing responsibility within the investment team, most recently overseeing all credit-related investment strategies of the Partnership.

On July 15, 2024, the General Partner circulated the following documents to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners of the Partnership, in each case by electronic mail transmission and international courier delivery in accordance with Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA:

> \(i\) a Successor Key Person Proposal letter, dated July 15, 2024, setting forth the qualifications, experience, and proposed roles of Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang as joint Successor Key Persons, together with biographical information and investment track records for each proposed Successor Key Person (the \"Successor Proposal\");

> \(ii\) a draft First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (the \"First Amendment\"), together with a blackline comparison to the A&R LPA showing all proposed amendments; and

> \(iii\) a Form of Written Consent of Limited Partners (the \"Form of Written Consent\"), to be executed and returned by each consenting Limited Partner on or before the LP Consent Deadline (as defined in Recital F below).
The First Amendment, among other things, provides for the following changes to the A&R LPA:

> \(a\) *Redefinition of \"Key Person.\"* Section 8.04(a) of the A&R LPA is amended to redefine \"Key Person\" to mean Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, jointly, for so long as each of them serves in her or his respective capacity with the General Partner and devotes substantially all of her or his professional time to the investment activities and affairs of the Partnership.

> \(b\) *Replacement Period for Loss of One Successor Key Person.* Sections 8.04(b) and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA are amended to provide that, in the event of the departure, death, permanent disability, incapacitation, or other loss of one (but not both) of the Successor Key Persons, a 180-calendar-day Replacement Period (rather than an automatic suspension of the Investment Period) shall be triggered, during which the remaining Successor Key Person and the General Partner shall identify and propose a replacement to the Limited Partners for approval. In the event of the departure, death, permanent disability, incapacitation, or other loss of both Successor Key Persons, a Key Person Event shall be deemed to have occurred, with consequences as previously provided in Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA.

> \(c\) *Establishment of Investment Committee.* A new Section 8.05 is added to the A&R LPA, establishing a three-member Investment Committee of the Partnership. The Investment Committee shall consist of: (1) Elaine R. Sato, who shall serve as Chair of the Investment Committee; (2) Jonathan K. Huang; and (3) one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee of the Partnership pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA. All new portfolio investments by the Partnership in excess of \$5.0 million shall require the approval of at least two (2) of the three (3) members of the Investment Committee. The Investment Committee shall meet no less frequently than bi-weekly during the first twelve (12) months following the Amendment Effective Date.

> \(d\) *Reduction of Follow-On Investment Cap.* The follow-on investment cap applicable during any future Key Person Event is reduced from \$28.7 million (representing 1.0% of the Partnership\'s assets under management) to \$14.35 million (representing 0.5% of the Partnership\'s assets under management), reflecting a more conservative posture during periods of leadership transition.

> \(e\) *Designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor.* Marcus J. Whitmore is designated as \"Senior Advisor\" to the Partnership and to the General Partner, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date. In such capacity, Mr. Whitmore shall have no governance authority, no voting rights with respect to any matter requiring the action or consent of the General Partner, and no authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner. Mr. Whitmore\'s role as Senior Advisor shall be limited to providing non-binding advisory input on investment matters, to the extent his health permits, and shall be subject to the terms and conditions of a separate Senior Advisor Agreement between Mr. Whitmore and DCM.

> \(f\) *Amendment to Schedule A (Carried Interest Allocation).* Schedule A to the A&R LPA is amended to reflect the following revised allocations of the General Partner\'s 20% incentive allocation (i.e., the \"Carried Interest\"):
> • Marcus J. Whitmore: 9% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (reduced from 18%);
> • Elaine R. Sato: 7% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (increased from 1.5%);
> • Jonathan K. Huang: 4% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (increased from 0.5%);
> • Remaining GP-level allocation (other DCM members and reserves): unchanged;
> • GP-level total incentive allocation: 20% (unchanged).

> Mr. Whitmore\'s carried interest shall vest on a modified schedule as follows: fifty percent (50%) of Mr. Whitmore\'s carried interest allocation shall be deemed vested immediately as of the Key Person Event Date (June 10, 2024); the remaining fifty percent (50%) shall vest ratably on a monthly basis over thirty-six (36) months commencing on June 10, 2024, subject to continued compliance by Mr. Whitmore with the non-competition and non-solicitation covenants set forth in the Operating Agreement of DCM and the Senior Advisor Agreement.
**E. Consent Requirement.**

Pursuant to Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, any amendment to the A&R LPA requires the written consent of the General Partner and of Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment). Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA further provides that the approval of Successor Key Persons and any related amendments to the A&R LPA shall be subject to the same consent threshold set forth in Section 14.01.
As of the Certification Date, the aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments for purposes of the consent vote (the \"Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments\") are calculated as follows:
> Total Fund Net Asset Value (as of Q2 2024 quarterly valuation): \$2,870.0 million
> Less: Marcus J. Whitmore capital commitment (committed through the GP vehicle, DCM): (\$57.4 million)
> Less: Elaine R. Sato capital commitment (committed through the GP vehicle, DCM): (\$14.35 million)
> **Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments: \$2,798.25 million**

The capital commitments of Mr. Whitmore and Ms. Sato are excluded from the Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments because they were committed through the General Partner\'s co-investment vehicle and are therefore excluded pursuant to Section 14.01 of the A&R LPA, which provides that \"for purposes of any vote or consent of the Limited Partners, the capital commitments of the General Partner and any Affiliate of the General Partner that are invested through the General Partner\'s co-investment shall be excluded from the denominator.\"
The required consent threshold is therefore:
**F. Consent Deadline.**

The General Partner established August 23, 2024 as the deadline by which all Forms of Written Consent were required to be received by the General Partner (the \"LP Consent Deadline\"). The LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024 represents forty (40) calendar days from the July 15, 2024 circulation date of the Successor Proposal, the First Amendment, and the Form of Written Consent. The forty-day consent period was determined by the General Partner to be reasonable and consistent with the time periods customarily afforded to Limited Partners in similar circumstances, and was within the Cure Period expiring September 8, 2024. The General Partner also delivered reminder notices to all Limited Partners who had not yet returned executed Forms of Written Consent on August 5, 2024 and August 12, 2024, respectively.
**G. IAC Review.**

The Investor Advisory Committee (the \"IAC\") of the Partnership, established pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA, consists of five (5) members, each of whom is a representative of a Limited Partner of the Partnership. As of the date hereof, the members of the IAC are as follows:
> 1\. Diana Cortland, Representative of Northvale Public Employees\' Retirement System --- IAC Chair;
> 2\. Richard Oshima, Representative of Sycamore Endowment Partners LP;
> 3\. Catherine Mercer, Representative of Velthorn Institutional Fund of Funds III, L.P.;
> 4\. Thomas Ashworth, Representative of Bridlewood Family Office Holdings Ltd.; and
> 5\. Nadia Al-Rashid, Representative of Atlas Sovereign Wealth Advisory LLC.

The IAC reviewed the Successor Proposal, the First Amendment, and related materials at a meeting held on July 29, 2024, at the offices of Wexford Crane & Albright LLP, 51 West 52nd Street, 40th Floor, New York, NY 10019. The meeting was attended by all five IAC members (Ms. Cortland, Mr. Oshima, Ms. Mercer, Mr. Ashworth, and Ms. Al-Rashid) and by legal counsel to the IAC, Wexford Crane & Albright LLP (Helen M. Calloway, Partner, and David Pineda, Senior Associate). Also in attendance at the invitation of the IAC were Ms. Sato and Mr. Huang, who presented their qualifications, investment philosophy, and proposed governance structure, and responded to questions from the IAC members and their legal counsel. The IAC meeting lasted approximately three hours and forty-five minutes. Following the presentation and discussion, the IAC unanimously confirmed that it did not object to the Successor Proposal or the First Amendment, and that the IAC would recommend to the Limited Partners that they approve the same. The IAC\'s recommendation was communicated to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners by separate letter from Ms. Cortland, as IAC Chair, dated August 1, 2024.
**[CERTIFICATIONS]{.underline}**
NOW, THEREFORE, the General Partner, acting through its duly authorized representative, hereby certifies as follows:
**Section 1. Certification of Consent Tabulation.**

**1.1 Receipt of Written Consents.** The undersigned, on behalf of DCM as General Partner of the Partnership, hereby certifies that the General Partner has received duly executed Forms of Written Consent from thirty-eight (38) of the forty-seven (47) Limited Partners of the Partnership (collectively, the \"Consenting LPs\"). Each Form of Written Consent received by the General Partner was executed by an authorized signatory of the respective Limited Partner and delivered to the General Partner in accordance with the delivery instructions set forth in the Form of Written Consent and the notice provisions of Section 16.01 of the A&R LPA. The General Partner has verified the authority of each signatory based on the relevant subscription documents, incumbency certificates, and/or powers of attorney on file with the Partnership.

All thirty-eight (38) written consents were received by the General Partner on or before August 19, 2024, which date is four (4) calendar days prior to the LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024. No Forms of Written Consent were received by the General Partner after August 19, 2024 and on or before the LP Consent Deadline of August 23, 2024. No Forms of Written Consent were received by the General Partner after the LP Consent Deadline.

**1.2 Tabulation of Consenting LP Capital Commitments.** The aggregate capital commitments of the thirty-eight (38) Consenting LPs total Two Billion Four Hundred Twelve Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,412,800,000) (\$2,412.8 million). A detailed schedule of each Consenting LP and its respective capital commitment amount, together with the date on which the Form of Written Consent was received from such Consenting LP, is attached hereto as **Exhibit A** and is incorporated herein by reference.

**1.3 Percentage of Voting LP Capital Commitments.** The Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment, as described in Recital E above) are Two Billion Seven Hundred Ninety-Eight Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,798,250,000) (\$2,798.25 million). The consenting LP capital commitments of \$2,412.8 million represent approximately eighty-six and two-tenths percent (86.2%) of the Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments, calculated as follows:
> \$2,412,800,000 ÷ \$2,798,250,000 = 86.2% (rounded to the nearest tenth of a percent)

**1.4 Satisfaction of Consent Threshold.** The required consent threshold under Sections 14.01 and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA is sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of the Aggregate Voting LP Capital Commitments, which equals One Billion Eight Hundred Sixty-Five Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,865,500,000) (\$1,865.50 million). The consenting LP capital commitments of \$2,412.8 million exceed the required threshold of \$1,865.50 million by Five Hundred Forty-Seven Million Three Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$547,300,000) (\$547.3 million). Accordingly, the General Partner hereby certifies that the consent threshold required under Sections 14.01 and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA has been satisfied, and the requisite written consent of the Limited Partners has been duly and validly obtained for purposes of approving the Successor Key Persons and the First Amendment.
**Section 2. Certification of Amendment Effectiveness.**

**2.1 Effectiveness of the First Amendment.** Having determined, as set forth in Section 1 above, that the requisite Limited Partner consent has been obtained in accordance with Sections 14.01 and 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, and having further confirmed that all other conditions precedent to the effectiveness of the First Amendment have been satisfied (including, without limitation, the execution and delivery of the First Amendment by the General Partner on behalf of the Partnership), the General Partner hereby certifies that the First Amendment to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. is effective as of August 26, 2024 (the \"Amendment Effective Date\"). The A&R LPA, as modified by the First Amendment, shall hereinafter be referred to as the \"LPA\" or the \"Partnership Agreement,\" and all references in any agreement, instrument, document, or certificate to the \"A&R LPA\" or the \"Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement\" shall be deemed to refer to the A&R LPA as amended by the First Amendment, unless the context otherwise requires.

**2.2 Summary of Key Amendments Now in Effect.** As of the Amendment Effective Date, the following material amendments to the A&R LPA, as effected by the First Amendment, are now in full force and effect:

> \(a\) *Section 8.04(a) --- Redefinition of \"Key Person.\"* The term \"Key Person\" is redefined to mean Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, jointly, for so long as each of them serves in her or his respective capacity with the General Partner and devotes substantially all of her or his professional time to the investment activities and affairs of the Partnership.

> \(b\) *Sections 8.04(b) and 8.04(c) --- Replacement Period.* Loss of one (but not both) Successor Key Person triggers a 180-calendar-day Replacement Period, during which the remaining Successor Key Person and the General Partner shall identify and propose a replacement to the Limited Partners for approval, rather than an automatic suspension of the Investment Period. Loss of both Successor Key Persons triggers a Key Person Event with consequences as previously provided in Section 8.04 of the A&R LPA.

> \(c\) *New Section 8.05 --- Investment Committee.* A three-member Investment Committee is established, consisting of Elaine R. Sato (Chair), Jonathan K. Huang, and one independent member to be designated by the Investor Advisory Committee pursuant to Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA. All new portfolio investments in excess of \$5.0 million require approval of at least two (2) of the three (3) members of the Investment Committee.

> \(d\) *Follow-On Investment Cap.* The follow-on investment cap applicable during any future Key Person Event is reduced from \$28.7 million (1.0% of assets under management) to \$14.35 million (0.5% of assets under management).

> \(e\) *Designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor.* Marcus J. Whitmore is designated as Senior Advisor to the Partnership and to the General Partner, effective as of the Amendment Effective Date, with no governance authority, no voting rights, and no authority to bind the Partnership or the General Partner.
> \(f\) *Schedule A --- Carried Interest Allocation.* The revised allocations of the General Partner\'s 20% incentive allocation are as follows:
> • Marcus J. Whitmore: 9% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (reduced from 18%);
> • Elaine R. Sato: 7% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (increased from 1.5%);
> • Jonathan K. Huang: 4% of the GP\'s 20% incentive allocation (increased from 0.5%);
> • GP-level total incentive allocation: 20% (unchanged).

> \(g\) *Whitmore Carried Interest Vesting.* Fifty percent (50%) of Mr. Whitmore\'s carried interest allocation vested immediately as of the Key Person Event Date (June 10, 2024). The remaining fifty percent (50%) vests ratably on a monthly basis over thirty-six (36) months commencing on June 10, 2024, subject to continued compliance by Mr. Whitmore with the non-competition and non-solicitation covenants set forth in the Operating Agreement of DCM and the Senior Advisor Agreement.

**2.3 Cure Period.** The 90-calendar-day Cure Period under Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA commenced on the Key Person Event Date of June 10, 2024 and was set to expire on September 8, 2024. The effectiveness of the First Amendment on the Amendment Effective Date of August 26, 2024 --- which date is thirteen (13) calendar days prior to the expiration of the Cure Period --- constitutes a cure of the Key Person Event within the Cure Period, in accordance with Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA. Accordingly, the September 8, 2024 Cure Period expiration date is rendered moot.

Furthermore, the suspension of the Investment Period that took effect automatically upon the occurrence of the Key Person Event on June 10, 2024, pursuant to Section 8.04(c) of the A&R LPA, is hereby terminated as of the Amendment Effective Date of August 26, 2024. The Investment Period shall continue from the Amendment Effective Date in accordance with its original terms as set forth in Section 7.01 of the A&R LPA (as amended by the First Amendment), and the General Partner (acting through the newly established Investment Committee) shall be permitted to make new portfolio investments on behalf of the Partnership, subject to the terms and conditions of the A&R LPA as amended by the First Amendment.
**Section 3. Governing Law.**

This Certificate and the matters set forth herein shall be governed by, and construed in accordance with, the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to the conflict of laws principles thereof that would cause the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. Any dispute arising out of or relating to this Certificate shall be resolved in accordance with the dispute resolution provisions set forth in Section 15.04 of the A&R LPA (as amended by the First Amendment).
**Section 4. Reliance and Distribution.**
This Certificate is delivered by the General Partner for the benefit of, and may be relied upon by, the following persons and entities:
> \(a\) the Limited Partners of the Partnership;
> \(b\) the Investor Advisory Committee of the Partnership;
> \(c\) the Fund Administrator: Pinnacle Fund Services (Cayman) Ltd.;
> \(d\) the Auditor: Graystone & Whitfield LLP;
> \(e\) the Prime Broker: Halcyon Securities International Ltd.; and
> \(f\) the Partnership\'s legal counsel: Calderwood & Harkness LLP, 1585 Broadway, 34th Floor, New York, NY 10036.

**[FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT OF DRIFTWOOD ABSOLUTE RETURN FUND LTD.]{.underline}**
*Effective as of August 26, 2024*
By and Among
**DRIFTWOOD CAPITAL MANAGEMENT LLC** a Delaware limited liability company, as General Partner
and
**THE LIMITED PARTNERS** of
**DRIFTWOOD ABSOLUTE RETURN FUND LTD.** a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership (Registration No. ELP-87234)
**FIRST AMENDMENT TO THE AMENDED AND RESTATED LIMITED PARTNERSHIP AGREEMENT OF DRIFTWOOD ABSOLUTE RETURN FUND LTD.**

This First Amendment (this \"Amendment\") to the Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement, dated as of March 15, 2017 (as in effect immediately prior to the effectiveness of this Amendment, the \"Agreement\" or the \"A&R LPA\"), of Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd., a Cayman Islands exempted limited partnership registered under the Exempted Limited Partnership Law (as revised) of the Cayman Islands under Registration No. ELP-87234 (the \"Partnership\" or \"DARF\"), is entered into as of August 26, 2024 (the \"Amendment Effective Date\"), by and among Driftwood Capital Management LLC, a Delaware limited liability company (\"DCM\" or the \"General Partner\"), having its principal office at 680 Lexington Avenue, 31st Floor, New York, New York 10022, and the limited partners of the Partnership (each, a \"Limited Partner\" and collectively, the \"Limited Partners\").

The Partnership maintains its registered office at 4th Floor, Harbour Place, 103 South Church Street, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1104, Cayman Islands, and its registered agent is Archipelago Corporate Services Ltd., P.O. Box 2681, George Town, Grand Cayman, KY1-1111, Cayman Islands. The Delaware registered agent of DCM is Capitol Registered Agents, Inc., 1209 Orange Street, Wilmington, Delaware 19801. The employer identification number of DCM is 82-4917653.
**[RECITALS]{.underline}**

**WHEREAS**, the Partnership was formed as an exempted limited partnership under the laws of the Cayman Islands with an inception date of March 15, 2017, and the parties entered into the A&R LPA on such date, which A&R LPA is governed by the laws of the State of Delaware (Recital A);

**WHEREAS**, pursuant to Section 8.04(a) of the Agreement, Marcus J. Whitmore was designated as the sole \"Key Person\" of the Partnership, and the rights, obligations, and protections associated with the Key Person provisions were established in reliance upon Mr. Whitmore\'s continued active involvement in the management of the Partnership\'s investment portfolio (Recital B);

**WHEREAS**, on June 3, 2024, Marcus J. Whitmore suffered a severe hemorrhagic stroke resulting in his medical incapacitation, and, pursuant to Section 8.04(b) of the Agreement, a Key Person Event was deemed to have occurred effective June 10, 2024, as the Key Person was unable to devote substantially all of his professional time to the affairs of the Partnership for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days following the date of such medical event (Recital C);

**WHEREAS**, as a consequence of the Key Person Event, and in accordance with Section 8.04(c) of the Agreement, the Investment Period was immediately suspended, follow-on investments were capped at Twenty-Eight Million Seven Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$28,700,000) (representing 1.0% of assets under management as of the most recent net asset value determination), and a ninety (90) calendar day Cure Period commenced on June 10, 2024, such Cure Period being scheduled to expire on September 8, 2024 (Recital D);

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner notified all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners in writing of the Key Person Event on June 14, 2024, within the five (5) business day deadline prescribed by Section 8.04(c) of the Agreement (such deadline being June 17, 2024), and such notices were delivered by electronic mail and overnight courier in accordance with the notice provisions of the Agreement (Recital E);

**WHEREAS**, following the Key Person Event, the General Partner proposed the designation of Elaine R. Sato, Deputy Chief Investment Officer and Managing Member (holding a 10% membership interest) of DCM, and Jonathan K. Huang, Head of Credit Strategies of DCM, as Successor Key Persons pursuant to Section 8.04 of the Agreement, and the General Partner circulated this Amendment to all forty-seven (47) Limited Partners on July 15, 2024 for their review and consent (Recital F);

**WHEREAS**, the Investor Advisory Committee of the Partnership (the \"IAC\"), established pursuant to Section 9.02 of the Agreement, reviewed the proposed Amendment at its duly convened meeting on July 29, 2024, at which a quorum was present, and the IAC discussed the qualifications of the proposed Successor Key Persons, the terms of the proposed Investment Committee, the proposed modifications to the Key Person provisions, and the proposed reallocation of carried interest (Recital G);

**WHEREAS**, pursuant to Section 14.01 of the Agreement, amendments to the Agreement require the written consent of Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment) (Recital H);

**WHEREAS**, as of the date hereof, aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments for voting purposes equal Two Billion Seven Hundred Ninety-Eight Million Two Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$2,798,250,000), being Two Billion Eight Hundred Seventy Million Dollars (\$2,870,000,000) of total net asset value less Fifty-Seven Million Four Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$57,400,000) attributable to Marcus J. Whitmore and Fourteen Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,350,000) attributable to Elaine R. Sato, each committed through the General Partner vehicle and therefore excluded from the voting base, and the required consent threshold equals One Billion Eight Hundred Sixty-Five Million Five Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$1,865,500,000), representing 66⅔% of \$2,798,250,000 (Recital I);

**WHEREAS**, written consents to this Amendment were received from thirty-eight (38) of forty-seven (47) Limited Partners by August 19, 2024, prior to the consent deadline of August 23, 2024, representing aggregate capital commitments of Two Billion Four Hundred Twelve Million Eight Hundred Thousand Dollars (\$2,412,800,000), constituting approximately 86.2% of voting Limited Partner capital commitments, which exceeds the required 66⅔% threshold by a substantial margin (Recital J); and

**WHEREAS**, the General Partner desires to amend the Agreement to reflect the designation of Successor Key Persons, the establishment of an Investment Committee, the modification of the Key Person provisions, the reallocation of carried interest among the principals of DCM, and the designation of Marcus J. Whitmore as Senior Advisor to the Partnership, all as more fully set forth herein (Recital K).

**NOW, THEREFORE**, in consideration of the mutual covenants and agreements contained herein, and for other good and valuable consideration, the receipt and sufficiency of which are hereby acknowledged, the parties hereto agree as follows:
**[ARTICLE I --- DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATION]{.underline}**

**Section 1.1 --- Defined Terms.** Unless otherwise defined herein, capitalized terms used in this Amendment shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement. The following new or amended defined terms are hereby added to, or shall replace existing definitions in, Article I of the Agreement, as applicable:
> \(a\) **\"Amendment Effective Date\"** means August 26, 2024.
> \(b\) **\"Investment Committee\"** has the meaning set forth in Section 8.05 of the Agreement, as added by Section 3.1 of this Amendment.

> \(c\) **\"Key Person\"** means, as of the Amendment Effective Date, Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, jointly. This definition replaces the prior definition of \"Key Person\" in its entirety, pursuant to which Marcus J. Whitmore was designated as the sole Key Person.
> \(d\) **\"Key Person Event\"** has the meaning set forth in amended Section 8.04(b) of the Agreement, as amended by Section 2.2 of this Amendment.
> \(e\) **\"Replacement Period\"** means the one hundred eighty (180) calendar day period described in amended Section 8.04(c)(ii) of the Agreement, as amended by Section 2.3 of this Amendment.
> \(f\) **\"Senior Advisor\"** means Marcus J. Whitmore, in the capacity described in Section 8.06 of the Agreement, as added by Section 4.1 of this Amendment.
> \(g\) **\"Single Key Person Departure\"** has the meaning set forth in amended Section 8.04(b) of the Agreement, as amended by Section 2.2 of this Amendment.
> \(h\) **\"Successor Key Person\"** means each of Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, designated as such pursuant to Section 8.04(a) of the Agreement as amended by this Amendment.

**Section 1.2 --- Interpretation.** References in this Amendment to \"Sections\" are to Sections of the Agreement as amended by this Amendment, and references to \"Schedules\" are to Schedules of the Agreement as amended by this Amendment, in each case unless the context otherwise requires. The Agreement, as amended by this Amendment, shall be read and construed as one integrated document. In the event of any conflict between the provisions of this Amendment and the provisions of the Agreement as in effect immediately prior to the Amendment Effective Date, the provisions of this Amendment shall control.
**[ARTICLE II --- AMENDMENT OF SECTION 8.04 (KEY PERSON PROVISIONS)]{.underline}**
**Section 2.1 --- Amendment of Section 8.04(a) --- Definition of Key Person.** Section 8.04(a) of the Agreement is hereby amended and restated in its entirety to read as follows:

> \"**Section 8.04(a)** --- *Definition of Key Person.* \'Key Person\' shall mean Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang, jointly. Both Successor Key Persons must remain actively engaged in the management of the Partnership\'s investment portfolio, and each must devote substantially all of his or her respective professional time to the affairs of the Partnership, for the Key Person requirement to be satisfied. For the avoidance of doubt, Marcus J. Whitmore is no longer designated as a Key Person as of the Amendment Effective Date and his designation as Senior Advisor pursuant to Section 8.06 hereof shall not, under any circumstances, be construed as constituting him as a Key Person for any purpose under this Agreement.\"
**Section 2.2 --- Amendment of Section 8.04(b) --- Key Person Event Trigger.** Section 8.04(b) of the Agreement is hereby amended and restated in its entirety to read as follows:

> \"**Section 8.04(b)** --- *Key Person Event.* A \'Key Person Event\' shall be deemed to have occurred if **both** Elaine R. Sato and Jonathan K. Huang are, at the same time, unable to devote substantially all of their respective professional time to the affairs of the Partnership, by reason of death, permanent disability (as determined in good faith by the General Partner based on medical evidence reasonably available), voluntary or involuntary departure from DCM or the Partnership, termination for cause, or any other cause, for a period of seven (7) consecutive calendar days. If only **one** of the two Key Persons ceases active involvement in the management of the Partnership\'s investment portfolio for any reason whatsoever (a \'Single Key Person Departure\'), a Key Person Event shall not be deemed to have occurred; provided, however, that the provisions of Section 8.04(c)(ii) (Replacement Period) shall apply in the case of a Single Key Person Departure. The determination of whether a Key Person Event or a Single Key Person Departure has occurred shall be made by the General Partner in good faith, and the General Partner shall promptly notify the Investor Advisory Committee and all Limited Partners of any such determination.\"

**Section 2.3 --- Amendment of Section 8.04(c) --- Consequences of Key Person Event and Single Key Person Departure.** Section 8.04(c) of the Agreement is hereby amended and restated in its entirety to read as follows:
> \"**Section 8.04(c)** --- *Consequences of Key Person Event and Single Key Person Departure.*

> **(i) Full Key Person Event (Both Key Persons).** Upon the occurrence of a Key Person Event (i.e., both Key Persons ceasing active involvement simultaneously or within seven (7) consecutive calendar days of each other):
> \(A\) the Investment Period shall be immediately suspended, and no new investments shall be permitted during the period of such suspension;

> \(B\) follow-on investments in existing portfolio positions shall be capped at Fourteen Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,350,000), representing 0.5% of assets under management as of the most recent net asset value determination available at the time of the Key Person Event (for the avoidance of doubt, this cap replaces the prior cap of \$28,700,000 representing 1.0% of assets under management that was applicable under the Agreement as in effect prior to the Amendment Effective Date);

> \(C\) the General Partner shall notify all Limited Partners in writing within five (5) business days of the occurrence of the Key Person Event, setting forth in reasonable detail the circumstances giving rise to the Key Person Event and the General Partner\'s initial assessment of the impact on the Partnership\'s investment activities;

> \(D\) a Cure Period of ninety (90) calendar days shall commence on the date of the Key Person Event, during which the General Partner may propose one or more replacement Key Persons for approval by the Limited Partners;

> \(E\) approval of any proposed replacement Key Person shall require the written consent of Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment), such consent to be solicited in writing in accordance with the notice provisions of the Agreement; and

> \(F\) if no replacement Key Person is approved within the Cure Period, Limited Partners holding a majority-in-interest of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment) may elect, by written notice delivered to the General Partner within thirty (30) calendar days following the expiration of the Cure Period, to (x) extend the Cure Period by up to ninety (90) additional calendar days on the same terms set forth in this Section 8.04(c)(i), or (y) direct the General Partner to commence an orderly wind-down of the Partnership in accordance with Section 12.01 of this Agreement.
> **(ii) Single Key Person Departure (One Key Person).** Upon the occurrence of a Single Key Person Departure (i.e., only one of the two Key Persons ceasing active involvement):
> \(A\) the Investment Period shall **not** be automatically suspended;
> \(B\) a Replacement Period of one hundred eighty (180) calendar days shall commence on the date of the Single Key Person Departure;

> \(C\) during the Replacement Period, the remaining Key Person shall continue to manage the Partnership\'s investments in the ordinary course, subject to oversight by the Investment Committee established under Section 8.05 of this Agreement, and the remaining Key Person shall not have the authority to make any new investment or commitment in excess of Fifty Million Dollars (\$50,000,000) without the prior approval of the Investment Committee;

> \(D\) during the Replacement Period, the General Partner shall use commercially reasonable efforts to identify and propose a replacement for the departed Key Person, and any such proposed replacement shall be subject to approval by Limited Partners holding not less than sixty-six and two-thirds percent (66⅔%) of aggregate Limited Partner capital commitments (excluding the General Partner\'s co-investment);

> \(E\) follow-on investments during the Replacement Period shall be capped at Fourteen Million Three Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$14,350,000), representing 0.5% of assets under management as of the most recent net asset value determination;

> \(F\) the General Partner shall notify all Limited Partners in writing within five (5) business days of a Single Key Person Departure, setting forth in reasonable detail the circumstances giving rise to the Single Key Person Departure, the identity of the remaining Key Person, and the General Partner\'s plan for identifying a replacement Key Person; and

> \(G\) if no replacement Key Person is approved prior to the expiration of the Replacement Period, a Key Person Event shall be deemed to have occurred on the date of such expiration, and the provisions of Section 8.04(c)(i) shall thereupon apply as if such Key Person Event had occurred on such date.\"
**[ARTICLE III --- ADDITION OF SECTION 8.05 (INVESTMENT COMMITTEE)]{.underline}**

**Section 3.1 --- New Section 8.05.** A new Section 8.05 is hereby added to the Agreement immediately following Section 8.04 (as amended by Article II of this Amendment), which Section 8.05 shall read in its entirety as follows:
> \"**Section 8.05** --- *Investment Committee.*

Limited partners do not have the right to participate in the day-to-day management of the Fund, and the LPAC (if constituted) serves in an advisory capacity only, without binding authority over the General Partner.

As described in the PPM, a defaulting limited partner may be subject to forfeiture of up to **50%** of such limited partner\'s interest in the Fund, in addition to other remedies available to the General Partner. BFO\'s side-letter negotiation should seek a **100% offset of Pinnacle\'s placement fee (\$750,000)** against management fees payable by BFO, to ensure that BFO is not economically disadvantaged by the placement agent arrangement.

**Priya Narayan** --- Co-Founder, Managing Partner & Chief Investment Officer. Ms. Narayan serves as the firm\'s Chief Investment Officer and is responsible for all aspects of the investment process, including deal sourcing, underwriting, due diligence, and investment committee deliberations. The PPM describes Ms. Narayan\'s background in real estate private equity and her leadership of the firm\'s investment activities since MPCA\'s founding.

Both Ellsworth and Narayan are identified as \"Key Persons\" under the LPA, which triggers certain protective provisions upon the departure, death, disability, or material reduction in time commitment of either individual. As discussed more fully in the LPA Review Memo, the LPA\'s key person provisions provide for a suspension of the investment period upon the occurrence of a \"Key Person Event,\" followed by a cure period during which the General Partner may identify and present a replacement key person to the LPAC for approval.

**C&H Recommendation:** C&H recommends that BFO seek enhanced key person protections in the side letter. Specifically, we recommend negotiating for (i) an automatic **ninety (90)-day suspension of the investment period** upon the departure of either Ellsworth or Narayan, during which no new investments may be made, and (ii) **BFO\'s option to cease future capital calls** (and thereby effectively withdraw from future investments) if the Key Person Event is not cured within the suspension period. These enhanced protections are justified by the degree to which Fund IV\'s investment thesis and track record are dependent on the continued involvement of both founding principals.

**Asset Management Platforms and GP-Stake Transactions.** Fund IV will pursue acquisitions of, or investments in, asset management platforms and GP-stake or GP-led transactions. These investments involve acquiring equity interests in investment management firms, including real estate-focused private equity managers, and are designed to provide the Fund with exposure to recurring management fee revenues and carried interest streams. The PPM notes that this strategy has been a growing component of the Sponsor\'s investment program in Funds II and III and is expected to represent a meaningful allocation in Fund IV.

> • **Single-Asset Concentration Limits:** The PPM indicates that no single investment may exceed a specified percentage of the Fund\'s total commitments, as set forth in the LPA. This is designed to ensure portfolio diversification and limit exposure to any single asset or transaction.

> • **Recycling Provisions:** The PPM notes that the General Partner may reinvest or \"recycle\" capital returned from early realizations during the investment period, subject to limitations set forth in the LPA. Recycling provisions can effectively increase the Fund\'s total invested capital beyond its committed capital amount and may impact management fee calculations and fund-level returns.

**Valuation Uncertainty.** As noted above, Fund IV\'s portfolio investments will be valued at the General Partner\'s determination of fair market value, which is inherently subjective. The PPM notes that there can be no assurance that the valuations assigned to unrealized investments will ultimately be achieved upon realization, and that material downward revisions in valuation are possible.

**Limited Governance Rights.** The PPM acknowledges that limited partners have **limited governance rights** under the LPA and limited ability to influence Fund IV\'s investment decisions, operational matters, or strategic direction. The General Partner has broad authority to manage the Fund\'s affairs, and limited partner consent or approval is required only for a narrow set of fundamental actions (e.g., amendment of certain material LPA provisions, removal of the General Partner for cause). Limited partners do not have the right to participate in the day-to-day management of the Fund, and the LPAC (if constituted) serves in an advisory capacity only, without binding authority over the General Partner.

**Default Provisions.** The PPM references the LPA\'s default provisions, which impose **severe penalties** on limited partners who fail to fund capital calls when due. As described in the PPM, a defaulting limited partner may be subject to forfeiture of up to **50%** of such limited partner\'s interest in the Fund, in addition to other remedies available to the General Partner. These provisions are designed to incentivize timely funding of capital calls but represent a significant risk to any limited partner that experiences liquidity constraints during the Fund\'s term. A detailed analysis of the default provisions is set forth in the LPA Review Memo.

**Effectively Connected Income (ECI).** The PPM notes that non-U.S. investors in Fund IV may be subject to U.S. federal income tax on income that is treated as effectively connected with a U.S. trade or business. While this risk is most directly relevant to non-U.S. investors, BFO should be aware that the Fund\'s investment in real estate operating companies and asset management platforms may generate income that raises ECI issues for certain investor categories.

**Relevance to BFO.** Although BFO is not itself an ERISA plan and is not a \"benefit plan investor,\" C&H recommends that BFO\'s side letter include **excuse rights** for any investment that would cause BFO (or any underlying beneficial owner of BFO) to be treated as holding \"plan assets\" under ERISA. This is a protective measure designed to insulate BFO from the risk that the Fund\'s investor composition changes over time in a manner that could trigger plan asset characterization.

The PPM does not indicate that the placement fee will be offset against management fees payable by the General Partner or the Sponsor. In the absence of such an offset, BFO would bear its proportionate share of the aggregate placement fees paid by the Fund in addition to its full management fee obligation, resulting in an effective \"double charge\" for the capital raise.

The LPAC seat provides an important platform for engaging with the General Partner on valuation, conflicts, exit planning, and other material matters.

> • The **governance protections** --- including the LPAC seat, dual Key Person provision, full tag-along rights at both the vehicle and AcquisitionCo levels, full MFN protection, and the Side Letter prohibition on excuse/exclusion without Pellegrino\'s consent --- are robust and provide Pellegrino with meaningful influence, transparency, and protection throughout the life of the investment.

> • The areas where Pellegrino\'s initial positions were not fully achieved --- including the carried interest rate (10% vs. requested 0%), the Key Person trigger structure (dual vs. requested single), the absence of LPAC approval authority for extensions, and the absence of a separate cure period for defaults --- represent reasonable compromises that are consistent with market practice and do not materially disadvantage Pellegrino\'s position.
> 1\. Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement of Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P. (execution version)
> 2\. Side Letter Agreement between Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest GP LLC and Pellegrino Capital Group LLC (execution version)
> 3\. Subscription Agreement (execution version)

**Section 9.1 --- Establishment and Composition**

The Partnership shall establish a Limited Partner Advisory Committee (the \"**LPAC**\") consisting of three (3) members. The members of the LPAC shall be appointed by the General Partner from among the Limited Partners or their designated representatives; provided, however, that Pellegrino Capital Group LLC shall be entitled to appoint one (1) member of the LPAC for so long as Pellegrino Capital Group LLC holds a Partnership Interest in the Partnership. LPAC members shall serve in a non-fiduciary, advisory capacity, except where specific approval or consent rights are expressly conferred upon the LPAC by this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, LPAC members shall not owe any fiduciary duties to the Partnership or to any other Partner by virtue of their service on the LPAC.
**Section 9.2 --- LPAC Functions**
The LPAC shall have the following functions and responsibilities:
\(a\) Review and approve (or disapprove) conflict transactions between the Partnership and the General Partner or any of its Affiliates as contemplated by Section 7.3(c);
\(b\) Review and approve (or disapprove) all other matters requiring LPAC consent as set forth in Section 7.3;
\(c\) Consult with the General Partner regarding valuations of the Investment, including the methodology and inputs used for such valuations;
\(d\) Review and approve (or disapprove) any proposed Distributions in kind pursuant to Section 6.7;
\(e\) Consult with the General Partner regarding the management transition plan in connection with a Key Person Event pursuant to Section 10.1; and

\(f\) Perform such other advisory functions as the General Partner may request from time to time, including review of the Partnership\'s annual financial statements and consultation on material strategic matters relating to the Investment.
**Section 9.3 --- LPAC Meetings**

\(a\) The LPAC shall meet at least once per calendar year, or more frequently as the General Partner or any two (2) LPAC members may request. Meetings may be held in person at the offices of the General Partner, by video conference, or by telephonic conference, as determined by the General Partner in consultation with the LPAC members.

\(b\) The General Partner shall provide at least ten (10) Business Days\' prior written notice of each meeting to all LPAC members, together with a written agenda and copies of any relevant materials to be discussed at such meeting.

\(c\) A quorum for any meeting of the LPAC shall consist of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members). Actions of the LPAC shall be taken by the affirmative vote or written consent of a majority of the LPAC members (i.e., two (2) of three (3) members).
\(d\) Actions may be taken by the LPAC without a meeting by written consent signed by a majority of the LPAC members, which consent shall be effective as of the date of the last signature.

LPAC members acting in good faith in the performance of their duties as LPAC members shall have no personal liability to the Partnership, the General Partner, or any Limited Partner for any actions taken or omitted to be taken in their advisory capacity as LPAC members.
**Section 9.5 --- Removal and Replacement**
\(a\) The General Partner may remove any LPAC member for Cause upon written notice to such LPAC member and the Limited Partner that appointed or designated such member.

\(b\) Any Limited Partner that appointed or designated an LPAC member may, at any time, designate a replacement for such LPAC member by written notice to the General Partner, and such replacement shall become effective upon receipt of such notice by the General Partner.

15: > **Re: Briarwood Family Office LLC --- Withdrawal of Proposed Commitment to Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P.**
16: 
17: Dear Mr. Drummond and Mr. Lockhart:
18: 
19: This firm represents Briarwood Family Office LLC (\"BFO\"), a Delaware limited liability company, in connection with BFO\'s evaluation of, and negotiations relating to, a proposed limited partnership commitment to Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Fund IV\"), a Delaware limited partnership whose general partner is Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC (the \"General Partner\"), and whose investment adviser is Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"Meridian Peak\" or the \"Adviser\"). The purpose of this letter is to formally notify Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, as counsel to Meridian Peak and Fund IV, and to notify Meridian Peak directly, that BFO has decided not to proceed with its proposed Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) capital commitment to Fund IV and is hereby withdrawing from further negotiations in connection therewith. The balance of this letter sets forth the relevant background, the basis and scope of BFO\'s withdrawal, and the parties\' respective obligations going forward.
20: 
21: **[Background and Summary of Negotiations]{.underline}**
22: 
23: By way of background, BFO received the Fund IV Confidential Private Placement Memorandum, dated December 15, 2023 (the \"PPM\"), and the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Fund IV, dated December 20, 2023 (the \"LPA\"), on or about January 8, 2024. These materials were transmitted electronically via Meridian Peak\'s secure data room, together with related subscription documents, investor questionnaire forms, and ancillary fund documentation.
24: 
25: Following an initial internal review of the PPM, the LPA, and related materials by BFO\'s investment professionals and in-house legal team, BFO engaged Calderwood & Harkness LLP on January 24, 2024 to advise BFO in connection with the proposed commitment and, specifically, to negotiate a side letter to the LPA (the \"Side Letter\") on BFO\'s behalf with respect to certain economic, governance, reporting, and regulatory terms.
26: 
27: Between February 7, 2024 and March 18, 2024, the parties engaged in extensive negotiations regarding the proposed Side Letter. The negotiation history is summarized as follows:
28: 
29: > • On February 7, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness transmitted an initial side-letter term sheet to Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP on behalf of BFO, setting forth BFO\'s principal requests across twelve subject-matter categories.
30: >
31: > • On February 14, 2024, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, on behalf of the General Partner and Meridian Peak, returned a markup of the initial term sheet reflecting the General Partner\'s responses, counterproposals, and comments on each category.
32: >
33: > • On February 21, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness delivered a revised term sheet incorporating certain of the General Partner\'s counterproposals and providing further detail on BFO\'s remaining requests.
34: >
35: > • On February 28, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness circulated the first full draft of the Side Letter, reflecting the substantially agreed term-sheet provisions and presenting the remaining open points in long-form contractual language.
36: >
37: > • On March 4, 2024, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP returned a markup of the first draft Side Letter on behalf of the General Partner, which included revisions to a number of substantive provisions and counter-drafting on several material terms.
38: >
39: > • On March 7, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness circulated a second draft of the Side Letter, which responded to the General Partner\'s March 4 markup and proposed compromise language on certain of the disputed provisions.
40: >
41: > • On March 11, 2024, a four-party conference call was held among representatives of Calderwood & Harkness, BFO, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, and Meridian Peak to discuss the remaining open negotiation points. That call addressed, among other things, the scope of excuse and exclusion rights, the structure of the most favored nation election mechanism, and certain aspects of the proposed management fee reduction.
42: >
43: > • On March 14, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness circulated a third draft of the Side Letter, reflecting the discussion points from the March 11 call and proposing revised language on the open items.
44: >
45: > • On March 18, 2024, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP returned a markup of the third draft Side Letter on behalf of the General Partner.
46: 
47: At the time negotiations were paused on March 28, 2024, certain material terms remained in brackets in the most recent draft of the Side Letter, including, without limitation, the excuse and exclusion cap percentage, the precise scope of the co-investment allocation methodology, and other items that had not been resolved to both parties\' mutual satisfaction. No final, execution-ready version of the Side Letter was produced.
48: 
49: **[Notification of Withdrawal]{.underline}**
50: 
51: We write to inform you that BFO\'s investment committee convened on April 2, 2024 and, following deliberation and consideration of the matter, voted to decline the proposed Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) capital commitment to Fund IV. This decision was reached after a thorough review of BFO\'s current portfolio allocation, liquidity requirements, and broader investment strategy, and reflects BFO\'s internal investment considerations at this time. BFO wishes to emphasize that this decision is not a reflection on the merits of Fund IV, its investment strategy, the quality of its management team, or the capabilities of Meridian Peak as an investment adviser. Rather, BFO has concluded that a commitment to Fund IV does not align with BFO\'s current investment priorities and allocation targets.
52: 
53: Accordingly, BFO will not be subscribing for a limited partnership interest in Fund IV and will not be participating in Fund IV\'s anticipated initial closing, which we understand is expected to occur on or about April 30, 2024, or in any subsequent closing of Fund IV.
54: 
55: **[Lapse of Negotiated Provisions]{.underline}**
56: 
57: As a direct result of BFO\'s decision not to proceed with the proposed commitment, all draft Side Letter provisions negotiated between the parties are of no further force or effect and have lapsed in their entirety, effective as of the date of this letter. For clarity and completeness, the lapsed provisions include, without limitation, the following:
58: 
59: > \(a\) **Most Favored Nation Rights.** All provisions relating to most favored nation (\"MFN\") protections for BFO, including the MFN election mechanism, the Fifty Million Dollar (\$50,000,000) limited partner commitment threshold for MFN eligibility, the Two Hundred Million Dollar (\$200,000,000) anchor investor carve-out from MFN disclosure, and the twenty (20) business day election period following delivery of MFN disclosure materials.
60: >
61: > \(b\) **Excuse and Exclusion Rights.** All provisions granting BFO the right to be excused or excluded from participation in, or the obligation to fund capital contributions with respect to, certain categories of investments, including investments in cannabis-related assets, gaming and casino properties, investments in jurisdictions subject to U.S. sanctions administered by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (\"OFAC\"), and investments that would cause Fund IV assets to constitute \"plan assets\" within the meaning of Section 3(42) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or the regulations promulgated thereunder.
62: >
63: > \(c\) **Management Fee Reductions.** All provisions providing for reduced management fees payable by BFO, including a management fee of one and one-half percent (1.50%) per annum on committed capital during the investment period and a management fee of one and one-quarter percent (1.25%) per annum on invested capital (net of write-downs and write-offs) following the expiration or termination of the investment period.
64: >
