lines.text: **CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP** **Attorneys at Law** 425 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10017 Tel: (212) 554-7800
www.calderwoodharkness.com
April 4, 2024
*Via Email and First Class Mail*
Harrison K. Drummond, Esq. Partner, Investment Funds Group Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP 1 Federal Street, Suite 3600 Boston, MA 02110
Gavin R. Lockhart Partner, Head of Investor Relations Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC 200 Clarendon Street, 42nd Floor Boston, MA 02116
> **Re: Briarwood Family Office LLC --- Withdrawal of Proposed Commitment to Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P.**
Dear Mr. Drummond and Mr. Lockhart:

This firm represents Briarwood Family Office LLC (\"BFO\"), a Delaware limited liability company, in connection with BFO\'s evaluation of, and negotiations relating to, a proposed limited partnership commitment to Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. (\"Fund IV\"), a Delaware limited partnership whose general partner is Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC (the \"General Partner\"), and whose investment adviser is Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC (\"Meridian Peak\" or the \"Adviser\"). The purpose of this letter is to formally notify Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, as counsel to Meridian Peak and Fund IV, and to notify Meridian Peak directly, that BFO has decided not to proceed with its proposed Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) capital commitment to Fund IV and is hereby withdrawing from further negotiations in connection therewith. The balance of this letter sets forth the relevant background, the basis and scope of BFO\'s withdrawal, and the parties\' respective obligations going forward.
**[Background and Summary of Negotiations]{.underline}**

By way of background, BFO received the Fund IV Confidential Private Placement Memorandum, dated December 15, 2023 (the \"PPM\"), and the Amended and Restated Agreement of Limited Partnership of Fund IV, dated December 20, 2023 (the \"LPA\"), on or about January 8, 2024. These materials were transmitted electronically via Meridian Peak\'s secure data room, together with related subscription documents, investor questionnaire forms, and ancillary fund documentation.

Following an initial internal review of the PPM, the LPA, and related materials by BFO\'s investment professionals and in-house legal team, BFO engaged Calderwood & Harkness LLP on January 24, 2024 to advise BFO in connection with the proposed commitment and, specifically, to negotiate a side letter to the LPA (the \"Side Letter\") on BFO\'s behalf with respect to certain economic, governance, reporting, and regulatory terms.
Between February 7, 2024 and March 18, 2024, the parties engaged in extensive negotiations regarding the proposed Side Letter. The negotiation history is summarized as follows:

> • On February 7, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness transmitted an initial side-letter term sheet to Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP on behalf of BFO, setting forth BFO\'s principal requests across twelve subject-matter categories.

> • On February 14, 2024, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, on behalf of the General Partner and Meridian Peak, returned a markup of the initial term sheet reflecting the General Partner\'s responses, counterproposals, and comments on each category.

> • On February 21, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness delivered a revised term sheet incorporating certain of the General Partner\'s counterproposals and providing further detail on BFO\'s remaining requests.

> • On February 28, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness circulated the first full draft of the Side Letter, reflecting the substantially agreed term-sheet provisions and presenting the remaining open points in long-form contractual language.

> • On March 4, 2024, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP returned a markup of the first draft Side Letter on behalf of the General Partner, which included revisions to a number of substantive provisions and counter-drafting on several material terms.

> • On March 7, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness circulated a second draft of the Side Letter, which responded to the General Partner\'s March 4 markup and proposed compromise language on certain of the disputed provisions.

> • On March 11, 2024, a four-party conference call was held among representatives of Calderwood & Harkness, BFO, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, and Meridian Peak to discuss the remaining open negotiation points. That call addressed, among other things, the scope of excuse and exclusion rights, the structure of the most favored nation election mechanism, and certain aspects of the proposed management fee reduction.
> • On March 14, 2024, Calderwood & Harkness circulated a third draft of the Side Letter, reflecting the discussion points from the March 11 call and proposing revised language on the open items.
> • On March 18, 2024, Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP returned a markup of the third draft Side Letter on behalf of the General Partner.

At the time negotiations were paused on March 28, 2024, certain material terms remained in brackets in the most recent draft of the Side Letter, including, without limitation, the excuse and exclusion cap percentage, the precise scope of the co-investment allocation methodology, and other items that had not been resolved to both parties\' mutual satisfaction. No final, execution-ready version of the Side Letter was produced.
**[Notification of Withdrawal]{.underline}**

We write to inform you that BFO\'s investment committee convened on April 2, 2024 and, following deliberation and consideration of the matter, voted to decline the proposed Seventy-Five Million Dollar (\$75,000,000) capital commitment to Fund IV. This decision was reached after a thorough review of BFO\'s current portfolio allocation, liquidity requirements, and broader investment strategy, and reflects BFO\'s internal investment considerations at this time. BFO wishes to emphasize that this decision is not a reflection on the merits of Fund IV, its investment strategy, the quality of its management team, or the capabilities of Meridian Peak as an investment adviser. Rather, BFO has concluded that a commitment to Fund IV does not align with BFO\'s current investment priorities and allocation targets.

Accordingly, BFO will not be subscribing for a limited partnership interest in Fund IV and will not be participating in Fund IV\'s anticipated initial closing, which we understand is expected to occur on or about April 30, 2024, or in any subsequent closing of Fund IV.
**[Lapse of Negotiated Provisions]{.underline}**

As a direct result of BFO\'s decision not to proceed with the proposed commitment, all draft Side Letter provisions negotiated between the parties are of no further force or effect and have lapsed in their entirety, effective as of the date of this letter. For clarity and completeness, the lapsed provisions include, without limitation, the following:

> \(a\) **Most Favored Nation Rights.** All provisions relating to most favored nation (\"MFN\") protections for BFO, including the MFN election mechanism, the Fifty Million Dollar (\$50,000,000) limited partner commitment threshold for MFN eligibility, the Two Hundred Million Dollar (\$200,000,000) anchor investor carve-out from MFN disclosure, and the twenty (20) business day election period following delivery of MFN disclosure materials.

> \(b\) **Excuse and Exclusion Rights.** All provisions granting BFO the right to be excused or excluded from participation in, or the obligation to fund capital contributions with respect to, certain categories of investments, including investments in cannabis-related assets, gaming and casino properties, investments in jurisdictions subject to U.S. sanctions administered by the Office of Foreign Assets Control (\"OFAC\"), and investments that would cause Fund IV assets to constitute \"plan assets\" within the meaning of Section 3(42) of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act of 1974, as amended (\"ERISA\"), or the regulations promulgated thereunder.

> \(c\) **Management Fee Reductions.** All provisions providing for reduced management fees payable by BFO, including a management fee of one and one-half percent (1.50%) per annum on committed capital during the investment period and a management fee of one and one-quarter percent (1.25%) per annum on invested capital (net of write-downs and write-offs) following the expiration or termination of the investment period.

> \(d\) **Co-Investment Rights.** All provisions granting BFO pro rata co-investment participation rights with respect to equity investments by Fund IV exceeding One Hundred Million Dollars (\$100,000,000) in aggregate transaction value, including the terms providing that such co-investment interests would be offered at no management fee and no carried interest to the General Partner or the Adviser.

> \(e\) **Enhanced Reporting Obligations.** All provisions imposing enhanced quarterly and annual reporting obligations on the General Partner or the Adviser with respect to BFO, including the delivery of supplemental portfolio and valuation reports on a quarterly basis and annual audited financial statements in enhanced form, as well as periodic environmental, social, and governance (\"ESG\") reporting in a format reasonably satisfactory to BFO.

> \(f\) **Key Person Event Enhancements.** All provisions modifying the key person provisions set forth in the LPA with respect to BFO, including the provision requiring a ninety (90) day automatic suspension of the investment period upon the departure, death, disability, or material reduction in involvement of either Conrad J. Ellsworth or Priya Narayan from Fund IV investment activities, and the related cure and notice mechanisms negotiated in connection therewith.

> \(g\) **Transfer Rights.** All provisions granting BFO the right to transfer all or a portion of its limited partnership interest in Fund IV to Hargrove family entities (as defined in the draft Side Letter) without the prior consent of the General Partner, subject to compliance with applicable securities laws and the delivery of customary transfer documentation.

> \(h\) **Confidentiality Carve-Outs.** All provisions expanding or modifying the confidentiality obligations set forth in the LPA as applied to BFO, including carve-outs permitting disclosure to BFO\'s affiliates, advisors, auditors, and regulatory authorities in the ordinary course.

> \(i\) **Accelerated Schedule K-1 Delivery.** All provisions requiring the General Partner to deliver, or cause to be delivered, Schedule K-1 (IRS Form 1065) and related tax information to BFO within seventy-five (75) days following the end of each fiscal year of Fund IV, in advance of the delivery timeline set forth in the LPA.

> \(j\) **Placement Agent Fee Offset.** All provisions requiring a one hundred percent (100%) offset of any placement agent fees, commissions, or other compensation paid or payable by Fund IV, the General Partner, the Adviser, or any of their affiliates to Pinnacle Capital Markets LLC (the \"Placement Agent\") in connection with BFO\'s commitment, against management fees otherwise payable by BFO.

All of the foregoing provisions, whether reflected in the initial term sheet dated February 7, 2024, the revised term sheet dated February 21, 2024, any of the three successive drafts of the Side Letter dated February 28, March 7, and March 14, 2024, any of the General Partner\'s markups received on February 14, March 4, and March 18, 2024, or discussed orally during the March 11, 2024 conference call or in any other communication between the parties, have lapsed in their entirety and are of no further force or effect as of the date hereof.
**[No Executed Agreements; No Binding Obligations]{.underline}**
For the avoidance of doubt, we confirm the following:
> \(i\) No subscription agreement or subscription booklet was executed by or on behalf of BFO in connection with Fund IV at any time during the course of negotiations.

> \(ii\) No capital commitment --- whether binding, conditional, or otherwise --- has been made by BFO to Fund IV, the General Partner, or the Adviser, whether pursuant to the LPA, any Side Letter, or any other agreement or instrument.

> \(iii\) No investor questionnaire, investor certification, or similar document was submitted by or on behalf of BFO to Fund IV, the General Partner, the Adviser, or any placement agent or other intermediary in connection with the proposed commitment.

> \(iv\) No binding obligations of any kind exist between BFO, on the one hand, and Fund IV, Meridian Peak Capital Partners GP IV LLC, Meridian Peak Capital Advisors LLC, or any of their respective affiliates, on the other hand, in connection with the proposed commitment to Fund IV, and no party has any claim against BFO arising out of or related to the negotiations described herein.
**[Confidentiality]{.underline}**

BFO acknowledges and expects that the terms of the parties\' negotiations, including all draft Side Letter provisions, term sheets, markups, and related communications (whether written or oral), will be treated as confidential by Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP, Meridian Peak, the General Partner, and Fund IV in accordance with customary practice applicable to fund subscription negotiations. BFO similarly will maintain the confidentiality of all Fund IV materials received by BFO and its advisors in connection with this process, including the PPM, the LPA, subscription documents, data room materials, and all related fund documentation, and will not disclose the terms thereof to any third party except as may be required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, or to BFO\'s professional advisors on a need-to-know basis subject to customary confidentiality undertakings.
**[Return and Retention of Materials]{.underline}**

We note that BFO and Calderwood & Harkness LLP will retain copies of Fund IV documents received during the course of this process --- including the PPM, the LPA, subscription documents, and related materials --- in their respective files, as required by applicable law, professional responsibility obligations, and firm and institutional document-retention policies. Neither BFO nor Calderwood & Harkness LLP will use or disclose such materials for any purpose other than as may be required by applicable law, regulation, or legal process, or in connection with BFO\'s internal recordkeeping. Should Meridian Peak or its counsel wish to discuss further arrangements regarding the retention or return of specific materials, we are happy to accommodate any reasonable request.
**[Professional Courtesy]{.underline}**

In closing, on behalf of BFO and this firm, we wish to express our sincere appreciation for the professionalism, responsiveness, and constructive engagement demonstrated by Ashford Crane & Hewitt LLP and the Meridian Peak team throughout the negotiation process. The negotiations were conducted in good faith and in a manner reflecting well on all parties involved. We reiterate that BFO\'s decision to decline the proposed commitment should not be taken as a negative assessment of Fund IV, its investment thesis, or the capabilities of Meridian Peak and its principals. BFO values the relationship it has developed with Meridian Peak during this process and does not foreclose the possibility of future engagement on matters of mutual interest.
Please do not hesitate to contact me if you have any questions regarding the foregoing or if there is anything further we can address in connection with this matter.
Very truly yours,
CALDERWOOD & HARKNESS LLP
Pamela Cross Partner, Funds & Asset Management Calderwood & Harkness LLP 425 Lexington Avenue New York, NY 10017 Tel: (212) 554-7846
Email: pcross@calderwoodharkness.com

{"file_path":"response.md","content":"# Funds & Asset Management matters involving a fund with an LP advisory committee

## Answer

**2 matters qualify.** I counted a matter only where:

1. the matter was staffed/identified as part of the firm’s **Funds & Asset Management** practice;
2. the relevant fund’s governing documents established an LP-facing advisory body — either an **LPAC** or an equivalent **Investor Advisory Committee (IAC)** composed of limited-partner representatives; and
3. the record shows that the fund’s LPA was executed/effective. I did **not** treat a proposed, first-draft, or “to be dated at first close” LPA as signed.

| Matter | Fund | LP advisory body | Signed-LPA basis |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1024-00002** | **Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd. (DARF)** | Five-member **Investor Advisory Committee (IAC)** under Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA | The fund operated under the **Amended & Restated LPA dated March 15, 2017**; the First Amendment was an execution version effective **August 26, 2024**, after the required LP consents were obtained. |
| **1027-00002** | **Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P.** | Three-member **Limited Partner Advisory Committee (LPAC)** under Article IX of the LPA; Pellegrino had a contractual right to appoint one member | The LPA is expressly titled an **“Execution Version,”** entered into effective **January 30, 2026**, and contains signature pages dated January 30, 2026 for the GP and Pellegrino. |

## Matter-by-matter support

### 1. Matter 1024-00002 — Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd.

**Why it qualifies:**

- The engagement letter identifies the client as Driftwood Capital Management LLC in its capacity as general partner of DARF and states that DARF was governed by an **Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement dated March 15, 2017**.
- The engagement letter identifies the relevant governance body as the **Investor Advisory Committee of the Fund** and expressly states that the firm did not represent the IAC.
- The key-person analysis states that DARF had **47 limited partners** and a **five-member IAC established under Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA**, serving in an advisory capacity regarding conflicts, valuation disputes, and key governance events.
- The closing certificate records the IAC’s five LP representatives, confirms that the LP consent threshold was satisfied, and certifies that the First Amendment to the A&R LPA became effective on **August 26, 2024**. That is execution/effectiveness evidence, not merely a draft proposal.

**Documents relied on:**

- `documents/matters/1024-00002/Engagement/engagement-letter-darf-gp-advisory.docx`
  - Identifies DARF, the March 15, 2017 A&R LPA, the IAC, and the Funds & Asset Management engagement team.
- `documents/matters/1024-00002/Analyses & Memos/key-person-event-analysis-memo.docx`
  - Describes the five-member IAC under Section 9.02 and its LP-governance role.
- `documents/matters/1024-00002/Closing/closing-certificate-consent-tabulation.docx`
  - Records the IAC review, the executed LP consents, satisfaction of the 66⅔% threshold, and the First Amendment’s August 26, 2024 effectiveness.
- `documents/matters/1024-00002/Transaction Documents/execution-first-amendment-ar-lpa.docx`
  - Execution-version First Amendment to the A&R LPA, effective August 26, 2024.

I treated “Investor Advisory Committee” as an LP advisory committee because the document describes it as a five-member body of fund LP representatives established under the LPA to review LP-protection and governance matters.

### 2. Matter 1027-00002 — Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P.

**Why it qualifies:**

- The engagement letter places the matter in the **Funds & Asset Management Practice Group** and concerns Pellegrino’s co-investment in Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P.
- The LPA’s Article IX establishes a three-member **LPAC**. It provides that Pellegrino may appoint one LPAC member while it holds an interest, and it gives the LPAC consultation and approval functions for specified conflicts, distributions, and other governance matters.
- The document is expressly an **execution version**, effective January 30, 2026. Its signature pages show the GP and Pellegrino signature blocks with January 30, 2026 dates.

**Documents relied on:**

- `documents/matters/1027-00002/Engagement/engagement-letter-pellegrino.docx`
  - Identifies Matter No. 1027-00002, the co-investment, the Funds & Asset Management team, and the scope covering the Co-Invest LPA and side letter.
- `documents/matters/1027-00002/Transaction Documents/co-invest-lpa-execution-version.docx`
  - “Execution Version” LPA; effective January 30, 2026; Article IX, Sections 9.1–9.5 establish and govern the LPAC; signature pages show the GP and Pellegrino dates.
- `documents/matters/1027-00002/Analysis & Advice/key-terms-summary-issues-memo.docx`
  - Confirms the LPAC structure, Pellegrino’s one-seat right, and the LPAC’s consultative role.

## Screening and exclusions

I also screened the other matter records that were identified as Funds & Asset Management matters and that referenced an LPAC/advisory committee. They were not included because the requested signed-LPA condition was not met, or because the relevant vehicle had no LPAC:

| Matter | Fund / vehicle | Why not counted |
|---|---|---|
| **1002-00003** | Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP | The engagement letter says the A&R LPA would be dated as of the First Close; the matter contains initial side-letter drafts and no executed LPA. The LPAC/advisory-committee provisions were prospective. |
| **1003-00002** | Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP and related vehicles | The first-close checklist lists the main LPA as **“Draft — initial draft circulated; redline under review,”** and lists the executed LPA as still **“In progress.”** The LPAC provisions were in the draft/fund-formation package, not an executed LPA. |
| **1004-00002** | Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP | The engagement letter and structuring memo describe an LPA to be drafted, with an LPAC to be established in that future LPA; the matter contains a first draft and a future first-close timetable, not a signed LPA. |
| **1023-00001** | ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP | Although the LP Agreement is an execution-version document, the governance memorandum expressly states that **no formal LPAC was established** because Ironside was the sole LP and had direct consent rights. |
| **1026-00001** | Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. | The LPA review describes an LPAC, but the matter-closing record says the first close had not occurred, BFO withdrew, and no subscription or commitment was executed. The matter file provides a dated LPA for review but no signed/execution-version LPA evidence; I therefore applied the requested signed-LPA filter conservatively and excluded it. |

## Bottom line

**Qualifying Funds & Asset Management matters: 2 — Matter Nos. 1024-00002 and 1027-00002.**
"}

  - Execution-version First Amendment to the A&R LPA, effective August 26, 2024.

**Documents relied on:**

- `documents/matters/1027-00002/Engagement/engagement-letter-pellegrino.docx`
  - Identifies Matter No. 1027-00002, the co-investment, the Funds & Asset Management team, and the scope covering the Co-Invest LPA and side letter.
- `documents/matters/1027-00002/Transaction Documents/co-invest-lpa-execution-version.docx`
  - “Execution Version” LPA; effective January 30, 2026; Article IX, Sections 9.1–9.5 establish and govern the LPAC; signature pages show the GP and Pellegrino dates.
- `documents/matters/1027-00002/Analysis & Advice/key-terms-summary-issues-memo.docx`
  - Confirms the LPAC structure, Pellegrino’s one-seat right, and the LPAC’s consultative role.

I also screened the other matter records that were identified as Funds & Asset Management matters and that referenced an LPAC/advisory committee. They were not included because the requested signed-LPA condition was not met, or because the relevant vehicle had no LPAC:

|---|---|---|
| **1002-00003** | Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP | The engagement letter says the A&R LPA would be dated as of the First Close; the matter contains initial side-letter drafts and no executed LPA. The LPAC/advisory-committee provisions were prospective. |
| **1003-00002** | Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP and related vehicles | The first-close checklist lists the main LPA as **“Draft — initial draft circulated; redline under review,”** and lists the executed LPA as still **“In progress.”** The LPAC provisions were in the draft/fund-formation package, not an executed LPA. |
| **1004-00002** | Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP | The engagement letter and structuring memo describe an LPA to be drafted, with an LPAC to be established in that future LPA; the matter contains a first draft and a future first-close timetable, not a signed LPA. |
| **1023-00001** | ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP | Although the LP Agreement is an execution-version document, the governance memorandum expressly states that **no formal LPAC was established** because Ironside was the sole LP and had direct consent rights. |
| **1026-00001** | Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. | The LPA review describes an LPAC, but the matter-closing record says the first close had not occurred, BFO withdrew, and no subscription or commitment was executed. The matter file provides a dated LPA for review but no signed/execution-version LPA evidence; I therefore applied the requested signed-LPA filter conservatively and excluded it. |

## Bottom line

**Qualifying Funds & Asset Management matters: 2 — Matter Nos. 1024-00002 and 1027-00002.**

The amendment: (i) amends certain defined terms to reflect the new holding company structure and the departure of Kellner and Trask; (ii) updates the GP commitment provisions to address the assumption of the departing principals\' unfunded commitment obligations (\$3,402,000 in aggregate); and (iii) makes conforming changes to Sections 5.2 (Key Person provisions), 8.3 (GP Removal and Replacement), and 9.4 (Amendments and Consents). The amendment was executed as of February 28, 2024, following receipt of LPAC consent on February 14, 2024, as required under LPA Section 9.4.

**3.2.4 GP Commitment Reallocation.** The restructuring required the reallocation of the GP\'s \$42,000,000 aggregate commitment to the Fund, specifically with respect to the assumption of the departing principals\' unfunded commitment obligations:
**Departing Principal**   **Total GP Commitment Share**   **Funded Amount**   **Unfunded Amount**

The combined unfunded departing commitment of \$3,402,000 was assumed by the remaining HoldCo members on a pro rata basis in accordance with their respective HoldCo membership interest percentages, as follows:
**Assuming Member**     **HoldCo %**            **Assumed Unfunded Amount**
The GP commitment reallocation was documented in the Second Amended and Restated LLC Agreement of the GP, the Amendment No. 1 to the Fund\'s LPA, and the HoldCo LLC Agreement.
**GP Commitment:** Kellner\'s unfunded GP commitment of \$1,890,000 was assumed by the remaining HoldCo members pro rata, as described in Section 3.2.4 above.
**GP Commitment:** Trask\'s unfunded GP commitment of \$1,512,000 was assumed by the remaining HoldCo members pro rata, as described in Section 3.2.4 above.

**3.4.1 LPAC Consent.** The Fund\'s LPA requires that certain amendments and structural changes receive the prior consent of the Limited Partner Advisory Committee (\"LPAC\") pursuant to LPA Section 9.4. The LPAC for Fund III consists of four members, each representing a significant limited partner:

Calderwood & Harkness prepared and sent an LPAC notification and consent solicitation letter to each LPAC member on February 5, 2024. The letter was accompanied by a comprehensive **LPAC Presentation Memorandum** that summarized: (i) the rationale for the restructuring, including the planned departures of Kellner and Trask; (ii) the new entity structure, including organizational charts depicting the pre- and post-restructuring structures; (iii) the economics realignment, including updated carry and management fee profit share allocations; (iv) the key terms of the departing principal separation agreements; and (v) a confirmation that the restructuring does not constitute a Key Person Event under LPA Section 5.2, as neither Kellner nor Trask is a designated Key Person (only Aldridge and Narayanan hold that designation).

A virtual LPAC meeting was convened on February 14, 2024, during which the LPAC members had the opportunity to ask questions and discuss the restructuring with the remaining principals and Calderwood & Harkness. Following the meeting, LPAC consent was obtained in the form of a written consent executed by all four LPAC members, constituting the approval required under LPA Section 9.4 for the execution of Amendment No. 1 to the LPA.
> • The receipt of LPAC consent on February 14, 2024;
> • The execution of Amendment No. 1 to the LPA; and

> • **Expanded Key-Person Provisions (6 side letters):** Six side letters contained expanded key-person provisions that named David Kellner as a \"Contributing Person\" (a broader designation than the LPA\'s \"Key Person\" definition, which includes only Aldridge and Narayanan). Under these expanded provisions, Kellner\'s retirement triggers a notification obligation requiring ManCo to provide written notice to the affected LPs within fifteen (15) business days. Additionally, three of those six side letters (Ridgeline Public Employees\' Retirement System, Pinnacle Insurance Group, and one additional LP) grant the affected LP the right to request a suspension of the investment period for up to ninety (90) days pending LPAC review. All required notifications were issued in connection with the LP notification process, and no LP elected to exercise the investment period suspension right.

The memorandum concluded that no Key Person Event was triggered under LPA Section 5.2 as a result of the restructuring, because neither Kellner nor Trask is a designated Key Person under the LPA. Only Marcus Aldridge and Priya Narayanan are designated Key Persons, and both are continuing with the platform in their existing roles as Co-Founders and Managing Partners. All required notifications and consents under the side letters were obtained prior to or concurrently with the LP notification process.

> • **Updated Schedule D:** The private fund reporting section (Schedule D) for Ardent Capital Partners III LP was updated to reflect the restructured general partner and management company arrangements.

A **Summary of Changes Memorandum** was prepared by Stephen Adler documenting each material change reflected in the Form ADV amendment, the rationale for the change, and the specific sections of the Form ADV affected. This memorandum is preserved in the matter file for reference.

> • **Calderwood & Harkness** was responsible for all restructuring-specific matters, including: the design and implementation of the holding company structure; all restructuring documentation (entity formation, governing document amendments, carry and economics agreements); all departing principal separation negotiations and documentation; LPAC consent solicitation and LP notifications relating to the restructuring; side-letter compliance analysis; and regulatory filings triggered by the restructuring.

> • **Pemberton Hale LLP** continued in its role as fund counsel for routine fund operations, including: portfolio company transactions; ongoing LP communications unrelated to the restructuring; compliance monitoring; and other day-to-day fund operation matters.

Pemberton Hale provided Calderwood & Harkness with copies of all 14 side letters, the current form of the Fund\'s LPA (including all prior amendments), the existing LLC Agreements of the GP and ManCo, and other governing documents necessary for the restructuring. The two firms coordinated regularly throughout the engagement to ensure consistency and avoid duplication, with particular attention to LP-facing communications.

Heathrow Whitman acknowledged the coordination and confirmed that its team would prepare updated Schedule K-1s for the 2024 tax year reflecting the restructuring, with coordination complete as of the matter closing date.

The following Fund performance data, as of September 30, 2023 (the most recent quarterly valuation date at the time of the restructuring), was referenced in the LPAC Presentation Memorandum and was relevant to the calculation of accrued carried interest and the economics of the departing principal separations:

These figures were provided by Broadleaf Consulting Group (valuation advisor) and confirmed by Heathrow Whitman & Co. (auditor) in the ordinary course of the Fund\'s quarterly reporting process. Calderwood & Harkness did not independently verify these figures but relied upon them for purposes of the engagement and the preparation of the restructuring documents and LPAC materials.
The following timeline sets forth the key dates and events in the course of the engagement, from the inception of Fund III through the closing of this matter:
February 5, 2024                    LPAC notification and consent solicitation letters sent to all four LPAC members
February 14, 2024                   Virtual LPAC meeting held; LPAC consent obtained pursuant to LPA Section 9.4
March 15, 2024                      Engagement closed --- all workstreams complete; matter closed

> 18\. LPAC Presentation Memorandum (enclosed with Item 17)
> 19\. Form of Written Consent --- LPAC (executed by all four LPAC members, February 14, 2024)

Total fees billed fell within the estimated fee range provided in the engagement letter (\$850,000 -- \$1,100,000). Disbursements consisted primarily of Delaware Secretary of State filing fees, research database charges, document production and delivery costs, and travel expenses in connection with the LPAC meeting.
> • All invoices were paid in full as of the matter closing date.

The following matters remain open or will occur following the closing of this engagement. In each case, no further action by Calderwood & Harkness is required, and the relevant obligations are self-executing or have been delegated to the appropriate party:

> 3\. **Management Fee Transition (June 30, 2025).** The Fund\'s management fee will transition from 1.75% on committed capital to 1.50% on invested capital when the investment period ends on June 30, 2025. This transition will be handled by Pemberton Hale LLP as part of routine fund operations and does not require Calderwood & Harkness involvement.

> 4\. **Lockwood Placement Partners LLC Tail-Fee Obligations.** Certain tail-fee obligations owed by ManCo to Lockwood Placement Partners LLC remain in effect in accordance with the terms of the placement agent agreement entered into in connection with Fund III fundraising. The restructuring did not affect these obligations, and no action is required from Calderwood & Harkness.

> 5\. **Fund Term Expiration (December 31, 2029).** The Fund\'s term expires on December 31, 2029, subject to two one-year extension options exercisable at the discretion of the GP. Future fund operations, including any extension elections, wind-down activities, and final distributions, remain with Pemberton Hale LLP as fund counsel.
A conflict check has been cleared, and no outstanding conflicts of interest exist with respect to this matter or any of the parties identified herein.

Matter No. 1001-00002 has been closed in the Firm\'s billing and matter management systems effective March 15, 2024. All time entries have been finalized, all invoices have been issued, and all invoices have been paid in full. No further billing activity is anticipated in connection with this matter.

### 1. Matter 1001-00002 — Ardent Capital Partners III LP
**Why it qualifies:**

- The conflict-check memorandum identifies the engagement team as the firm’s **Private Funds** group, which is the fund-practice label used in this matter’s records, and describes the engagement as advising Ardent Capital Management LLC on restructuring its private equity fund platform.
- The matter concerns Ardent Capital Partners III LP, a Delaware private equity fund with **47 limited partners** and a completed final close on April 15, 2019.
- The fund’s LPA requires LPAC consent under Section 9.4. The record identifies a **four-member LPAC**, with each member representing a significant limited partner.

- The matter-closing memorandum says that the virtual LPAC meeting occurred on February 14, 2024, all four LPAC members executed written consent, and **Amendment No. 1 to the LPA was executed as of February 28, 2024**. This satisfies both the LP-advisory-committee and signed-LPA conditions.
**Documents relied on:**
- `documents/matters/1001-00002/Engagement & Administration/conflict-check-memo.docx`
- Identifies the Private Funds engagement team, the Fund III restructuring scope, and the four LPAC members.
- `documents/matters/1001-00002/Engagement & Administration/matter-closing-memo.docx`
- Records the completed final close, four-member LPAC, executed LPAC consent, and execution of Amendment No. 1 to the LPA on February 28, 2024.
- `documents/matters/1001-00002/LP Consent & Notification/lpac-form-of-written-consent.docx`
- LPAC written-consent document used for the restructuring approval.
- `documents/matters/1001-00002/Amended Governing Documents/lpa-amendment-no-1.docx`
- Amendment to the fund’s LPA implementing the restructuring.
### 2. Matter 1024-00002 — Driftwood Absolute Return Fund Ltd.
**Why it qualifies:**

- The engagement letter identifies the client as Driftwood Capital Management LLC in its capacity as general partner of DARF and states that DARF was governed by an **Amended and Restated Limited Partnership Agreement dated March 15, 2017**.
- The engagement letter identifies the relevant governance body as the **Investor Advisory Committee of the Fund** and expressly states that the firm did not represent the IAC.

- The key-person analysis states that DARF had **47 limited partners** and a **five-member IAC established under Section 9.02 of the A&R LPA**, serving in an advisory capacity regarding conflicts, valuation disputes, and key governance events.

- The closing certificate records the IAC’s five LP representatives, confirms that the LP consent threshold was satisfied, and certifies that the First Amendment to the A&R LPA became effective on **August 26, 2024**. That is execution/effectiveness evidence, not merely a draft proposal.
**Documents relied on:**
- `documents/matters/1024-00002/Engagement/engagement-letter-darf-gp-advisory.docx`
- Identifies DARF, the March 15, 2017 A&R LPA, the IAC, and the Funds & Asset Management engagement team.
- `documents/matters/1024-00002/Analyses & Memos/key-person-event-analysis-memo.docx`
- Describes the five-member IAC under Section 9.02 and its LP-governance role.
- `documents/matters/1024-00002/Closing/closing-certificate-consent-tabulation.docx`
- Records the IAC review, the executed LP consents, satisfaction of the 66⅔% threshold, and the First Amendment’s August 26, 2024 effectiveness.
- `documents/matters/1024-00002/Transaction Documents/execution-first-amendment-ar-lpa.docx`
- Execution-version First Amendment to the A&R LPA, effective August 26, 2024.

I treated “Investor Advisory Committee” as an LP advisory committee because the document describes it as a five-member body of fund LP representatives established under the LPA to review LP-protection and governance matters.
### 3. Matter 1027-00002 — Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P.
**Why it qualifies:**
- The engagement letter places the matter in the **Funds & Asset Management Practice Group** and concerns Pellegrino’s co-investment in Ridgeline-Clarion Co-Invest, L.P.

- The LPA’s Article IX establishes a three-member **LPAC**. It provides that Pellegrino may appoint one LPAC member while it holds an interest, and it gives the LPAC consultation and approval functions for specified conflicts, distributions, and other governance matters.
- The document is expressly an **execution version**, effective January 30, 2026. Its signature pages show the GP and Pellegrino signature blocks with January 30, 2026 dates.
**Documents relied on:**
- `documents/matters/1027-00002/Engagement/engagement-letter-pellegrino.docx`
- Identifies Matter No. 1027-00002, the co-investment, the Funds & Asset Management team, and the scope covering the Co-Invest LPA and side letter.
- `documents/matters/1027-00002/Transaction Documents/co-invest-lpa-execution-version.docx`
- “Execution Version” LPA; effective January 30, 2026; Article IX, Sections 9.1–9.5 establish and govern the LPAC; signature pages show the GP and Pellegrino dates.
- `documents/matters/1027-00002/Analysis & Advice/key-terms-summary-issues-memo.docx`
- Confirms the LPAC structure, Pellegrino’s one-seat right, and the LPAC’s consultative role.
## Screening and exclusions

I also screened the other matter records identified in the Funds & Asset Management / Private Funds records that referenced an LPAC/advisory committee. They were not included because the requested signed-LPA condition was not met, or because the relevant vehicle had no LPAC:
| Matter | Fund / vehicle | Why not counted |

| **1002-00003** | Pinnacle Venture Fund II LP | The engagement letter says the A&R LPA would be dated as of the First Close; the matter contains initial side-letter drafts and no executed LPA. The LPAC/advisory-committee provisions were prospective. |

| **1003-00002** | Harrowgate Private Equity Fund V LP and related vehicles | The first-close checklist lists the main LPA as **“Draft — initial draft circulated; redline under review,”** and lists the executed LPA as still **“In progress.”** The LPAC provisions were in the draft/fund-formation package, not an executed LPA. |

| **1004-00002** | Cobalt Life Sciences Opportunities Fund I, LP | The engagement letter and structuring memo describe an LPA to be drafted, with an LPAC to be established in that future LPA; the matter contains a first draft and a future first-close timetable, not a signed LPA. |

| **1023-00001** | ICM Cascadia Co-Invest, LP | Although the LP Agreement is an execution-version document, the governance memorandum expressly states that **no formal LPAC was established** because Ironside was the sole LP and had direct consent rights. |

| **1026-00001** | Meridian Peak Capital Partners Fund IV, L.P. | The LPA review describes an LPAC, but the matter-closing record says the first close had not occurred, BFO withdrew, and no subscription or commitment was executed. The matter file provides a dated LPA for review but no signed/execution-version LPA evidence; I therefore applied the requested signed-LPA filter conservatively and excluded it. |
## Bottom line
**Qualifying Funds & Asset Management matters: 3 — Matter Nos. 1001-00002, 1024-00002, and 1027-00002.**
